## 11. Capability, analysis, provider, raw-result, validation, and normalization contracts

### 11.1 Analysis Capability Profile carrier

`AnalysisCapabilityProfileRecord` contains profile identity `JAN-CSAA-CAP-001` through `JAN-CSAA-CAP-032`, exact version, lifecycle, source binding, and one ordered value for every label:

| Label | Candidate field |
| --- | --- |
| `F01` | `profileIdentity` |
| `F02` | `profileLifecycle` |
| `F03` | `sourceBinding` |
| `F04` | `purpose` |
| `F05` | `analysisLane` |
| `F06` | `subjectPerimeter` |
| `F07` | `supportedSurface` |
| `F08` | `requiredInputs` |
| `F09` | `producedObjectMeanings` |
| `F10` | `producedRelationMeanings` |
| `F11` | `capabilityDependencies` |
| `F12` | `soundnessObjective` |
| `F13` | `completenessObjective` |
| `F14` | `coverageBasis` |
| `F15` | `knownFalsePositiveClasses` |
| `F16` | `knownFalseNegativeClasses` |
| `F17` | `unsupportedBehavior` |
| `F18` | `epistemicTreatment` |
| `F19` | `confidenceMeaning` |
| `F20` | `invalidationDependencies` |
| `F21` | `provenanceRequirements` |
| `F22` | `failureAndPartiality` |
| `F23` | `explanationOrWitness` |
| `F24` | `resourceAndOrderBehavior` |
| `F25` | `informationControls` |
| `F26` | `compositionAndSemanticLoss` |
| `F27` | `oracleAllocation` |
| `F28` | `authorityLimit` |

The contract uses label-to-field mapping, not punctuation parsing. `capabilityDependencies.required` and `capabilityDependencies.optionalEnrichment` are separate sets. Required dependencies form a directed acyclic graph and contain no self-reference.

### 11.2 Analysis Request and Plan

`AnalysisRequestRecord` contains request identity, authorization context, exact subject, requested capability profiles, desired result families, population/perimeter, project and execution contexts, information controls, resource budgets, deadline/cancellation reference, freshness requirement, and partial-result policy.

`AnalysisPlanRecord` contains the materialized capability dependency graph, exact profile versions, provider-independent steps, declared optional enrichments, input/output contracts, validation stages, scheduling constraints, budgets, expected coverage, publication policy, and `recordDigest`. Scheduling order is not semantic order.

### 11.3 Analysis Run and Provider Invocation

`AnalysisRunRecord` contains one plan, one declared static subject and optional dynamic subject, configuration, start/end, content-bound child invocation and produced-record manifests finalized under §7.2, aggregate health, validation results, partiality, conflicts, and publication disposition.

`ProviderInvocationRecord` contains:

- identity-only parent run reference and exact plan step;
- provider, adapter, method, engine/rule/model/database/feed, and exact versions;
- exact capability profile and configuration;
- exact input manifest and authorization grant;
- resource budget and execution boundary;
- start/end, cancellation, timeout, retry, and attempt identity;
- raw request and raw response references;
- `modelExchangeBinding`, a closed union of `applicable` with exact content-bound Model Exchange reference or `not-applicable` with reason and rationale;
- provider-native health/diagnostics;
- validation and normalization references;
- result availability, truncation, and semantic-loss disclosure.

Every retry, reformat, repair, or model turn is another invocation and another exchange with predecessor and purpose relation.

### 11.3.1 Model Exchange Record

`ModelExchangeRecord` is a closed logical union of two material definitions: `ScopedModelExchangeRecord` uses `ScopedObservationEnvelope` and requires an exact non-repository scope; `SubjectModelExchangeRecord` uses `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` and requires an exact repository subject. The Package Manifest assigns each definition to only that one envelope, and a discriminator prevents the two variants from overlapping. Both variants contain:

| Field | Cardinality and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invocationRef` | 1 `RecordIdentityRef` to the not-yet-finalized parent invocation |
| `exchangeRole` | 1 of `initial`, `retry`, `reformat`, `repair` |
| `predecessorExchangeRef` | 0..1 `ContentBoundRecordRef`; required unless initial |
| `purpose` | 1 exact bounded purpose |
| provider/adapter/method/config refs | 1 exact set |
| `resolvedModelIdentity` | 1 closed union of exact provider/model/version/evidence or `unreported`/`unresolvable` with rationale |
| `promptTemplateRef`, `promptTemplateFingerprint` | 1 each; the fingerprint is a `DigestDescriptor` |
| `materializedInputArtifactRef` | 1 exact bytes actually presented after redaction |
| `inputRedactionManifestRef` | 1 |
| `rawOutputBeforeCoercionRef` | 1 exact raw output |
| `transportMetadataRef` | 0..1 |
| `truncationState` | 1 of `none-declared`, `declared`, `detected`, `unknown` |
| `omittedRegions` | 0..* exact role, reason, and known-bound state |
| parse, validation, disposition | exact parse outcome; validation refs; `accepted-for-normalization`, `rejected`, `quarantined`, or `repair-requested` |
| observations and controls | resource/time observations, diagnostics, information controls, limitations |

Repair never rewrites predecessor raw output. A fingerprint never substitutes for retained materialized input or raw output. Finalization order is invocation identity, finalized exchange with identity-only parent reference, then finalized invocation content-binding the exchange. This is the one content-bound direction.

### 11.4 Analyzer Provider Declaration carrier

`AnalyzerProviderDeclarationRecord` contains:

- stable provider, adapter, and declaration identities/versions;
- implemented capability IDs/versions;
- language, compiler, project, framework, and construct support;
- unsupported contexts and blind spots;
- inputs, preconditions, environment, and configuration;
- output classes, raw availability, transformations, and retention;
- engine, rule-set, model, database, advisory-feed, and configuration versions;
- declared soundness/completeness objectives;
- partial, unsupported, crash, cancellation, timeout, and malformed signals;
- determinism, seed, concurrency, cache, and reproducibility limits;
- incremental and invalidation behavior;
- CPU, memory, storage, time, and result-size behavior;
- filesystem, process, network, secret, egress, sandbox, and hostile-input constraints;
- licensing and redistribution constraints;
- normalization, location, severity, confidence, deduplication, and semantic-loss mappings;
- raw-to-normalized trace;
- health/self-diagnostic signals;
- disagreement and substitution limits;
- qualification-reference slot.

`qualificationRef` is either an exact `JAN-CSAA-011` reference or explicit `unqualified`, `unknown`, or `not-applicable`. The declaration itself never populates a qualified state.

### 11.4.1 Provider and adapter health

`HealthScopeBinding.scopeKind` is `provider-global`, `adapter-global`, `capability-subject`, `provider-subject`, `publication-subject`, or `operation-target`. Its discriminator requires the exact applicable provider, adapter, declaration, configuration, capability, subject, operation, or run references. It never invents a repository subject.

`ProviderHealthObservationRecord` uses `ScopedObservationEnvelope` and contains exact scope; provider declaration; optional adapter descriptor; observed provider/adapter/engine/rule-set/model/database/feed/configuration versions; check method/configuration; observed/expiry times; raw and diagnostic references; limitations; and these independent dimensions:

| Dimension | Exact values |
| --- | --- |
| `operationalHealth` | `healthy`, `degraded`, `unavailable`, `failed`, `unknown`, `not-checked` |
| `contractHealth` | `compatible`, `incompatible`, `unknown`, `not-checked` |
| `resourceHealth` | `within-budget`, `degraded`, `exhausted`, `unknown`, `not-checked` |
| `securityBoundaryHealth` | `within-declared-boundary`, `violation-observed`, `unknown`, `not-checked` |

It also carries freshness, dependency health, actual qualification standing, and `capabilityHealthAssessments: SET_CANONICAL(JAN-CSAA-007-EAT-C-005; key=CapabilityHealthAssessmentCanonicalKey)` under `JAN-CSAA-007-ECK-024`. Health never establishes correctness, completeness, qualification, assurance, authority, or semantic truth.

### 11.5 Raw result and transformation

`RawProviderResultRecord` contains invocation reference, media type/format version, exact `rawPayloadDigest`, availability, retention, redaction manifest, transport status, provider-native diagnostics, declared truncation, and safe preview metadata. Its payload is not a normalized semantic fact.

`TransformationRecord` contains exact source and target content-bound references, transformation kind and version, implementation/generator identity, content-bound configuration, mapping table, dropped/added/defaulted fields, coercions, semantic-loss classification, diagnostics, and `recordDigest`.

Semantic loss is `none-demonstrated`, `bounded-disclosed`, `unresolved`, or `prohibited`. `none-demonstrated` is an evidence-backed conclusion, not a default.

### 11.6 Validation stages

Validation executes logically in this order:

| Stage | Stage ID | Principal checks | Failure effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Transport/envelope | `V01` | availability, size, media type, framing, decode | Raw material retained; no normalized admission |
| Schema | `V02` | exact schema/version, closed fields, types, bounds | Invalid output inert |
| Subject/identity | `V03` | repository, snapshot, project, evidence set, references | Mismatched output inert |
| Semantic invariant | `V04` | owner constraints, endpoint closure, epistemic distinctions, `INV-*` | Invalid fact or relation rejected/quarantined |
| Provenance/raw trace | `V05` | producer, invocation, inputs, raw reference, lineage | No accepted normalized fact |
| Authorization/redaction | `V06` | grant, partition, disclosure, extension, secret policy | Deny or safely redact; no completeness fabrication |
| Publication eligibility | `V07` | health, freshness, coverage, conflict, partiality, manifest integrity | Refuse or publish explicitly bounded partial product |

`ValidationResultRecord` contains stage, subject, input/output references, validator identity/version, start/end, outcome, diagnostics, rejected regions, content-bound predecessor references, and correction rationale. Reverse successor navigation is derived rather than serialized into a predecessor. Outcome is `passed`, `failed`, `inconclusive`, `not-applicable`, or `not-run`. Only `passed` satisfies a required stage.

`NormalizationResultRecord` contains admitted and rejected record manifests, transformations, validation results, conflicts, semantic loss, coverage consequences, and raw lineage. Provider disagreement remains multiple records plus explicit conflict relations; normalization never selects truth by majority, score, or convenience.

### 11.7 Incremental and clean-full equivalence

`IncrementalAnalysisEquivalenceRecord` uses `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` and binds exact subject, incremental run, clean full run, compatible profile/provider/method/configuration references, comparison policy ID/version, compared families and populations, reused and recomputed manifests, invalidation closure, unsupported/missing regions, oracle reference with actual standing, and overall outcome.

It contains exactly one `DimensionComparison` for each of:

```text
semantic-result-sets
epistemic-states
coverage
provenance
conflicts
failures
explanations
deterministic-ordering
```

Each comparison records `equivalent`, `permitted-difference`, `different`, `not-compared`, or `inconclusive`, with before/after evidence, difference manifest, and any exact owner-governed allowed-difference policy. Overall outcome is `demonstrated-equivalent`, `demonstrated-non-equivalent`, `inconclusive`, or `not-run`. Only complete equivalent or explicitly permitted comparisons produce `demonstrated-equivalent`; counts, aggregate hashes, or matching record IDs alone never prove equivalence.

---

## 12. Query, slice, comparison, graph-delta, and change-impact contracts

### 12.1 Query Definition, Reference, and Request

`QueryDefinitionRecord` contains stable identity/version, purpose, subject/evidence binding policy, population, perimeter, graph/relation families, typed predicate expression, joins, traversal directions and bounds, project/build/environment/workload contexts, capability prerequisites, ordering policy, budgets, pagination, cancellation, truncation policy, access/redaction policy, and explanation obligations.

`QueryReferenceRecord` binds one definition and materialized parameters to exactly one Static Semantic Snapshot Identity and either one compatible Execution Evidence Set Identity or explicit `not-applicable`.

`QueryRequestRecord` combines the Query Reference with authorization, freshness requirement, requested page, result budget, deadline, cancellation reference, and partial-result acceptance. Cross-snapshot comparison uses independent query bindings plus a separate comparison record.

### 12.2 Typed query expression

The candidate query expression is a closed abstract syntax tree, not a provider-native query string:

| Node | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| `kind-is` | object or relation discriminator set |
| `id-equals` | typed reference |
| `attribute-predicate` | registered field path, typed operator, typed value |
| `has-relation` | relation kind, direction, endpoint predicate |
| `traverse` | relation kinds, direction, depth/path bounds, node predicate |
| `and` / `or` | ordered nonempty child expressions |
| `not` | one child expression |
| `exists` | closed population and child expression |
| `for-all` | closed population and child expression |
| `join` | left/right population, key expressions, join kind, loss policy |
| `aggregate` | population, grouping, measure, denominator, completeness policy |

Provider-specific syntax is an adapter input only. The adapter retains both native query and normalized AST plus transformation evidence.

`QueryExpression` is a registered same-document recursive definition. Every root expression carries one `ExpressionBudget` with positive safe-integer `maxNodes`, `maxDepth`, and `maxFanout`, plus an exact `resourceBudgetRef`. Traversal depth, aggregate-group, result-size, and execution-time bounds remain separate typed query and resource-budget fields. A validator counts the fully materialized normalized AST, rejects a root that exceeds any expression bound, and rejects a recursive reference outside the registered `QueryExpression` definition. An adapter cannot replace, relax, or bypass these bounds through provider-native syntax.

### 12.3 Query Result and explanation

`QueryResultRecord` contains:

- query definition/reference and producing Analysis Run;
- exact subject and capability/provider invocation references;
- materialized parameters;
- declared population, included/excluded/unknown regions, and closure basis;
- supported matches and supported non-matches as separate collections;
- predicate-truth projection per material region;
- the six-dimensional epistemic state per region;
- counts, numerators, denominators, lower-bound markers, and grouping context;
- ordering, page, cursor, truncation, traversal, and resource state;
- witness/explanation references;
- raw and transformation provenance;
- observation/record times and invalidation dependencies.

`predicateTruth` is `supported-true`, `supported-false`, `unknown`, or `conflicting`. Coverage, health, freshness, and perimeter states remain in their own fields.

`QueryExplanationRecord` contains material claim, supporting and contradicting records, witness paths, composition rules, omitted/unknown regions, semantic-loss disclosures, and safe human-readable rendering. If parent correlation is required, it uses an identity-only Query Result reference under §7.2; the finalized Query Result content-binds the explanation. Rendering never substitutes for the typed explanation graph.

### 12.4 Pagination and ordering

`PageRequest` contains `pageSize`, optional opaque `cursor`, and expected query-result lineage. `PageResult` contains returned count, opaque `nextCursor`, `hasMore`, total-count state, truncation state, canonical ordering identity, and covered region.

Total count is either `exact`, `lower-bound`, `unknown`, or `withheld`; only `exact` carries a population-wide exact value. Cursor identity binds query definition/version, parameters, subject, authorization/redaction context, ordering, and source publication. A mismatch invalidates the cursor.

Default deterministic order is `DefaultQueryResultOrderCanonicalKey` (`JAN-CSAA-007-ECK-025`), exactly `(kind, recordId, recordDigest.algorithm, recordDigest.value, recordDigest.profileId, recordDigest.profileVersion, recordDigest.representation)`, unless the query declares another complete key and deterministic tie-breaker. A presentation-only unordered projection cannot be a material paginated result and carries no positional semantics.

### 12.5 Slice

`SliceRequestRecord` contains criterion identity/location, direction `forward`, `backward`, or `chop`, included graph/relation families, interprocedural/context-sensitivity policy, alias/dispatch/exception/async/generated/runtime treatment, exact capability profiles, subject, scope, and bounds.

`SliceResultRecord` contains included members, typed witness paths, unresolved frontier, unsupported seams, excluded regions, conflicts, truncation, coverage basis, and invalidation dependencies. Runtime observations can add or corroborate paths but never silently prune unobserved static possibilities.

### 12.6 Semantic Comparison and Graph Delta

`SemanticComparisonRecord` contains before/after subject references, role labels, semantic/profile/graph/provider/project/resolver/generated/build/runtime compatibility decisions, lineage method, ambiguous and unmatched regions, coverage/health differences, raw inputs, producing run, explanations, and invalidation dependencies.

`GraphDeltaRecord` uses `ScopedObservationEnvelope` and contains exact before/after Graph Snapshot content-bound references, producing Semantic Comparison and Analysis Run references, the complete compatibility-decision set, population and coverage basis, a content-bound `entries` manifest, explanations, and invalidation dependencies. `entries` is `SET_CANONICAL(JAN-CSAA-007-EAT-C-006; key=GraphDeltaEntryManifestBindingCanonicalKey)` under `JAN-CSAA-007-ECK-026`. Each binding serializes `entryId` beside the finalized `entryRef`; the value must equal the referenced entry’s authoritative `/scope/parameters/entryId`, and canonicalization never dereferences a target. Repeated `entryId` is invalid. Entry-to-live-parent and finalized-entry-to-parent directions remain exactly FDR-010 / `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D013`. `GraphDeltaEntryRecord` is an addressable material record using `ScopedObservationEnvelope` with `graph-delta-entry` scope. It identity-references its not-yet-finalized parent Graph Delta and contains `entryId`, one exact `deltaKind`, `beforeRef` and `afterRef` as content-bound references or explicit reasoned `not-applicable`, the applicable compatibility-decision reference, lineage state and method, evidence references, confidence basis, inverse behavior, and any inverse-entry identity-only reference. The parent identity, entry IDs, and final content-bound manifest obey the §7.2 finalization direction. The exact delta-kind registry is:

```text
added
removed
modified
moved
renamed
reclassified
relation-added
relation-removed
coverage-changed
health-changed
freshness-changed
provenance-changed
provider-changed
conflicting
unknown
incomparable
```

Every entry binds before and after references as applicable. `lineageState` is exactly `stable-identity`, `supported-lineage`, `inferred-lineage`, `ambiguous`, or `unmatched`. `inverseBehavior` is `exact-inverse`, `inverse-with-declared-loss`, `not-invertible`, or `not-applicable`. An `exact-inverse` entry names the corresponding inverse kind and reverses the content-bound before/after references. A non-invertible or lossy entry identifies the information that prevents exact inversion. Reverse lifecycle discovery is not serialized as a successor pointer.

### 12.7 Change Seed and Impact

`ChangeSeedRecord` uses `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` and is a closed discriminated union. Every variant contains `seedId`, `seedKind`, exact subject identity, applicable Working Change Set reference, changed ranges and semantic-object/relation identities, unresolved source-to-semantic mappings, derivation method/version, coverage basis, epistemic state, occurrence time, provenance, source references, invalidation dependencies, and `recordDigest`. Variant-specific fields are:

| `seedKind` | Required variant fields |
| --- | --- |
| `source-operation` | operation `edit`, `add`, `delete`, `move`, or `rename`; before/after source locations or reasoned `not-applicable`; affected artifact references |
| `semantic-delta` | exact `GraphDeltaEntryRecord` references and affected object/relation populations |
| `contract-declaration-generated-change` | affected contract, declaration, generator, generated artifact, and mapping-chain references |
| `dependency-resolution-change` | affected manifest, lockfile, package, resolver, path-alias, conditional-export, and resolution-attempt references |
| `configuration-tool-provider-profile-change` | affected project, compiler, framework, generator, analyzer, provider, model, rule, or profile identities and before/after versions |
| `build-instrumentation-execution-change` | affected build, instrumentation, test-selection, environment, collector, schema, workload, coverage, trace, or source-map references |
| `invalidated-evidence-or-assumption` | exact invalidated record references, invalidation causes, and prior support assumptions |

`ImpactCandidateRecord.state` is:

```text
directly-affected
transitively-affected
runtime-observed-affected
inferred-possibly-affected
unresolved
not-evaluated
unsupported
stale
incompatible
not-affected-within-closed-basis
```

`ChangeImpactResultRecord` uses `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope`; its `SubjectBinding` carries the exact primary subject and any comparison subjects with explicit roles. It contains the exact seed, query definition/reference and Analysis Plan, propagation profiles and relation families, Reachability Assessment references, direct/transitive/inferred/runtime witness paths, candidate states, confidence bases, unresolved frontiers, unsupported seams, exclusions, conflicts, population and closure basis, coverage, budgets, semantic and presentation truncation, partiality, failure, full epistemic state, suggested next evidence, provenance, explanations, and invalidation dependencies. Each candidate binds its exact object or relation reference, one state, at least one witness for every positive affected state, and the evidence still required for every unresolved state.

Zero observed static callers is represented through explicit reachability surface, entry-population closure, unresolved mechanisms, positive candidates, and bounded conclusion. No discriminator or Boolean named `deadCode` exists in this contract.

### 12.8 Reachability Surface and Assessment

`ReachabilitySurfaceDefinitionRecord` uses `DefinitionEnvelope` and contains a stable definition identity/version, exact applicability rule, named entry populations, entry-mechanism registry, included and excluded graph/relation families, dynamic/generated/runtime treatment, closure criteria, required capability profiles, provider constraints, and invalidation dependencies.

The permanent entry-mechanism registry and exact source mapping are:

| Entry-mechanism ID | Exact mechanism | `JAN-CSAA-006` zero-static-callers mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `package-or-executable-entry` | package and executable entry points | `not-applicable` — added from `JAN-CSAA-003` §6.3 |
| `framework-route-component-action-loader-handler-or-hook` | framework routes, components, actions, loaders, handlers, and hooks | `JAN-CSAA-006-ZSC-001` |
| `test-runner-or-configured-test-discovery` | test runners and configured test discovery | `not-applicable` — added from `JAN-CSAA-003` §6.3 |
| `dynamic-import-or-conditional-loading` | dynamic imports and conditional loading | `JAN-CSAA-006-ZSC-003` |
| `dependency-injection-or-service-registry` | dependency-injection and service registries | `JAN-CSAA-006-ZSC-005` |
| `event-message-command-callback-timer-or-subscription` | event, message, command, callback, timer, and subscription registration | `JAN-CSAA-006-ZSC-004` |
| `decorator-or-metadata-driven-discovery` | decorator- or metadata-driven discovery | `not-applicable` — added from `JAN-CSAA-003` §6.3 |
| `reflection-or-name-based-lookup` | reflection and name-based lookup | `JAN-CSAA-006-ZSC-002` |
| `configuration-manifest-script-plugin-or-extension` | configuration, manifest, script, plugin, and extension entry | `JAN-CSAA-006-ZSC-009` |
| `generated-or-virtual-source-entry` | generated and virtual-source entry | `JAN-CSAA-006-ZSC-008` |
| `externally-invoked-api-job-protocol-or-native-boundary` | externally invoked APIs, jobs, protocols, and native boundaries | `JAN-CSAA-006-ZSC-006` |
| `runtime-observed-entry-for-exact-workload` | runtime-observed entries for one exact workload | `JAN-CSAA-006-ZSC-007` |

`ReachabilityAssessmentRecord` uses `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` and binds one surface definition, exact subject, target population, producing run and invocations, one `EntryMechanismAssessment` for every registered mechanism, static and runtime witness paths, positive entry candidates, unresolved frontiers, coverage, health, freshness, and invalidation dependencies. Each mechanism assessment binds its exact entry-population reference and records `applicable`, `not-applicable`, or `unresolved` applicability plus `closed-and-resolved`, `open`, `unsupported`, `not-analyzed`, `failed`, `stale`, or `incompatible` resolution state, entry candidates, closure evidence, evidence limits, and rationale. An observed unregistered mechanism is retained as an explicit unsupported frontier and prevents negative closure until a contract successor registers and analyzes it.

`reachabilityConclusion` is `reachable`, `candidate-unreachable-within-closed-surface`, or `inconclusive`. A positive supported entry yields `reachable`. `candidate-unreachable-within-closed-surface` is permitted only when every applicable entry population is nonempty where required, closed, completely analyzed, current, compatible, and successfully resolved with no positive entry. Every other negative-looking state is `inconclusive`. None of these values means dead code, safe removal, a finding, or permission.

## 13. Test, coverage, and runtime-trace contracts

### 13.1 Test definitions, selection, run, attempt, result, and assertion

| Record | Required variant fields |
| --- | --- |
| `TestSuiteRecord` | framework/runner definition, source occurrence, contained test references |
| `TestRecord` | runner-scoped definition, source occurrence, declared identity |
| `TestCaseRecord` | test reference, parameter/example coordinates |
| `TestTargetRecord` | target mode, source/build/execution artifact, project/runtime context |
| `TestSelectionRecord` | runner config, filters, shards, tags, files, resolved selected tests, selection time |
| `TestRunRecord` | static subject, target, runner/config/version, environment, selection, start/end, content-bound finalized attempt manifest |
| `TestAttemptRecord` | identity-only not-yet-finalized run parent, test/case, attempt ordinal, start/end, raw result |
| `TestResultRecord` | attempt, outcome, diagnostics/output, duration |
| `AssertionOutcomeRecord` | attempt, assertion identity/location, target claim/condition, outcome, diagnostics |

Test and assertion outcomes use `passed`, `failed`, `errored`, `timed-out`, `cancelled`, `skipped-by-declared-policy`, `not-run`, or `unknown`. Retry aggregation retains every attempt. `skipped-by-declared-policy` is not passing evidence.

### 13.2 Coverage

`CoverageObservationRecord` binds exact Test Run or Runtime Execution, Instrumentation Configuration and sites, target Execution Artifact, selection/workload, regions, Denominator Basis, Measurement Granularity, metric, provider declaration and exact provider method/version, source mappings, collection health, and time.

`CoverageRegionRecord` binds target artifact, provider coordinates, source mapping, generated/authored role, metric kind, covered measure, and total eligible measure.

`DenominatorBasisRecord` contains provider/metric, eligible region universe, include/exclude rules, target, subject, and derivation. `MeasurementGranularityRecord` names unit and aggregation level.

Coverage values use exact integer counts or `DecimalMeasure`. Percentages without numerator, denominator, compatible target, provider, granularity, selection/workload, and mapping are invalid.

### 13.3 Runtime build, environment, workload, and execution

`RuntimeBuildIdentityRecord` contains Execution Artifact, `artifactContentDigest`, producing build/configuration, packaging/deployment coordinates, and source mapping.

`RuntimeEnvironmentIdentityRecord` contains OS/runtime/platform, content-bound relevant dependency and configuration references, container/host or bounded environment reference, and `recordDigest`. Secrets are referenced through `SecretReference`; they are never embedded.

`WorkloadSelectionRecord` contains workload identity, filters, dataset/request references, included and excluded population, boundary, and `recordDigest`.

`RuntimeExecutionRecord` binds runtime build, environment, exact execution input as a separate `RawArtifactRef` or content-bound input record, workload selection, time boundary, instrumentation, authorization, resource limits, execution health, raw outputs, and the content-bound finalized child-trace manifest required by §7.2.

### 13.4 Trace schema, collector, trace, span, and event

`TraceSchemaRef` is a `ContractRef` with exact schema owner, schema identity/version, `contractContentDigest`, media type, semantic scope, compatibility state, and any required extension-registry reference.

`TraceCollectorDefinitionRecord` uses `DefinitionEnvelope` and contains collector identity/version, implementation artifact reference, supported Trace Schema contracts, configuration contract, clock-source and synchronization capabilities, trace/span context-propagation capabilities, supported sampling and capture policies, ordering guarantees, buffering/flush behavior, declared dropped-event and backpressure signals, known loss modes, security/redaction requirements, resource behavior, and invalidation dependencies.

`TraceCollectionObservationRecord` uses `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` and content-binds one Trace Collector Definition, exact configuration, and Trace Schema. It identity-references the not-yet-finalized target Runtime Execution, and carries the actual clock/context behavior, sampling/capture policy, time boundary, dropped-event and backpressure observations, redaction and information-control binding, resource observations, raw-output references, health, limitations, and invalidation dependencies. The `SemanticObject.trace-collector` variant is this exact occurrence projection and carries its `collectorDefinitionRef`; it is not a second collector definition.

`TraceRecord` contains Runtime Execution identity reference, Runtime Environment Identity, Workload Selection, trace schema, Trace Collection Observation, trace identity within that context, time boundary, content-bound root/span/event manifests finalized under §7.2, sampling/capture state, ordering/clock basis, observation limits, and completeness limits. Event-manifest order is keyed first by explicit `eventOrdinal`, then `occurredAt`, event identity, and the complete content-bound reference key; timestamp alone never orders events.

`SpanRecord` identity-references its not-yet-finalized Trace and contains Trace Schema, Trace Collection Observation, Runtime Execution identity, Runtime Environment Identity, Workload Selection, span identity, parent/link context, operation, time interval, status, observation limits, and a closed `SpanAttributeSet` whose registered keys have exact value types and disclosure rules. Provider-native or unregistered attributes remain in the raw trace or an explicit namespaced extension and cannot become semantic facts by key similarity. `EventRecord` identity-references its not-yet-finalized Trace where applicable and contains Trace Schema, Trace Collection Observation, Runtime Execution identity, Runtime Environment Identity, Workload Selection, trace/span or execution reference, event identity/ordinal, time, schema-typed payload reference, capture context, and observation limits.

Runtime-to-source correlation binds the runtime artifact and location through build/origin mappings. A captured execution remains one observed workload and never becomes exhaustive runtime possibility.

## 14. Rule, result, finding, treatment, gate, and assurance-reference contracts

### 14.1 Analysis Rule Profile contract and registry

`AnalysisRuleProfileRecord` uses `DefinitionEnvelope`. `AnalysisRuleProfileRef` is a `ContentBoundRecordRef` containing permanent profile ID, exact version, `recordDigest`, lifecycle, and definition-carrier reference. The full record contains exactly these eighteen named facets; each is required and each inapplicable value carries an exact rationale:

| Facet field | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| `identityAndVersion` | permanent ARP ID, semantic version, immutable content identity, lifecycle, and predecessor relation |
| `purposeAndProtectedDecision` | engineering question and explicit `rule-only` protected-action treatment |
| `subjectAndApplicability` | subject policy, scope, configuration, generated/excluded regions, dirty-worktree treatment, and applicability predicate |
| `claim` | exact polarity and one fixed claim character |
| `requiredEvidence` | exact capability profiles, coverage, freshness, provenance, and permitted corroboration |
| `criteriaAndOutcomes` | supported, violated, inconclusive, and not-applicable criteria |
| `severityAndConfidence` | profile interpretation independent of raw provider metadata and blocking effect |
| `transitionEffectTreatment` | `rule-only` or exact inert RGT design provenance; never a current transition effect |
| `profileOwnerAndAuthority` | content owner plus `unassigned` binding-authority state for the bound baseline |
| `nonBypassBoundary` | exact `N/A — no instantiated RGP or protected transition` |
| `failureAndLocalRunTreatment` | timeout, failure, unsupported, stale, conflict, and early-feedback behavior |
| `interimCarrier` | exact `N/A — no instantiated RGP or protected transition` |
| `independence` | author, oracle, provider, executor, disposer, exception authority, carrier, and canonical-authority separation |
| `eligibleCapabilities` | full capability-profile identities/versions and permitted provider declarations |
| `falsePositiveAndDisagreementTreatment` | false-positive/negative classes, evidence, review, conflict preservation, and no-majority-vote rule |
| `remediationAndReanalysis` | successor-subject requirement and historical preservation |
| `exceptionAuthorityAndRecord` | exact `N/A — no instantiated RGP or protected transition` for the baseline, plus prospective eligibility constraints |
| `retention` | raw, normalized, transformation, contradiction, evaluation, and supersession history |

`claim.character` is exactly `hard-invariant`, `owner-defined-rule`, `heuristic-smell`, or `metric-advisory`. The following registry is closed for `JAN-CSAA-004@0.1.0 / Draft`; every row incorporates the exact common-clause set `ARP-COM-001` through `ARP-COM-028` and its profile-specific addendum from that source:

| Profile ID | Assurance area | Fixed claim character | Transition design |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-001` | Composite implementation readiness | `owner-defined-rule` | inert `RGT-001` provenance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-002` | Syntax and type correctness | `hard-invariant` | inert `RGT-002` provenance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-003` | Contract conformance | `owner-defined-rule` | inert `RGT-003` provenance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-004` | Architecture-boundary conformance | `owner-defined-rule` | inert `RGT-004` provenance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-005` | Dependency integrity and cycles | `owner-defined-rule` | inert `RGT-005` provenance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-006` | Dead or unreachable code | `heuristic-smell` | `rule-only` |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-007` | Coupling and change amplification | `metric-advisory` | `rule-only` |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-008` | Behavioral preservation | `owner-defined-rule` | inert `RGT-008` provenance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-009` | Test adequacy | `owner-defined-rule` | inert `RGT-009` provenance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-010` | Security weakness and taint flow | `owner-defined-rule` | inert `RGT-010` provenance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-011` | Third-party and supply-chain exposure | `owner-defined-rule` | inert `RGT-011` provenance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-012` | Unsafe input/output handling | `owner-defined-rule` | inert `RGT-012` provenance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-013` | Concurrency and asynchronous-control risk | `heuristic-smell` | `rule-only` |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-014` | Error and recovery behavior | `heuristic-smell` | `rule-only` |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-015` | Observability sufficiency | `owner-defined-rule` | `rule-only` |

| `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-017` | Semantic-index freshness and completeness | `hard-invariant` | inert `RGT-017` provenance |

For every row, `bindingAuthority` is `unassigned` with reason `no recognized ARP-binding record`; `definitiveCarrier` and `interimCarrier` carry exact reason `N/A — no instantiated RGP or protected transition`. Neither state defaults from omission.

### 14.2 Rule Application Result

`RuleApplicationResultRecord` is an immutable, addressable top-level record. An embedding operation may include a projection, but the projection always carries and resolves the top-level immutable reference.

The record contains:

- permanent identity, contract and semantic versions, `recordDigest`, lifecycle, and predecessor relations;
- producing Analysis Run and Provider Invocation identities;
- exact subject and Analysis Rule Profile `ContentBoundRecordRef`;
- exact concern-owning criterion or rule reference;
- every capability profile, provider, adapter, required qualification, configuration, raw result, and normalized fact;
- raw-to-normalized transformation and validation lineage;
- rule-outcome product and rationale;
- coverage, unsupported/excluded/unresolved regions, freshness, and invalidation dependencies;
- criterion-by-criterion results and explanations;
- bounded technical conclusion;
- profile-derived severity, confidence basis, and blocking context as independent fields;
- no serialized forward finding reference; findings content-bind this finalized result and reverse finding lookup is derived;
- observation and record times.

The rule-outcome product preserves:

| Dimension | Exact carrier |
| --- | --- |
| `applicability` | `applicable`, `not-applicable`, `unresolved` |
| `executionHealth` | `complete`, `partial`, `not-analyzed`, `failed`, `timed-out`, `cancelled`, `unavailable`, `malformed` |
| `evidenceState.freshness` | `current`, `stale`, `invalidated`, `unknown` |
| `evidenceState.capability` | `supported`, `unsupported`, `partial`, `unknown` |
| `evidenceState.coverage` | `complete-for-declared-basis`, `incomplete`, `unknown` |
| `epistemicConclusion` | `supported`, `violated`, `inconclusive` |
| `agreement` | `consistent`, `conflicting` |

This product is separate from the six-dimensional common `epistemic` field. A universal status enum is prohibited because it cannot preserve both products.

### 14.3 Engineering Evidence Record and Analyzer Finding Record

`EngineeringEvidenceRecord` contains exact subject, producing facts/run, technical scope, provenance, limitations, and lifecycle. A result or finding that uses it content-binds the finalized evidence record; reverse use lookup is derived and is never serialized into the evidence predecessor. Its discriminator never implies canonical Evidence.

`AnalyzerFindingRecord` contains:

- stable occurrence identity and recurrence lineage;
- producing Rule Application Result `ContentBoundRecordRef`;
- exact repository subject and Rule Profile;
- precise claim, location, deficiency, implication, and rule character;
- profile-derived severity and blocking context;
- raw provider severity/confidence as separate provider metadata;
- evidence, raw result, invocation, provider/rule/configuration, validation, normalization, and transformation references;
- capability, health, freshness, unsupported regions, and conflicts;
- content-bound predecessor finding references for recurrence or correction, with recurrence basis;
- creation time, invalidation dependencies, and append-only lifecycle.

Treatment, exception, suppression, remediation, and reanalysis records content-bind the finalized finding; reverse treatment lookup is derived and never serialized into the finding predecessor. Recurrence creates a new occurrence. Deduplication creates typed `duplicate-of` and `surviving-occurrence` relations; it does not erase either finding.

### 14.4 Finding treatment records

The treatment axes remain independent:

| Axis | Exact values |
| --- | --- |
| `review` | `unreviewed`, `confirmed`, `disputed`, `false-positive`, `duplicate` |
| `remediation` | `unresolved`, `remediation-proposed`, `changed-pending-reanalysis`, `resolved-by-successor-subject-reanalysis` |
| `freshness` | `current`, `stale`, `invalidated`, `superseded` |
| `exceptionEffect` | `none`, `effective`, `expired`, `revoked`, `invalid` |
| `suppressionEffect` | `none`, `presentation-only`, `configuration-only`, `presentation-and-configuration-only` |

`FindingDispositionRecord` carries exact finding and applicable result `ContentBoundRecordRef` values, one review value, reviewer and recognized review authority, decision/record times, evidence, rationale, assumptions, limits, conflict treatment, and subtype fields for duplicate, disputed, or false-positive conclusions.

`RemediationRecord` content-binds its finding/result targets and carries actor, proposed or performed action, exact successor change/subject where applicable, rationale, status, times, and lineage.

`ReanalysisRecord` content-binds the finding and prior result, and carries run, invocation, successor subject, compatible profile/criterion, provider/qualification, evidence health, outcome, and failure history. Only a successful current compatible successor result can support `resolved-by-successor-subject-reanalysis`.

`SuppressionTreatmentRecord` carries target/scope, content-bound configuration or policy reference, actor/authority, rationale, effect, effective time, expiry/review trigger, predecessor relations, and mandatory-visibility indicator. Reverse successor navigation is derived.

`EngineeringExceptionRecord` carries independent identity/lifecycle plus exact rule, criterion, RGP, protected transition, subject/version scope, finding/result or exact prerequisite deficiency, effective authority evidence, residual technical risk, author/reviewer, effect and record times, expiry/review/renewal, conditions, compensating controls, downstream impact, non-waivability, and history.

An inapplicable consequential field uses `{ "state": "not-applicable", "rationale": "..." }`; a bare `N/A`, null, blank, or absent required field is invalid.

### 14.5 Repository Gate Template, designation, and possible future Profile

`RepositoryGateTemplateRecord` uses `DefinitionEnvelope` and carries the same eighteen named facet fields defined in §14.1, but every field whose value can arise only from designation uses the exact unresolved state below. Its reusable fields describe prospective protected transition, subject/applicability, claim, evidence, criteria, severity/confidence, failure/local-run treatment, independence, eligible capabilities, false-positive/disagreement treatment, remediation/reanalysis, and retention. It cannot carry an RGP identity, effective authority, carrier, qualification, oracle conferral, exception authority, or transition effect.

Its exact lifecycle fields are:

```text
designationState: undesignated-template
profileState: not-a-profile
bindingAuthority: unresolved-by-designation
definitiveCarrier: unresolved-by-designation
protectedTransitionEffect: unresolved-by-designation
providerQualification: unresolved-by-designation
effectiveOracle: unresolved-by-designation
```

The closed template registry is:

| Template ID | Component ARP | Prospective assurance area |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-001` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-001` | Composite implementation readiness |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-002` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-002` | Syntax and type correctness |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-003` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-003` | Contract conformance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-004` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-004` | Architecture-boundary conformance |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-005` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-005` | Dependency integrity and cycles |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-008` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-008` | Behavioral preservation |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-009` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-009` | Test adequacy |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-010` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-010` | Security weakness and taint flow |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-011` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-011` | Third-party and supply-chain exposure |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-012` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-012` | Unsafe input/output handling |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-016` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-016` | Maintainability and complexity |
| `JAN-CSAA-004-RGT-017` | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-017` | Semantic-index freshness and completeness |

There is no Repository Gate Profile instance in the current source baseline. A template reference is rejected anywhere a profile reference is required.

`RepositoryGateDesignationRecord` is a reserved `ControlEventEnvelope` variant. It requires authoritative designation record and effective time; assurance area and exact protected transition; exact component ARP identities, versions, and content identities; nonempty closed blocking and closed advisory populations; concern owner; binding authority or reasoned `unbound`; definitive carrier and enforcement artifact or reasoned `unbound`; interim carrier and transfer plan or reasoned `not-applicable`; provider-qualification prerequisites; independently governed oracle and change procedure; exception authority and non-waivable conditions; subject/applicability/scope/exclusions; and retention, invalidation, re-evaluation, supersession, and withdrawal rules.

`RepositoryGateProfileRecord` is a reserved future `DefinitionEnvelope` variant. It requires a content-bound designation reference, collision-checked permanent RGP ID, exact component ARPs, protected transition, subject applicability, nonempty closed blocking population, closed advisory population, binding authority or explicit reasoned `unbound`, definitive carrier or explicit reasoned `unbound`, interim carrier/transfer plan, provider qualifications, independently governed oracle, exception authority, local-run treatment, failure/disagreement/staleness behavior, scope, retention, invalidation, re-evaluation, supersession, and withdrawal. Its eighteen named facets use the §14.1 field registry but carry RGP-specific transition-effect, authority, carrier, and exception values. The variant cannot validate without the designation reference and every designation-supplied field.

### 14.6 Repository Gate Evaluation

`RepositoryGateEvaluationRecord` requires an exact RGP reference and therefore cannot be instantiated from the current baseline. Its reserved shape contains:

- immutable evaluation identity and exact subject;
- exact RGP and component ARP versions/digests;
- Rule Application Results, admitted evidence, findings, and raw references;
- capability, health, freshness, unsupported regions, and conflicts;
- every effective, expired, invalid, rejected, or inapplicable exception;
- advisory findings;
- execution/record times;
- aggregate result and derivation;
- currentness/invalidation boundary and history.

`aggregateResult` is `satisfied-without-exception`, `permitted-with-effective-exception`, `blocked`, `withheld`, or `not-applicable`. It is derived by the ordered predicates owned by `JAN-CSAA-004`; a numeric maximum, majority, confidence average, provider count, or Boolean reduction is not a valid derivation.

`permitted-with-effective-exception` remains visibly qualified and retains every underlying violation or exact eligible evidence deficiency.

### 14.7 Canonical assurance references

`GovernedAssuranceReference` contains external owner, permanent/versioned identity, exact scope, subject, status, authority, and provenance. `AssuranceMappingRecord` carries technical source records, mapping method/version, admissibility evaluation reference, resulting external reference, and limitations.

No CSAA record discriminator is named canonical `evidence`, `assessment`, `observation`, `decision`, `waiver`, `approval`, or `baseline`. A canonical service independently evaluates admissibility and owns any resulting canonical record.

## 15. Fixture, scenario, proposed expected-judgment, oracle, matrix, mutation, and degradation contracts

### 15.1 Fixture Manifest

`FixtureManifestRecord` contains:

- fixture identity/version/lifecycle and lane `synthetic` or `dated-jpwb`;
- exact source, project, build, configuration, generated, test, coverage, runtime, trace, source-map, and external artifacts;
- immutable initial state and reset identity;
- scenario manifest and required capability/rule/gate-template coverage;
- proposed expected-judgment manifest;
- mutation manifest;
- access, confidentiality, redaction, retention, and isolation treatment;
- raw supporting `RawArtifactRef` values;
- oracle lifecycle and review references;
- known gaps and invalidation dependencies.

A dated lane also contains exact repository cutoff and evidence identity. It never floats to a later repository state.

Fixture construction follows the §7.2 direction. A Fixture Manifest identity is minted first. Its `scenarioManifest` and `proposedExpectedJudgmentManifest` become content-bound only when the Fixture Manifest is finalized after those records. A Scenario Profile's `S11` carries the identity-only Fixture Manifest reference plus the exact raw artifact/content digests from which the fixture is constructed; it cannot carry the not-yet-finalized Fixture Manifest `recordDigest`. The `mutationManifest` is a closed plan manifest of mutation definitions/classes and target coordinates, not a collection of later `MutationRecord` occurrences. Oracle lifecycle and review references include only already-finalized records admitted by that manifest version. A new admission creates a successor Fixture Manifest; no Scenario Profile, Expected Judgment, or earlier Fixture Manifest is rewritten.

### 15.2 Thirty-facet Scenario Profile

`ScenarioProfileRecord` uses `DefinitionEnvelope` and contains one explicit typed value for each ordered facet `S01` through `S30`. The labels and meanings are exact:

| Facet | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `S01` | scenario identity and semantic version |
| `S02` | scenario lifecycle and oracle state |
| `S03` | fixture lane, family, case, and outcome mode |

| `S08` | included and excluded implementation, configuration, and generated perimeter |

| `S10` | manifest, lockfile, tool, and evidence coordinates |
| `S11` | identity-only parent Fixture Manifest reference plus exact fixture artifact/content digests; never the not-yet-finalized parent record digest |

Missing, blank, silently defaulted, reordered, or merged facets are invalid. `scenarioFacets` is `ORDERED` by the permanent `S01` through `S30` registry; positional order never replaces the facet discriminator.

### 15.3 Proposed Expected Record and oracle lifecycle

`ExpectedJudgmentRecord` uses `DefinitionEnvelope` and contains judgment identity/version; scenario; exact subject; requirement, invariant, capability, query, ARP, and inert RGT references as applicable; expected semantic objects, relations, truth projection, epistemic state, slice/delta/impact, Rule Application Result, finding and treatment state; expected non-green failure behavior; rationale; structured support basis; limitations; author; required independent-review and conferral-authority policies; the three state axes below; content-bound predecessor relations for correction or supersession; and invalidation dependencies. It never contains a forward reference to a later review, conferral, divergence, or correction record. A field not applicable to the exact scenario carries a typed reasoned `not-applicable` value rather than null, blank, or omission.

Its independent state product is:

| Axis | Exact values |
| --- | --- |
| `proposalState` | `proposed`, `withdrawn`, `superseded` |
| `conferralState` | `not-conferred`, `conferred`, `rejected`, `divergent`, `revoked` |
| `executionState` | `not-executed`, `executed`, `stale`, `invalidated` |

All expected judgments imported from `JAN-CSAA-006@0.1.0` carry `proposed / not-conferred / not-executed`.

`OracleLifecycleRecord` uses `ControlEventEnvelope` and content-binds the exact prior Expected Judgment or Oracle Lifecycle predecessor. It contains exact judgment grain, author, authorized independent reviewer, authority record, lifecycle action, resulting proposal/conferral/divergence state, rationale, decision/record times, evidence, and predecessor relations. Later challenge or correction events content-bind this finalized record; reverse history is derived. Provider or implementation output is never an oracle source by itself.

### 15.4 Matrix cell, mutation, and degradation

`CoverageMatrixDefinitionRecord` uses `DefinitionEnvelope`; `CoverageMatrixCellRecord` uses `DefinitionEnvelope` and content-binds its already-finalized matrix definition, Scenario Profile, and proposed Expected Judgment. It contains matrix identity/version, exact row identity, exact column identity, exact scenario identity, proposed expectation reference, coverage claim, gaps, trace tuple, and verification allocation. The matrix definition contains row/column registries and expected cell coordinates, but no forward content-bound cell references; complete cell-set validation is a package/fixture-manifest validation result or derived index. Three closed matrix registries exist:

| Matrix | Exact row registry | Exact ordered column registry | Exact cell count |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Capability outcome | `JAN-CSAA-CAP-001` through `JAN-CSAA-CAP-032` | `POS`, `NEG`, `UNK`, `PAR`, `CON`, `STA`, `DYN`, `NVA` | 256 |
| ARP judgment | `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-001` through `JAN-CSAA-004-ARP-017` | `positive`, `negative`, `inconclusive`, `partial`, `stale`, `disagreement`, `provider-failure`, `exception`, `suppression`, `non-bypass`, `zero-static-callers` | 187 |
| RGT inertness | the twelve exact §14.5 template IDs | `inert-baseline`, `misuse-rejection` | 24 |

Every cell binds a full scenario or zero-static-callers identity; a requirement-cluster shorthand cannot substitute for that identity. All cells remain proposed, non-conferred, and non-executed.

`MutationRecord` uses `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` and contains base fixture/scenario, one exact mutation-class ID, mutation operation, target, typed before/after `artifactContentDigest` or `recordDigest` values as applicable, intended semantic effect, affected facts/graphs/queries/rules/findings/matrix cells/judgments, expected failure or kill obligation, reset identity, successor-trigger conditions, lineage, and either an exact `IncrementalAnalysisEquivalenceRecord` reference or explicit `not-run`/`inconclusive` equivalence state. No incremental-equivalence claim validates without the exact comparison record. The closed mutation-class registry is:
