## 16. Logical operation, tool-call, authorization, cancellation, and response envelopes

### 16.1 Operation registry

Logical operations have permanent IDs and versions:

| Operation ID | Purpose | Principal response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `csaa.contract.negotiate` | Negotiate supported contract package/families | Compatibility decision |
| `csaa.subject.describe` | Resolve and describe exact subject identity | Subject manifest |
| `csaa.snapshot.get` | Retrieve one exact published snapshot manifest | Publication and subject refs |
| `csaa.analysis.plan` | Materialize provider-neutral analysis plan | Analysis Plan |
| `csaa.analysis.start` | Request separately authorized analysis | Operation acceptance/run ref |
| `csaa.analysis.status` | Inspect one run or operation | Operation state and diagnostics |
| `csaa.analysis.cancel` | Request cancellation | Cancellation acknowledgment |
| `csaa.query.execute` | Execute one normalized query | Query Result or partial/error |
| `csaa.slice.compute` | Compute one bounded slice | Slice Result or partial/error |
| `csaa.comparison.compute` | Compare exact subjects | Semantic Comparison |
| `csaa.impact.compute` | Propagate exact Change Seed | Change-Impact Result |
| `csaa.finding.get` | Read one authorized technical finding | Finding projection/reference |
| `csaa.finding.list` | Query authorized technical findings | Paged finding references |
| `csaa.raw.get` | Retrieve authorized raw material | Raw Artifact response |
| `csaa.fixture.describe` | Read fixture/scenario and actual oracle standing | Fixture projection |
| `csaa.gate.evaluate` | Reserved future RGP evaluation | Rejected without exact effective RGP |
| `csaa.health.get` | Inspect separate operational/provider/semantic health dimensions | Health response |

Transport binding is external. These operations can map to an in-process API, CLI, IPC, language server, or service only under a separately selected topology.

`operationInput` and the `success.result` union are keyed by the same exact `operationId`; cross-paired variants are invalid:

| Operation | Request-input variant | Success-result variant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `csaa.contract.negotiate` | `ContractNegotiationInput` | `CompatibilityDecisionRecord` |
| `csaa.subject.describe` | `SubjectDescribeInput` | `SubjectManifestRecord` |
| `csaa.snapshot.get` | `SnapshotGetInput` | `PublicationManifestRecord` |
| `csaa.analysis.plan` | `AnalysisPlanInput` | `AnalysisPlanRecord` |
| `csaa.analysis.start` | `AnalysisStartInput` | `AnalysisStartAcceptanceRecord` |
| `csaa.analysis.status` | `AnalysisStatusInput` | `AnalysisStatusRecord` |
| `csaa.analysis.cancel` | `AnalysisCancelInput` | `CancellationRecord` |
| `csaa.query.execute` | `QueryExecutionInput` | `QueryResultRecord` |
| `csaa.slice.compute` | `SliceComputationInput` | `SliceResultRecord` |
| `csaa.comparison.compute` | `SemanticComparisonInput` | `SemanticComparisonRecord` |
| `csaa.impact.compute` | `ChangeImpactInput` | `ChangeImpactResultRecord` |
| `csaa.finding.get` | `FindingGetInput` | `AnalyzerFindingRecord` |
| `csaa.finding.list` | `FindingListInput` | `FindingPageRecord` |
| `csaa.raw.get` | `RawGetInput` | `RawArtifactResponseRecord` |
| `csaa.fixture.describe` | `FixtureDescribeInput` | `FixtureProjectionRecord` |
| `csaa.gate.evaluate` | `GateEvaluationInput` | `RepositoryGateEvaluationRecord` |
| `csaa.health.get` | `HealthGetInput` | `HealthResponse` |

Each request-input variant contains only operation-specific fields in addition to `OperationRequestBase`; no generic property bag is permitted. `csaa.gate.evaluate` cannot return success unless an exact effective RGP exists, so the current baseline must return the applicable typed error.

### 16.2 Operation Request

`OperationRequestBase` uses `ControlEventEnvelope` and contains:

| Field | Cardinality |
| --- | ---: |
| `operationId` and `operationVersion` | 1 |
| `requestId` | 1 |
| `requestIdempotencyKey:RequestIdempotencyBinding` | 1 |
| `operationKey` | 1 |
| `requestedAt` | 1 |
| `compatibilityInput` | 1 |
| `repositoryWorktreeScope` | 0..1, as required by operation policy |
| `subjectInput` | 1 |
| `operationInput` | 1 |
| `freshnessRequirement` | 1 |
| `resourceBudget` | 1 |
| `deadline` | 0..1 |
| `cancellationTokenRef` | 0..1 |
| `partialResultPolicy` | 1 |
| `redactionPolicyRef` | 1 |
| `auditContext` | 1 |

The inherited `ControlEventEnvelope.authorityBinding.authorizationContextRef` is the only serialized authorization-context path. `OperationRequestBase` does not duplicate it. Its `requestedAt` satisfies the envelope's `occurredAt` mapping.

`subjectInput` is a closed union:

| Discriminator | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| `resolved-subject` | one exact `SubjectBinding` |
| `subject-locator` | repository/worktree locator, requested revision/change coordinates, project hints, and resolution policy; never a fabricated subject |
| `scoped-target` | an authorized scope plus one or more exact target populations needed by the operation |
| `target-record` | one content-bound target record reference whose own subject is retained |
| `live-target` | one `RecordIdentityRef` to a not-yet-finalized operation/run/invocation plus exact expected state, monotonic state revision, concurrency-token `DigestDescriptor`, and authorization scope |
| `not-applicable` | exact operation-policy reason; no subject fields |

`compatibilityInput` is `negotiation-offer` only for `csaa.contract.negotiate`; it contains offered package/family versions, required features, and unknown-field policy without claiming prior compatibility. Every other operation requires `resolved-compatibility` with an exact successful compatibility-decision reference. The negotiation operation rejects `resolved-compatibility`, and every non-negotiation operation rejects `negotiation-offer`.

The operation-to-subject policy is closed:

| Operation | Permitted `subjectInput` variants |
| --- | --- |
| `csaa.contract.negotiate` | `not-applicable` |
| `csaa.subject.describe` | `subject-locator` |
| `csaa.snapshot.get` | `resolved-subject`, `subject-locator` |
| `csaa.analysis.plan` | `resolved-subject`, `subject-locator` |
| `csaa.analysis.start` | `resolved-subject` |
| `csaa.analysis.status` | `live-target`, `target-record` |
| `csaa.analysis.cancel` | `live-target` |
| `csaa.query.execute` | `resolved-subject`, `target-record` |
| `csaa.slice.compute` | `resolved-subject`, `target-record` |
| `csaa.comparison.compute` | `scoped-target` |
| `csaa.impact.compute` | `resolved-subject`, `scoped-target`, `target-record` |
| `csaa.finding.get` | `target-record` |
| `csaa.finding.list` | `scoped-target` |
| `csaa.raw.get` | `target-record` |
| `csaa.fixture.describe` | `target-record`, `scoped-target` |
| `csaa.gate.evaluate` | `scoped-target` |
| `csaa.health.get` | `not-applicable`, `scoped-target`, `target-record` |

`SubjectResolutionOutcome` is a closed union: `resolved` carries one exact `SubjectBinding`; `not-found` carries `locatorDigest: DigestDescriptor`, its registered digest-profile reference, and a safe reason; `ambiguous` carries authorized candidate references or a withheld count; `forbidden` carries only the access-decision reference; `unavailable` carries safe diagnostics and retry state; and `incompatible` carries the compatibility decision. A `live-target` is valid only when its state revision and concurrency token match the authorized current observation; mismatch produces the applicable lifecycle typed error rather than rebinding the target. A denied or unresolved locator never causes the server to invent, widen, or silently substitute a subject.

`ToolCallRecord` additionally contains coding-agent or client identity, employment-point reference if later provided by `JAN-CSAA-010`, materialized arguments, presentation truncation separate from semantic truncation, result reference, and stop/escalation outcome.

### 16.3 Operation Response and state

`OperationResponse` is an abstract closed outcome union. Its four exact material definitions—`OperationProgressResponseRecord`, `OperationSuccessResponseRecord`, `OperationPartialResponseRecord`, and `OperationErrorResponseRecord`—each use `ControlEventEnvelope`; the outcome discriminator makes them disjoint. Every variant content-binds the finalized request and applicable access decision. A success variant content-binds its finalized operation result; a partial or error variant content-binds its finalized partial/error payload; a progress variant content-binds its finalized progress observation and uses only the `JAN-CSAA-007-FDR-016` identity reference for any live target. Every applicable Redaction Manifest is content-bound under `JAN-CSAA-007-FDR-014`. The response contains request/operation IDs, response time, the applicable exact `SubjectResolutionOutcome` or operation-policy `not-applicable`, diagnostics, and continuation/cancellation information. Request ID, operation/version, authorization context, principal, subject/data scope, and access-decision references must equal their bound predecessor values. A `forbidden` Subject Resolution Outcome carries the same access-decision reference as `authorityBinding`. A later audit event content-binds the finalized response; the response has no forward audit reference:

| Outcome variant | Exact material definition | Permitted state | Required variant content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `progress` | `OperationProgressResponseRecord` | `requested`, `accepted`, `running` | progress record and optional run/invocation reference; no success result |
| `success` | `OperationSuccessResponseRecord` | `succeeded` | one operation-specific result reference plus pagination and coverage/health/freshness summaries as applicable |
| `partial` | `OperationPartialResponseRecord` | `partial` | one `PartialResultRecord`; any admitted result references live inside it |
| `error` | `OperationErrorResponseRecord` | `failed`, `cancelled`, `timed-out`, `resource-refused`, `authorization-refused`, `incompatible`, `unknown` | one primary `TypedErrorRecord` and zero or more related diagnostics |

Operation state is:

```text
requested
accepted
running
partial
succeeded
failed
cancelled
timed-out
resource-refused
authorization-refused
incompatible
unknown
```

The `state` and outcome discriminator must satisfy the table; no other pair validates. Only `succeeded` means the logical operation completed its declared work. It says nothing by itself about predicate truth, rule satisfaction, gate result, assurance, or authority. A `partial` response identifies completed and missing regions and cannot occupy a success-only result variant.

`HealthResponse` is the operation-specific success result for `csaa.health.get`. It contains the requested `HealthScopeBinding`; an `ORDERED` `observationRefs` sequence of `HealthObservationBinding` values keyed by `JAN-CSAA-007-ECK-027`, exactly `(observedAt, observationKind, observationRef.ContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey)`; and five separately typed dimensions: `providerExecutionHealth`, `capabilityCoverage`, `evidenceFreshness`, `findingState`, and `laterGateOutcome`. The wrapper timestamp and kind agree with the finalized referenced observation. The response-to-observation edge follows `D001`; only a nested operation-target scope on that observation may use FDR-016 / `D019`. Each dimension carries exact observation or result references, actual standing, observation cutoff, omitted/withheld regions, and diagnostics; a dimension not requested carries reasoned `not-applicable`. It has no aggregate `healthy` Boolean or universal health status. Provider availability cannot establish semantic completeness, semantic currentness, qualification, finding state, gate outcome, or correctness; none of the other dimensions can establish provider availability.

### 16.4 Cancellation

`CancellationRecord` content-binds the cancellation request and access decision, identity-references the live target operation/run/invocation with its accepted state revision and concurrency token, and contains requester, authority binding, requested/effective times, reason, acknowledgment, final execution state, partial outputs, raw material, and cleanup/recovery allocation state. A later cleanup or recovery record content-binds the finalized cancellation; reverse recovery lookup is derived.

Cancellation is cooperative at a declared boundary. A cancellation request is not proof that execution stopped. Material produced before effective cancellation retains its actual identity, health, partiality, and publication eligibility.

---

### 16.5 Operational correlation without response-state overloading

The seventeen logical operations, their exact request/input pairings, public concurrency token, response discriminators, and closed state/outcome union remain unchanged. An operation request or response may carry an exact identity-only or finalized content-bound operational reference only where Appendix F registers the field and finalization direction. `AnalysisStatusRecord` carries an exact durable target reference, state revision, and public concurrency token; it does not become a claim, work-unit, attempt, candidate-lifecycle, read-view, cache, retention, or migration record.

`OperationTransitionRecord` records only an actual operation-response transition. Every operational machine transition is instead an immutable occurrence under its own stable machine identity and monotonic machine-specific revision. The operation transition and operational occurrence may correlate when both happened, but neither substitutes for the other.
## 17. Diagnostics, typed errors, unsupported regions, conflict, and partial results

### 17.1 Diagnostic

`DiagnosticRecord` contains stable code, severity, stage, safe summary, subject/operation/invocation refs, source locations, content-bound prior related-diagnostic and cause references, evidence/raw references, retryability, remediation category, and redaction state. Diagnostic dependency and cause references form an acyclic finalized-record graph; reverse related-diagnostic lookup is derived.

Diagnostic severity is `info`, `warning`, `error`, or `fatal`. It is operational/technical metadata and never substitutes for profile-derived severity, gate blocking, or canonical risk.

### 17.2 Typed error envelope

`TypedErrorRecord` uses exactly one value from the package-wide closed stable-code registry below: 65 preserved legacy codes plus twelve affected operational additions, for exactly 77 registered codes:

| Family | Exact codes |
| --- | --- |
| Request | `CSAA-E-REQUEST-MALFORMED`, `CSAA-E-REQUEST-UNSUPPORTED-OPERATION`, `CSAA-E-REQUEST-UNSUPPORTED-OPERATION-VERSION`, `CSAA-E-REQUEST-INVALID-PARAMETER` |
| Authorization | `CSAA-E-AUTH-UNAUTHENTICATED`, `CSAA-E-AUTH-UNAUTHORIZED`, `CSAA-E-AUTH-SCOPE-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-AUTH-REDACTION-REFUSED` |
| Subject | `CSAA-E-SUBJECT-UNIDENTIFIED`, `CSAA-E-SUBJECT-UNAVAILABLE`, `CSAA-E-SUBJECT-STALE`, `CSAA-E-SUBJECT-MIXED-REVISION`, `CSAA-E-SUBJECT-SNAPSHOT-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-SUBJECT-EVIDENCE-SET-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-SUBJECT-WORKTREE-MISMATCH` |
| Configuration | `CSAA-E-CONFIG-MISSING`, `CSAA-E-CONFIG-INVALID`, `CSAA-E-CONFIG-INCOMPATIBLE` |
| Capability | `CSAA-E-CAPABILITY-UNSUPPORTED`, `CSAA-E-CAPABILITY-EXCLUDED`, `CSAA-E-CAPABILITY-PARTIAL`, `CSAA-E-CAPABILITY-NOT-ANALYZED`, `CSAA-E-CAPABILITY-INCOMPATIBLE` |
| Semantic | `CSAA-E-SEMANTIC-PARSE-FAILED`, `CSAA-E-SEMANTIC-BIND-FAILED`, `CSAA-E-SEMANTIC-TYPE-FAILED`, `CSAA-E-SEMANTIC-RESOLUTION-FAILED`, `CSAA-E-SEMANTIC-GRAPH-CONSTRUCTION-FAILED`, `CSAA-E-SEMANTIC-INVARIANT-FAILED`, `CSAA-E-SEMANTIC-CORRELATION-FAILED`, `CSAA-E-SEMANTIC-MAPPING-FAILED` |
| Provider | `CSAA-E-PROVIDER-UNAVAILABLE`, `CSAA-E-PROVIDER-CRASHED`, `CSAA-E-PROVIDER-MALFORMED-OUTPUT`, `CSAA-E-PROVIDER-CONTRACT-VIOLATION`, `CSAA-E-PROVIDER-DISAGREEMENT` |
| Execution | `CSAA-E-EXECUTION-TIMED-OUT`, `CSAA-E-EXECUTION-CANCELLED`, `CSAA-E-EXECUTION-RESOURCE-EXHAUSTED`, `CSAA-E-EXECUTION-BUDGET-REFUSED` |
| Result | `CSAA-E-RESULT-TRUNCATED`, `CSAA-E-RESULT-PAGINATION-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-RESULT-PARTIAL`, `CSAA-E-RESULT-REGION-UNAVAILABLE` |
| Evidence | `CSAA-E-EVIDENCE-BUILD-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-EVIDENCE-INSTRUMENTATION-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-EVIDENCE-SELECTION-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-EVIDENCE-COVERAGE-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-EVIDENCE-TRACE-SCHEMA-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-EVIDENCE-COLLECTOR-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-EVIDENCE-WORKLOAD-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-EVIDENCE-ENVIRONMENT-MISMATCH`, `CSAA-E-EVIDENCE-SOURCE-MAP-MISMATCH` |
| Comparison | `CSAA-E-COMPARE-INCOMPATIBLE-BASIS`, `CSAA-E-COMPARE-AMBIGUOUS-LINEAGE`, `CSAA-E-COMPARE-NON-INVERTIBLE-LOSS` |
| Validation | `CSAA-E-VALIDATION-STAGE-FAILED`, `CSAA-E-VALIDATION-PROVENANCE-GAP`, `CSAA-E-VALIDATION-SEMANTIC-LOSS`, `CSAA-E-VALIDATION-PUBLICATION-REFUSED` |
| Lifecycle | `CSAA-E-LIFECYCLE-INVALIDATED`, `CSAA-E-LIFECYCLE-SUPERSEDED`, `CSAA-E-LIFECYCLE-CURSOR-EXPIRED`, `CSAA-E-LIFECYCLE-SUCCESSOR-REQUIRED` |
| Internal | `CSAA-E-INTERNAL-UNEXPECTED` |
| Operational configuration | `CSAA-E-CONFIG-OPERATIONAL-CONTEXT-STALE` |
| Operational provider | `CSAA-E-PROVIDER-QUALIFICATION-NONPASS` |
| Operational lifecycle | `CSAA-E-LIFECYCLE-OPERATIONAL-BASIS-UNRESOLVED` |
| Publication | `CSAA-E-PUBLICATION-GENERATION-CONFLICT`, `CSAA-E-PUBLICATION-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN` |
| Integrity | `CSAA-E-INTEGRITY-MATERIAL-NONPASS` |
| Migration | `CSAA-E-MIGRATION-EXECUTION-NONPASS` |
| Material lifecycle | `CSAA-E-MATERIAL-LIFECYCLE-ACTION-NONPASS` |
| Security control | `CSAA-E-SECURITY-CONTROL-NONPASS` |
| Audit durability | `CSAA-E-AUDIT-DURABILITY-FAILED` |
| External effect | `CSAA-E-EXTERNAL-EFFECT-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN` |
| Isolation | `CSAA-E-ISOLATION-BASIS-MISMATCH` |

Each error contains one primary code, exact stage, safe summary, code-discriminated `safeDetails`, content-bound prior cause and diagnostic references, affected region, retryability, and subject impact. Error cause references form an acyclic finalized-record graph. `safeDetails.kind` equals the full primary code exactly; a family-only discriminator never validates. Each exact code has its own closed schema that requires the corresponding row's fields and prohibits fields from every other family. The family registry below defines those code-specific field vocabularies:

| Family | Permitted safe fields |
| --- | --- |
| Request | parameter name, expected type/range, reason code |
| Authorization | access-decision and policy references; no protected target details |
| Subject | expected identity digests, authorized observed identity digests, mismatch dimension |
| Configuration | configuration kind, configuration reference, validation reason |
| Capability | capability/profile reference, affected perimeter, support state |
| Semantic | semantic stage, authorized source locations, failed invariant or mapping reference |
| Provider | provider declaration, invocation, contract version, safe provider status |
| Execution | budget/cancellation reference, resource class, retry boundary |
| Result | completed/omitted region references, cursor lineage, truncation boundary |
| Evidence | evidence coordinate kind, expected/observed authorized identity digests |
| Comparison | compatibility-decision reference, basis dimension, lineage/loss reference |
| Validation | validation stage/result, rejected-region reference, semantic-loss state |
| Lifecycle | affected record identity, invalidation/supersession reference, required successor kind |
| Internal | opaque safe correlation ID only |
| Operational configuration | profile instantiation, configuration kind, expected/observed authorized digests, staleness reason, required successor |
| Operational provider | provider declaration, qualification state/reference, qualification policy, retry boundary |
| Operational lifecycle | basis kind/reference or digest, unresolved state, affected region, reconciliation kind |
| Publication | authorized channel/candidate identities, predecessor and generation observations, idempotency digest, uncertainty boundary, reconciliation |
| Integrity | failure kind, material reference or digest, incident, containment, affected region |
| Migration | execution identity, failure kind, source/target profiles, checkpoint applicability, residual state |
| Material lifecycle | action kind/reference, policy, material class, verification and residual-copy state |
| Security control | control kind, policy/control references, control state, partition, retry boundary |
| Audit durability | evidence/event class, durability boundary, correlation, reconstructability, reconciliation |
| External effect | effect kind/key digest, intent, target, observed standing, reconciliation |
| Isolation | mismatch kind, expected/observed partition and revision or cutoff, affected operation |

Every exact-code variant rejects unregistered fields. Pagination mismatch, provider contract violation, lifecycle invalidation, and every other code therefore have distinct payload discriminators even when they share a family vocabulary. A path refusal is referenced through the selected authorization or subject error's `PathResolutionRefusalRecord` field; it does not add an unregistered error code. Secret values, unrestricted source excerpts, credentials, internal stack traces, absolute host paths, and unauthorized count, shape, target-existence, or identity information are excluded.

### 17.3 Partial Result

`PartialResultRecord` contains parent operation/result kind, exact completed region, exact missing/failed/withheld regions, causes, coverage and epistemic consequences, budgets/truncation, continuation if valid, invalidation dependencies, and admitted result references.

Partiality never uses the full-success discriminator. A consumer cannot infer population-wide false, absence, safety, conformance, or permission from completed regions alone.

### 17.4 Unsupported Region and Conflict

`UnsupportedRegionRecord` contains subject perimeter, constructs/contexts, capability/provider, reason, attempted method, known blind spot, required next evidence, and consequence.

`ConflictRecord` contains conflict kind, every contributing immutable record and raw reference, incompatible claims/values, subject and compatibility basis, detection method, unresolved/resolved state, resolution authority where applicable, and content-bound predecessor relations. A resolution record content-binds its conflict predecessor and retains every contributing record; reverse successor navigation is derived.

A typed error, diagnostic, unsupported region, conflict, or partial result is never encoded as successful emptiness, supported false, an Analyzer Finding Record, or a gate result.

---

### 17.5 Operational typed-error extension

Appendix F closes the twelve `JAN-CSAA-009-A007-ERR-GAP-001` through `012` distinctions with twelve stable operationally scoped codes in the configuration, provider, lifecycle, publication, integrity, migration, material-lifecycle, security, audit, external-effect, and isolation families, each with a code-discriminated safe payload. Section 17.2 lists all 77 package codes and every permitted family vocabulary; Appendix F supplies the twelve exact new code-to-gap and required-field variants. Gap identifiers are source-trace identities and are never serialized as codes. `CSAA-E-INTERNAL-UNEXPECTED` remains the opaque fallback only when no registered distinction is knowable; it cannot close a known configuration, qualification, dependency, publication, integrity, migration, retention, security, audit, external-effect, or partition mismatch.
## 18. Contract versioning, compatibility, unknown fields, deprecation, and logical migration

### 18.1 Version dimensions

The package distinguishes:

- document version;
- package manifest version;
- individual schema/contract version;
- semantic owner version;
- generated-derivative version;
- provider adapter declaration/version;
- record payload contract version;
- physical storage/migration version, owned later by `JAN-CSAA-009`.

Compatibility is directional and exact. `consumer A reads producer B` and `producer A writes consumer B` are different claims.

### 18.2 SemVer change classification

| Change | Minimum candidate classification |
| --- | --- |
| Clarification with identical validation and meaning | Patch |
| Add optional field at an explicit extension-compatible location | Minor |
| Add a new operation or independent record variant | Minor, unless exhaustive consumers break |
| Add enum value to a closed enum | Major |
| Add required field | Major |
| Remove or rename field/variant/operation | Major |
| Change discriminator, ID grammar, digest profile or identity projection, reference kind/direction, envelope assignment, collection semantics, recursive-definition budget, operation policy, typed-error registry, null, or unknown-field behavior | Major |
| Widen accepted input while preserving all prior semantics | Minor only with consumer analysis |
| Narrow accepted input or change output meaning | Major |
| Fix schema that previously accepted semantically invalid records | Major unless no valid instance changes and evidence proves patch safety |
| Change semantic owner meaning | New affected contract version; classification follows compatibility analysis |

Major version compatibility requires an explicit compatibility map or rejection. Same-major versions are not presumed compatible without the package manifest's directional declaration.

### 18.3 Unknown fields and extensions

Strict ingress rejects unknown core fields. `extensions` accepts only registered namespaced keys and bounded JSON. Core processors preserve but ignore unrecognized extension values. They cannot derive truth, completeness, severity, authority, or gate effect from them.

Adapters retain unknown provider-native data in the raw artifact. A normalized core mapping requires a versioned transformation and validation rule.

### 18.4 Compatibility Claim and Map

`CompatibilityClaimRecord` contains source/target contract and semantic-owner versions, direction, scope, assumptions, compared surface, result, semantic-loss state, evidence references, author/reviewer, time, and invalidation. The compared surface explicitly includes digest profiles and purpose projections; identity-only versus content-bound reference kinds and permitted directions; envelope assignments; collection semantics; recursive-definition registry and budgets; object/relation shape registries; operation/request/response policy; typed-error codes and code-specific safe payloads; and extension behavior.

Result is `compatible`, `compatible-with-bounded-loss`, `incompatible`, `unknown`, or `not-applicable`.

`CompatibilityMapRecord` contains exact source and target fields/variants/enums/registries, digest and reference projection changes, envelope and collection changes, operation/error changes, transform, defaults, rejected states, preserved unknowns, information loss, reversibility, validation, and test allocation. Structural similarity is not a compatibility result.

### 18.5 Deprecation and logical migration

`DeprecationRecord` contains target contract element, announced version/time, reason, supported replacement, last compatible version, removal precondition, consumer inventory, and migration allocation.

`LogicalMigrationPlanRecord` contains source and target contracts, affected record families, compatibility maps, transform identity, expected loss, historical-record treatment, validation, rollback representation, and later physical migration owner.

`LogicalMigrationResultRecord` is reserved for separately executed migration evidence. Database backfill, deployment, dual-write, cutover, rollback, transaction, and retention mechanics belong to `JAN-CSAA-009`.

---

## 19. Provider-adapter boundary and raw-to-normalized trace

### 19.1 Adapter Descriptor

`AdapterDescriptorRecord` contains:

- permanent adapter identity/version and implementation artifact reference;
- provider declaration reference;
- supported capability-profile and operation versions;
- input and output contract versions;
- provider-native configuration schema reference;
- mapping, transformation, validation, and normalization versions;
- subject/project/build/runtime constraints;
- raw-result availability and retention;
- deterministic/reproducibility behavior;
- partial/failure/cancellation/resource signals;
- security, filesystem, process, network, secret, and egress requirements;
- semantic-loss and known-blind-spot declarations;
- health/self-diagnostic operations;
- qualification reference slot.

The current documentation phase leaves `implementationArtifactRef` and `qualificationRef` explicitly not authored/not qualified.

### 19.2 Logical adapter operations

| Operation | Contract effect |
| --- | --- |
| `describe` | Return immutable provider/adapter declaration |
| `plan` | Validate requested profiles and materialize provider-native invocation inputs |
| `execute` | Produce invocation identity and raw result only under separate execution authority |
| `cancel` | Request cancellation and return actual acknowledgment state |
| `health` | Return one closed `HealthResponse` containing exact `ProviderHealthObservationRecord` references and separately typed requested operational or semantic observations |
| `map-query` | Map normalized query AST to native request with trace |
| `validate-raw` | Apply `V01`–`V06` as applicable |
| `normalize` | Produce candidate normalized records plus transformation/validation lineage |
| `explain-loss` | Return every dropped, approximated, defaulted, or unsupported meaning |

An implementation can combine operations internally, but evidence retains their logical boundaries.

Every model-using `execute` operation binds the exact `ModelExchangeRecord` through `ProviderInvocationRecord.modelExchangeBinding`. Raw request and response payloads remain referenced through raw artifact identities and `rawPayloadDigest`; a normalized record cannot erase model, prompt/template, tool, seed, sampling, response, validation, or redaction lineage.

### 19.3 Capability Binding and semantic-loss disclosure

`AdapterCapabilityBindingRecord` contains capability profile/version, provider method/version, supported perimeter, required inputs, output mappings, coverage basis, unsupported constructs, known false-positive/negative classes, invalidation behavior, and qualification reference.

`AdapterMappingRecord` contains normalized input/output contract elements, provider-native elements, direction, transformation, coercion, defaults, omissions, location mapping, raw severity/confidence treatment, deduplication behavior, and semantic loss.

Provider disagreement remains explicit. Adapters do not vote, average, choose a winner, or rewrite semantic ground. Provider-native severity, confidence, status, and identifiers remain raw metadata until independently mapped under an owning rule.

### 19.4 Qualification boundary

An adapter declaration is a claim. Concrete provider/adapter selection, security review, version/configuration acceptance, licensing, installation, qualification, substitution, removal, deployment, and operation belong to `JAN-CSAA-011` and separately authorized implementation.

Two providers or adapters with identical declared labels do not inherit one another's qualification. A result requiring qualification carries the exact qualification reference or remains non-eligible for that use.

---

## 20. Authorization, repository/worktree scope, redaction, confidentiality, retention, and audit

### 20.1 Authorization Context

`AuthorizationContextRecord` contains:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `principalRef` | Authenticated principal or service identity |
| `delegationChain` | Exact bounded delegation references |
| `grantRefs` | Applicable grants/policies and versions |
| `purpose` | Declared operation purpose |
| `allowedOperationIds` | Exact logical operations |
| `subjectScopes` | Repository/worktree/snapshot/evidence-set partitions |
| `dataClassScopes` | Permitted metadata, source, raw, finding, trace, or audit classes |
| `issuedAt` / `expiresAt` | Validity boundary |
| `decisionPolicyRef` | Exact policy or decision procedure to be applied; this context never points forward to its later decision |
| `constraints` | Resource, egress, redaction, retention, and presentation limits |

An absent, expired, ambiguous, or mismatched authorization context yields refusal rather than widened access.

### 20.2 Repository and worktree scope

`RepositoryWorktreeScopeRecord` contains repository ID, revision/snapshot, worktree/branch observation where applicable, included/excluded paths, project variants, security partition, applicable tenant, and observation cutoff.

Authorization is checked before traversal, aggregation, pagination, raw retrieval, or count computation. Cross-repository, worktree, branch, snapshot, evidence-set, principal, tenant, or fixture-run mixing is an identity and authorization failure unless an explicit comparison scope permits named subjects.

### 20.2.1 Information Control Binding

Every material record and raw artifact carries one `InformationControlBinding` or a content-bound reference to an inherited binding whose applicability is exact. The binding contains classification owner and policy/version; separate `confidentialityClassification`, `accessClassification`, and `retentionClassification`; compartments; record class (`source`, `raw-provider-result`, `trace`, `finding`, `query-result`, or another registered class); authorized principal, role, tenant, and purpose scopes; permitted operations and derivative uses; existence-disclosure policy; path/source/raw/trace/finding/audit disclosure rules; redaction policy; egress and presentation limits; retention reference; inheritance and derivation rule; and effective/expiry times. If the binding itself was created by a prior authorization decision, it may content-bind that decision; later access decisions bind the finalized information-control record and are found by reverse lookup.

Classification and authorization are evaluated at record grain. A package, graph, page, aggregate, explanation, diagnostic, or derived record computes the conservative composition of its members under the named composition rule; it cannot silently inherit the least restrictive member. Missing, conflicting, expired, or non-composable bindings cause refusal or an explicitly bounded redacted result.

### 20.2.2 Resolved paths and path refusal

`ResolvedPathRecord` uses `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` and contains repository/worktree-scope reference; caller-supplied logical path as a protected raw reference or safe digest; normalized repository-relative path; canonical resolved path represented relative to the authorized root; path kind; case-normalization policy; symlink/junction chain as authorized relative references; resolution method/version; access-decision reference; within-authorized-root result; existence-disclosure treatment; observation time; and invalidation dependencies. It never serializes an unrestricted absolute host path.

`PathResolutionRefusalRecord` uses `ControlEventEnvelope` and contains request/locator digest, scope and access-decision references, safe refusal code, rejected boundary class, and retryability. A later audit event content-binds the finalized refusal; the refusal never points forward to that audit event. Its exact refusal codes are `invalid-path`, `outside-authorized-root`, `symlink-or-junction-escape`, `scope-mismatch`, `existence-withheld`, `unavailable`, and `ambiguous-case`. It carries no resolved target, unauthorized prefix, existence confirmation, or protected host path.

Path authorization occurs after canonical resolution against an exact authorized root and before file metadata, content, traversal, aggregation, or existence is disclosed. `..`, alternate separators, case aliases, device paths, drive changes, UNC changes, symlink/junction hops, and provider-normalized aliases cannot escape the authorized root. A failure produces `PathResolutionRefusalRecord`; it never falls back to the caller text or widens scope.

### 20.3 Access Decision and Redaction Manifest

`AccessDecisionRecord` content-binds both the finalized Operation Request and its authorization context and contains principal, requested operation/data, subject scope, policy/grant versions, decision `allow`, `deny`, or `allow-with-redaction`, rationale code, decision time, and expiry. Request ID, operation/version, principal, subject/data scope, and authorization-context digest must equal the bound request values. A later audit event content-binds the finalized decision; reverse audit lookup is derived.

`RedactionManifestRecord` content-binds its source record/raw artifact and finalized redacted payload/result, and contains information-control binding, redaction policy/version, redacted fields/regions/classes, method, reason, actor/component, output `artifactContentDigest` or `recordDigest` as applicable, completeness consequence, count/shape/existence leakage treatment, and reversibility/retention state. Its output target cannot be the Operation Response that later embeds the manifest reference; finalization follows §7.2.

Redaction never substitutes a fabricated empty collection, zero count, complete flag, supported false, or healthy state. A withheld value uses an explicit `withheld-by-policy` state.

### 20.4 Secret and retention references

`SecretReferenceRecord` contains secret-system owner, opaque secret identifier/version, permitted purpose/scope, availability state, and rotation/expiry. Audit events content-bind the finalized secret reference where disclosure policy permits; the secret reference contains no audit forward pointer and no secret value.

`RetentionReferenceRecord` contains record/artifact class, controlling policy/version, retention period or event, legal/authority holds, redaction/deletion eligibility, raw/history requirements, expiry state, and later physical-operation allocation policy. A separately executed physical-operation record content-binds the retention reference; this record never points forward to an unperformed operation.

Retention policy never authorizes correction of semantic history. Physical deletion, cryptographic erasure, tombstoning, compaction, and archival are distinct later operational actions.

### 20.5 Audit Event

`AuditEventRecord` contains event identity/type, actor/principal/component, authorization context, exact subject, operation/run/invocation, input/output references, decision/action, start/end, result/health, resource use, redaction, failure/diagnostics, and content-bound prior correlation/causation references. Audit correlation and causation form an acyclic finalized-record graph; reverse navigation is derived.

Logical event types include request, acquisition, discovery, classification, plan, schedule, invocation, raw capture, validation, normalization, publication, refusal, invalidation, query, cancellation, timeout, failure, recovery, access, denial, redaction, retention, migration, repair, and administrative change.

Audit records expose safe metadata only to an authorized audience. They remain reconstructable without leaking protected source, raw data, secrets, paths, counts, graph shape, or existence across a denied boundary.

---

### 20.6 Operational health, no-current standing, and safe physical-action carriage

Appendix F defines a non-material `HealthObservationView` whose closed `binding` union is `committed-publication-vector`, `no-current-binding`, `binding-unavailable`, or `binding-corrupt`. Every non-content branch carries no traversable semantic-content reference. Bootstrap, restore, migration, recovery, corruption, and withdrawal standing are represented through source references, source-owned reasons where applicable, and H01–H14 rather than additional binding discriminators. `HealthResponse.operationalDimensions` carries H01–H14 as fourteen independent dimensions alongside the five preserved `HealthResponse` axes; neither the binding union nor the dimension set is an aggregate Boolean or an inferred gate result.

Operational payloads carry exact authorization, information-control, encryption-property, repair, residual-loss, backup/restore, migration/routing, retention/tombstone/GC, and audit references. They serialize evidence and state without selecting an algorithm, product, topology, retention limit, recovery objective, provider, or implementation.
## 21. Contract Package Manifest, generated-artifact trace, and source-to-contract reconciliation

### 21.1 Contract Package Manifest

`ContractPackageManifestRecord` uses `PackageEnvelope` and contains:

- package ID/version/lifecycle and `recordDigest`;
- exact `JAN-CSAA-007` document identity and `artifactContentDigest`;
- exact semantic-source identities and `artifactContentDigest` values;
- every designated schema-source identity, path, version, `contractContentDigest`, dependency, and state;
- every generated derivative identity, path, `artifactContentDigest`, source schema set, generator identity/version/`artifactContentDigest`, and fidelity state;
- the digest-profile, collection-semantics, finalization-direction, envelope-assignment, identity-projection, object-profile, object-variant, relationship-profile, relation-variant, auxiliary-logical-type, exact-enum/property, reference-target/predicate, canonical-key, bounded-substitution, entry-mechanism, ARP, RGT, scenario-facet, matrix, mutation, degradation, operation-policy, and typed-error registries defined by this candidate, including Appendix E;
- directional compatibility declarations;
- extension registry reference;
- canonicalization and digest-profile rules;
- validation stage and conformance-suite references;
- publication/effective state;
- content-bound predecessor relations; reverse supersession history is derived.

Current state values for every schema and derivative remain those in §6. No manifest instance exists in this documentation phase.

Package construction follows §7.2. The package identity/version is minted first. Each `ContractArtifactDescriptorRecord` and `GeneratedArtifactDescriptor` carries that scalar package identity/version or an identity-only parent reference and is finalized without a content-bound manifest-parent reference. A `SourceToContractTraceRecord` may then content-bind the finalized descriptors it allocates. The final `ContractPackageManifestRecord` content-binds canonically complete manifests of every descriptor and trace. Embedded registry definitions are manifest-owned values, not children that point back to their containing record. Reverse package membership is derived.

### 21.2 Contract Artifact Descriptor

`ContractArtifactDescriptorRecord` contains artifact ID, path, schema URN, contract family, version, `contractContentDigest` for schema contracts or `artifactContentDigest` for other files, status, semantic owners, dependencies, generated consumers, compatibility relations, validation evidence, and lifecycle.

Status is `candidate`, `designated-source`, `enforced-source`, `generated-derivative`, `superseded`, `withdrawn`, or `historical`. Only a separately authorized and validated artifact can use `designated-source` or `enforced-source`.

### 21.3 Source-to-Contract Trace

`SourceToContractTraceRecord` contains:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `traceId` | Permanent trace identity |
| `sourceRef` | Exact semantic or authority source |
| `sourceRequirementIds` | Individual source obligations |
| `sourceConcepts` | Exact owned meanings |
| `contractFamilyIds` | Candidate shape families |
| `schemaDefinitionIds` | Future exact definitions |
| `generatedTypeIds` | Future derivative types |
| `validationStageIds` | Required validation |
| `conformanceTestIds` | Later `JAN-CSAA-008` allocation |
| `semanticLossState` | Demonstrated none, bounded, unresolved, or prohibited |
| `reviewEvidence` | Author and independent review |
| `lifecycle` | Correction and content-bound predecessor trace; reverse successor trace is derived |

The initial horizontal trace is:

| `JAN-CSAA-002` ten object profiles, 127 objects | `JAN-CSAA-007-CF-COM`, `JAN-CSAA-007-CF-SEM` | Closed variant, common facets, owner, epistemic and lifecycle |

### 21.4 Generation fidelity

The future generation process produces a `GeneratedArtifactDescriptor` for each derivative. Fidelity evidence covers:

- exact schema source set and `contractContentDigest` values;
- generator implementation `artifactContentDigest`, content-bound configuration, and version;
- deterministic invocation;
- output `artifactContentDigest` and exports;
- one-to-one contract definition/type/validator coverage;
- discriminator and enum parity;
- required/optional/null/unknown-field parity;
- digest-profile and purpose-specific digest parity;
- identity-only/content-bound reference kind and direction parity;
- envelope-assignment and collection-semantics registry parity;
- recursive-reference registry, expression-budget, and union parity;
- operation-policy, request/response union, state/outcome, and typed-error registry parity;
- source-location and numeric-bound parity;
- no handwritten semantic defaults;
- reproducible regeneration.

Any manual output change, missing definition, widened/narrowed validation, enum loss, optionality drift, or unknown-field mismatch makes the derivative unverified.

## 23. Material decisions, open alternatives, and conservative defaults

### 23.1 Candidate decisions made by this Draft

| Decision | Candidate resolution | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Schema source language | JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 | Provider-neutral closed structural validation and composable definitions |
| Wire representation | UTF-8 JSON | Portable logical interchange without transport selection |
| Schema identity | Versioned `urn:janumi:csaa:schema:*` | Stable identity without hosting/topology assumption |
| Version granularity | Individual contract versions plus package manifest version | Compatibility is not uniform across every family |
| Identifier model | Type-prefixed opaque ID plus purpose-specific identity projections and `DigestDescriptor` values | Identity is not forced to equal content or path |
| Common envelopes | One closed Identity base plus exactly one Definition, Subject Occurrence, Scoped Observation, Control Event, or Package assignment for every material definition | Preserves applicable horizontal facets without fabricating a universal subject |
| Unknown fields | Closed core plus explicit namespaced `extensions` | Prevents silent meaning drift while permitting bounded forwarding |
| Source locations | Four-way discriminated union with half-open ranges | Preserves tool coordinate systems explicitly |
| Query form | Typed provider-neutral AST | Native query strings cannot own semantic meaning |
| Rule Application Result | Immutable addressable top-level record; embedded projection by exact ref only | Supports findings that content-bind the result, derived reverse lookup, history, and reuse without a cycle |
| Epistemic carriers | Six-dimensional common product and separate five-dimensional rule product | Prevents lossy universal status |
| Pagination | Opaque subject/query/auth/order-bound cursor | Prevents cursor reuse across incompatible contexts |
| Default order | `DefaultQueryResultOrderCanonicalKey` (`JAN-CSAA-007-ECK-025`): `kind`, `recordId`, and all five `DigestDescriptorCanonicalKey` components of `recordDigest` | Complete deterministic tie-break without semantic rank |
| Raw provider output | Immutable typed reference with availability/redaction/retention | Normalization cannot erase raw lineage |
| Operation model | Operation-keyed request/result unions plus state/outcome invariant | Does not select orchestrator or transport |
| Logical migration | Contract maps/results separated from 009 physical migration | Shape compatibility does not choose rollout mechanics |
| RGT/RGP | Templates encode unresolved designation inputs; RGP variant requires designation | Prevents template promotion by serialization |
| Oracle lifecycle | Independent proposal/conferral/execution axes | Proposed or executed does not mean conferred |
| Record digest | Registered RFC 8785 JCS profile omitting only top-level `recordDigest` | Reproducible non-circular record content identity |

Every resolution is a Draft hypothesis until the exact member and later artifacts receive their own applicable lifecycle treatment.

### 23.2 Open alternatives

| Open surface | Options | Conservative default and later owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Final repository package path | `packages/csaa-contracts`; another controlled package | Treat §6 path as candidate; reconcile after final implementation refresh |
| Extension registry authority | Corpus registry; repository reference artifact; external owner | Unregistered extensions carry no core meaning |
| Authenticity/signing | Registered digest descriptors only; signatures; transparency log | Digest integrity only; no authenticity claim until separately designed |
| Numeric resource/page limits | Fixed package defaults; operation/profile/provider limits | No invented number; require exact caller/profile/provider budget and refuse unsafe unbounded work |
| Decimal unit registry | Corpus-owned; standards-owned; contract-local | Require registered unit reference; do not coerce unknown units |
| External-reference caching | Embedded copy; content-addressed cache; online resolution | Preserve exact reference/version/`DigestDescriptor` and actual availability |
| Native query escape hatch | Prohibit; raw provider extension | Raw provider extension only, never normalized semantic authority |
| Transport binding | Library; CLI; IPC; language server; HTTP/service | None selected |
| Signature of generated artifacts | Package manifest; build attestation; both | Require fidelity evidence; exact mechanism later |
| Large result transfer | Pages; stream; immutable result bundle | Logical page/partial contracts only; transport later |
| Operation persistence | Ephemeral; durable job; hybrid | State meaning only; `JAN-CSAA-009` owns physical behavior |
| Contract archive retention | Repository history; artifact registry; both | Preserve exact historical resolvability; physical policy later |

None blocks documentation-only authoring. A fork blocks artifact enforcement when its unresolved choice affects exact bytes, validation, security, compatibility, or reproducibility.

## 24. Normative requirement catalog

Requirement identifiers are permanent within `JAN-CSAA-007`. Retirement creates a successor treatment and never reuses an identifier. Each requirement is independently ledgered and verified.

| `CSAA-007-QRY-004` | Cross-snapshot semantics SHALL use independent subject bindings plus a separate comparison relationship. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-005` | The normalized query language SHALL be a closed typed AST rather than an authoritative provider-native string. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-006` | Native query mapping SHALL retain native input, normalized AST, transformation, validation, and semantic-loss evidence. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-007` | Predicate truth SHALL preserve `supported-true`, `supported-false`, `unknown`, and `conflicting`. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-008` | Predicate truth SHALL NOT replace the six-dimensional epistemic state. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-009` | Supported false SHALL require a declared closed and adequately covered basis. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-010` | Counts and aggregations SHALL expose numerator, denominator, excluded/unknown regions, grouping, and exact/lower-bound state. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-011` | Joins SHALL preserve dimension-specific composition and disclose dropped keys or regions. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-012` | Timeout, cancellation, truncation, page cutoff, traversal bound, or budget exhaustion SHALL NOT produce a population-wide absence claim. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-013` | A Query Result SHALL retain exact query, run, subject, capabilities, providers, population, matches/non-matches, truth, epistemic state, bounds, explanation, provenance, times, and invalidation. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-014` | An empty match collection SHALL carry enough coverage and epistemic state to distinguish supported absence from inability to determine. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-015` | A cursor SHALL bind query, parameters, subject, authorization/redaction context, order, and publication identity. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-016` | Cursor mismatch or expiry SHALL produce a typed lifecycle error rather than continuation against another context. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-017` | A material query result SHALL use a complete deterministic order key; only a nonmaterial, nonpaginated presentation may declare an unordered state. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-018` | Ranking SHALL NOT imply severity, importance, causal responsibility, permission, or authority. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-019` | A Slice Result SHALL retain included members, witnesses, unresolved frontier, unsupported seams, exclusions, conflicts, truncation, and coverage. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-020` | Runtime evidence SHALL NOT silently prune unobserved static slice possibilities. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-021` | Exclusion from a slice SHALL NOT be represented as proof of irrelevance, non-impact, dead code, or safe removal. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-022` | A Semantic Comparison SHALL bind exact before/after subjects and explicit compatibility decisions for every material basis. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-023` | Incompatible or ambiguous comparison regions SHALL remain incomparable or ambiguous rather than forced into a delta. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-024` | Every Impact Candidate SHALL retain a typed witness path or an explicit unresolved frontier. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-025` | The impact contract SHALL NOT encode zero static callers as dead-code truth, safe-removal permission, a finding, or a gate result. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-026` | Graph Delta SHALL bind exact before/after graph references, typed entry kinds, before/after member references, lineage state, evidence, confidence, compatibility, and inverse behavior. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-027` | Change Seed SHALL bind the exact change set, changed artifacts and ranges, changed semantic identities, unresolved mappings, derivation method, coverage, and epistemic state. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-028` | Change Impact Result SHALL bind the exact seed, query and plan, impact candidates, witness paths, reachability surface, unresolved frontier, exclusions, conflicts, coverage, partiality, provenance, and epistemic state. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-029` | Every recursive `QueryExpression` root SHALL carry positive safe-integer `maxNodes`, `maxDepth`, and `maxFanout` bounds. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-030` | Query-expression validation SHALL reject budget excess without truncating or widening the expression. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-031` | `GraphDeltaRecord` SHALL bind exact before/after graphs, comparison/run, compatibility set, coverage basis, and canonical delta entries. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-032` | Every graph-delta entry SHALL declare exact inverse behavior without creating a content-bound inverse cycle. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-033` | `ChangeSeedRecord` SHALL use the closed seven-variant seed registry with exact change-set, range, semantic-identity, mapping, derivation, coverage, and epistemic fields. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-034` | `ReachabilitySurfaceDefinitionRecord` SHALL bind every registered applicable entry mechanism, entry population, closure rule, capability, and invalidation dependency. |
| `CSAA-007-QRY-035` | A negative reachability conclusion SHALL remain inconclusive unless every applicable entry population is closed, current, compatible, completely analyzed, and successfully resolved without a positive entry. |

| `CSAA-007-EXE-015` | Captured runtime evidence SHALL NOT be represented as exhaustive runtime possibility. |

| `CSAA-007-RUL-011` | Review, remediation, freshness, exception, and suppression treatment axes SHALL remain independent. |

| `CSAA-007-RUL-013` | A provider, producer, or affected change author SHALL NOT self-dispose a finding solely by declaration. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-014` | A remediation claim SHALL bind exact successor change and subject where a change was performed. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-015` | Resolution by reanalysis SHALL require a current compatible successful successor result and explicit predecessor links. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-016` | Suppression SHALL affect presentation or configuration only. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-017` | An Engineering Exception SHALL bind exact target, transition, subject, authority, residual risk, effect boundary, expiry, controls, and history. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-018` | An exception SHALL NOT alter the underlying result, finding, evidence, freshness, or canonical assurance state. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-019` | Repository Gate Template SHALL carry inert lifecycle and unresolved designation fields exactly. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-020` | A Repository Gate Template reference SHALL be rejected wherever a Repository Gate Profile reference is required. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-021` | A Repository Gate Profile variant SHALL require a recognized designation record and every designation-controlled field. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-022` | Repository Gate Evaluation SHALL be invalid without an exact designated Repository Gate Profile. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-023` | Gate aggregate results SHALL preserve the five exact meanings and owning predicate derivation. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-024` | `permitted-with-effective-exception` SHALL remain visibly qualified and retain every underlying violation or deficiency. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-025` | A CSAA technical record SHALL NOT impersonate a canonical assurance record or confer canonical authority. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-026` | Suppression SHALL NOT create satisfaction, exception, or permission. |
| `CSAA-007-RUL-027` | Assurance Mapping Record SHALL bind technical source records, mapping method and version, independently evaluated admissibility result, external canonical assurance reference when one exists, limitations, provenance, and lifecycle without conferring authority. |

| `CSAA-007-ORC-018` | Logical fixture/oracle records SHALL NOT claim that physical fixtures, conferred judgments, or executed results exist. |
| `CSAA-007-ORC-019` | A dated-JPWB fixture SHALL NOT float to a later repository state. |
| `CSAA-007-ORC-020` | Optional example, vendor, or hostile-repository expansion SHALL NOT be represented as authored until separately created and reviewed. |

| `CSAA-007-API-017` | Operation inputs and outputs SHALL expose contract compatibility and exact subject binding. |
| `CSAA-007-API-018` | No logical operation SHALL mutate source, configuration, tests, fixtures, or oracle state as an implicit analysis side effect. |
| `CSAA-007-API-019` | `OperationRequestBase.subjectInput` SHALL use the closed resolved-subject, subject-locator, scoped-target, target-record, live-target, or not-applicable union. |
| `CSAA-007-API-020` | Every operation SHALL enforce its exact registered subject-input and operation-input variants. |
| `CSAA-007-API-021` | Subject resolution SHALL return the closed resolved, not-found, ambiguous, forbidden, unavailable, or incompatible outcome union. |
| `CSAA-007-API-022` | Failed or denied subject resolution SHALL NOT invent, widen, or silently substitute a subject. |
| `CSAA-007-API-023` | `OperationResponse` SHALL use the closed progress, success, partial, or error outcome union with operation-keyed result variants. |
| `CSAA-007-API-024` | Every operation-response state SHALL satisfy its exact outcome-discriminator invariant. |

### 24.16 Contract versioning, compatibility, unknown fields, deprecation, and migration

| ID | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-001` | Document, package, schema, semantic-owner, generated-derivative, adapter, payload, and physical-storage versions SHALL remain distinguishable. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-002` | Compatibility SHALL identify exact producer, consumer, direction, versions, and scope. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-003` | Same-major versions SHALL NOT be presumed compatible without an explicit package-manifest declaration. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-004` | Adding a required field SHALL be classified as a major contract change. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-005` | Removing or renaming a field, variant, or operation SHALL be classified as a major contract change. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-006` | Adding a value to a closed enum SHALL be classified as a major contract change. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-007` | Changing discriminator, identifier grammar, digest profile/projection, reference direction, envelope assignment, collection semantic, recursive budget, operation policy, error registry, null, or unknown-field behavior SHALL be classified as a major contract change. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-008` | An optional-field or independent-variant addition MAY be minor only when explicit consumer analysis demonstrates compatibility. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-009` | A semantic-owner meaning change SHALL trigger affected contract versioning and compatibility analysis. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-010` | Strict ingress SHALL reject unknown core fields. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-011` | Forwarding components SHALL preserve bounded unrecognized namespaced extensions without interpreting them. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-012` | A Compatibility Claim SHALL bind source/target contracts, direction, scope, assumptions, compared surface, result, loss, evidence, review, time, and invalidation. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-013` | Structural similarity SHALL NOT be represented as semantic compatibility. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-014` | A Compatibility Map SHALL expose every field, variant, enum, registry, digest, reference, envelope, collection, operation, error, transform, default, rejection, preserved unknown, loss, and reversibility mapping. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-015` | Deprecation SHALL identify target, reason, replacement, last compatible version, removal precondition, consumer inventory, and migration allocation. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-016` | Logical migration SHALL bind exact source/target contracts, compatibility maps, transform, loss, historical treatment, validation, and rollback representation. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-017` | Logical migration SHALL NOT prescribe database backfill, deployment, dual-write, transaction, cutover, or retention mechanics. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-018` | An incompatible or unknown contract negotiation SHALL fail explicitly rather than select a convenient version silently. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-019` | The operational record, identity, preimage, health, and typed-error additions SHALL be classified as the MAJOR successor `JAN-CSAA-007@1.0.0`. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-020` | Directional compatibility from `0.1.0` to `1.0.0` SHALL remain incompatible or unknown unless an exact map proves every required operational distinction. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-021` | Logical contract migration SHALL remain distinct from the physical migration evidence represented by operational records. |
| `CSAA-007-CMP-022` | A `0.1.0` consumer SHALL NOT decode, discard, or coerce a `1.0.0` operational record without an exact compatible consumer declaration. |

### 24.18 Authorization, scope, redaction, confidentiality, retention, and audit

| ID | Requirement |
| --- | --- |

### 24.25 Publication, read-view, and current-binding closure

| ID | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-001` | Publication candidate lifecycle, sealed candidate content, and authoritative publication decision SHALL use three distinct record contracts. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-002` | Pre-seal lifecycle revisions SHALL carry `candidateLifecycleId` while excluding `publicationCandidateId`. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-003` | `PublicationCandidateRecord` SHALL be the sole predecision publication-content carrier, include exact finalized V01–V06 results and the reproducible static legacy-Manifest projection digest, and exclude V07, lifecycle, legacy Manifest, decision, current-binding, response, audit-completion, health-completion, and output-complete replay dependencies. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-004` | A new immutable SEALED lifecycle revision SHALL bind the candidate alone; only a later postdecision successor may bind the finalized decision and legacy Manifest without rewriting any prior revision. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-005` | `publicationCommitId` SHALL be absent from intent, COMMITTING, and unresolved-commit states, with minting permitted only for a finalized authoritative decision. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-006` | Physical current binding SHALL remain separate from immutable Publication Decision history; use the exact `(securityPartitionId, publicationChannelId)` key and complete generation/decision/candidate/completed-Manifest-projection-digest value; and advance that key/value only under an exact typed predecessor/current-binding observation, expected generation, active claim right, byte-equal fence/revision/cutoff P12 projection, and authoritative linearization evidence. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-007` | P07 SHALL exclude a candidate lane's own future decision and generation while binding a committed read lane to the exact postdecision decision/Manifest pair whose static and complete semantic projections reproduce the candidate and decision digests, plus security partition, channel, generation, evidence revision, static snapshot, and cutoff. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-008` | A read acquisition SHALL always have `readViewLifecycleId`, with `readViewId` or `rawMaterialReadViewId` present only after ACQUIRED. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-009` | Content and raw-material read views SHALL remain distinct without merging their vectors, acquisition predicates, authorization, or effects. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-010` | A read acquisition and continuation SHALL remain pinned to one vector proven current-or-explicitly-historical and admissible as a whole at one common cutoff, with the current branch materially comparing every complete partition/channel/generation/decision/candidate/completed-digest binding tuple and both branches retaining exact compatibility pairs, authorization, policy, and expiry. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-011` | The publication finalization DAG SHALL follow the exact nine-step candidate-to-decision-to-legacy-Manifest-to-lifecycle/read order in Appendix F. |
| `CSAA-007-PUB-012` | Premature, backfilled, rebound, self-inclusive, future-dependent, or cyclic publication/replay identity construction SHALL be rejected as a typed non-green outcome. |

## 26. Draft acceptance state

This Draft is structurally eligible for author-side closure only when:

1. every applicable inherited obligation is extracted and bidirectionally traced;
2. all 637 local atomic requirements are uniquely ledgered;
3. every designated family, source, derivative, status, dependency, digest, reference, envelope, collection, operation, error, and other closed registry is accounted for;
4. all 127 object and 137 relationship variants are present exactly once with unique discriminators and exact field definitions;
5. all 14 cross-graph invariants map to validation and later conformance;
6. all 32 capability profiles map to exactly 28 ordered facets without punctuation parsing;
7. query, slice, comparison, impact, reachability, incremental equivalence, execution evidence, model exchange, legacy and H01–H14 health, rule/finding/gate, fixture/oracle, operation, 31 operational roles, 37-row/40-name identities, publication/read vectors, error, compatibility, adapter, information-control, and path-safety shapes preserve source meaning;
8. no current repository, enforced-artifact, executable-test, oracle-conferral, provider-qualification, gate-effect, implementation, or authority claim is made;
9. every author-side method other than post-ledger self-review has exact reproducible evidence and the ledger closes;
10. post-ledger author self-review completes and every blocking finding is resolved before Proposed freeze.

This stable document does not declare those conditions satisfied. The exact requirement ledger, objective verification record, author self-review, promotion record, independent review, and integrity record control their respective lifecycle conclusions.

The future package is not executable-ready merely because this documentation is complete. Enforced schemas, generated derivatives, independently governed oracle judgments, red-first conformance, provider qualification, security evidence, and operations evidence remain separate prerequisites.

## 27. Closing contract rule

A machine contract is trustworthy only when it preserves the exact semantic owner, subject, provenance, epistemic dimensions, lifecycle, validation, compatibility, information controls, and failure boundary of the record it carries.

No serialized value is authority merely because it validates. No generated type is a second source. No provider payload is a fact before validation. No empty result is knowledge without a closed healthy basis. No template is a gate profile. No proposed judgment is an oracle. No successful operation is assurance.

## Appendix B — Exact semantic-relation variant registry

This appendix is a mechanical, source-faithful projection of all 137 rows in `JAN-CSAA-002@0.3.0` §15. `REL-nnn` is the permanent relation discriminator; the relationship-kind text is its stable readable name. Every future variant is closed and inherits the common envelope plus its relationship profile.

| Relation ID | Relationship kind | Family | Profile | Contract definition | Typed endpoints and required supplement | Specific limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `REL-001` | `revision-parent` | Revision | `R-STR` | `SemanticRelation.REL-001` | child Repository Revision → parent Repository Revision; parent ordinal/role | Both revisions are immutable |
| `REL-002` | `ref-target` | Revision | `R-STR` | `SemanticRelation.REL-002` | Ref → Repository Revision; observation time | Moving observation |
| `REL-003` | `branch-head` | Revision | `R-STR` | `SemanticRelation.REL-003` | Branch → Repository Revision; observation time | Moving observation |

| `REL-005` | `candidate-merge-input` | Revision | `R-STR` | `SemanticRelation.REL-005` | Candidate Merge → input revision/change set; input role | No implicit input |
| `REL-006` | `candidate-merge-result` | Revision | `R-STR` | `SemanticRelation.REL-006` | Candidate Merge → synthetic Repository Snapshot | Synthetic is explicit |

Appendices A and B are source-faithful projections that preserve every source row without interpreting punctuation as structure. Appendices C and D are the exact normative candidate shape-definition registries for those projected rows. A source-catalog or shape-definition change requires regeneration, affected trace review, a contract-version decision, and rerun of the object/relation/invariant verification methods.

## Appendix C — Exact semantic-object shape-definition registry

This appendix is a normative serialization decision of `JAN-CSAA-007`; it does not reinterpret semantic ownership held by `JAN-CSAA-002`. Appendix A remains the source-faithful catalog projection. This appendix binds every Appendix A discriminator to one schema-only profile facet map, one exact envelope assignment, and one closed set of variant-specific payload fields. A generated schema rejects undeclared variant fields and does not introduce an `attributes`, `properties`, `metadata`, `data`, `details`, or other generic property bag.

### C.1 Field-descriptor mini-grammar

Each object-variant field descriptor has the exact form:

`<json-pointer> : <TypeRef> : <Cardinality> : <CollectionSemantics> : <IdentityParticipation> : <InvalidationRole>`

| Token position | Closed values and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `json-pointer` | An RFC 6901 pointer rooted only at `/payload`. The profile scalar remains the top-level `profile` discriminator from §10.2; a descriptor never creates a child below `/profile`. Common-envelope fields are constrained through the schema-facet mapping in §C.2 and are not repeated in `/payload`. |
| `TypeRef` | A §7 type; a PascalCase local `$defs` key; `ObjRef<discriminator>`; `ObjIdentityRef<discriminator>`; the corresponding `*Choice` forms; `EnumRef<registry-id>`; `ManifestRef<registry-id>`; or `BindingRef<registry-id>`. `ObjRef` and `ObjRefChoice` constrain `ContentBoundRecordRef`; `ObjIdentityRef` and `ObjIdentityRefChoice` constrain `RecordIdentityRef`. |
| `Cardinality` | Exactly `1`, `0..1`, `0..*`, or `n..*`, where `n` is a positive safe-integer minimum. Null never satisfies a cardinality. |
| `CollectionSemantics` | `SCALAR`, `ORDERED(key=<registered-key>)`, or `SET_CANONICAL(key=<registered-key>)`. A collection cites the exact §7.2 reference key, `SourceLocationCanonicalKey`, or another registry row below. |
| `IdentityParticipation` | `ID` places the normalized field in the variant identity projection. `NON_ID` excludes it. Every `ID` field has cardinality `1` or `n..*`; a field with cardinality `0..1` or `0..*` is always `NON_ID`. A possibly empty identity-bearing collection is represented by a required `ManifestRef`, and branch-dependent identity is represented by a required `BindingRef`. |
| `InvalidationRole` | `SELF`, `DEPENDENCY`, `PROVENANCE`, `OBSERVATION`, or `NONE`, with the meanings fixed by §10.2 and the concern-owning source. |

Descriptor order is normative. `ORDERED` and `SET_CANONICAL` are material §7.10 semantics. A collection key is an executable registered projection. When an order component such as `role`, `ordinal`, `family`, or `stageOrdinal` is not native to the referenced value, the array entry is a closed wrapper containing those components and `value`; generators do not synthesize such values after acceptance.

A source trace identifies the semantic source row and candidate discriminator row. The Limit column is represented by the exact `invariantIds` assignment in §C.3 or by a closed local constraint. An absent enum, binding, manifest, local `$defs`, key, or constraint row is a package-integrity failure.

#### C.1.1 Exact local scalar and key registry

| Local type or key | Exact closed meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ExternalVersion` | `NonEmptyString` carrying the producer's exact version token. It is SemVer only when the producer's identified version scheme says so; otherwise it is opaque and has no inferred ordering. |
| `ProviderNativeId` | `NonEmptyString` issued by a named provider, VCS, compiler, checker, runner, or collector. It never satisfies `OpaqueId` unless Janumi independently issues the record ID. |
| `PermanentId` | `NonEmptyString` interpreted only under the exact identified owner and identifier scheme; it does not confer authority. |
| `MediaType` | Lowercase type/subtype with registered or explicitly vendor-qualified parameters normalized by the schema package. |
| `JsonPointer` | RFC 6901 JSON Pointer string. |
| `Limitation` | `NonEmptyString` whose NFC-normalized text is the complete bounded limitation assertion; no untyped object or supplemental property bag is permitted. |
| `FreshnessState` | Closed string enum `current-for-subject`, `stale`, `invalidated`, or `unknown`, exactly matching §7.7. |
| `DocumentMemberIdentityRef` | Closed `{ documentId: PermanentId, version: ContractVersion, status: NonEmptyString, contentDigest: DigestDescriptor }`. |
| `SourceLocationCanonicalKey` | The exact §7.3 named discriminated-union projection. |
| `RecordIdentityRefCanonicalKey` | The exact §7.2 named projection. |
| `ContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey` | The exact §7.2 named projection. |
| `ContractRefCanonicalKey` | The exact §7.2 named projection. |
| `ExternalRefCanonicalKey` | The exact §7.2 named projection. |
| `RawArtifactRefCanonicalKey` | The exact §7.2 named projection. |
| `AuthorityRefCanonicalKey` | The exact §7.2 named projection. |
| `LimitationCanonicalKey` | NFC limitation text ordered by its JCS UTF-8 bytes, exactly as §7.10 fixes. |
| `EvidenceMember` | Closed `{ role: NonEmptyString, ordinal: Count, recordRef: ContentBoundRecordRef }`; canonical order begins with `ordinal`, then `role`, then `ContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey`. |
| `GraphEdgeEndpoint` | Closed `{ role: NonEmptyString, ordinal: Count, nodeRef: ObjRef<graph-node> }`; the node reference is content-bound and endpoint order is `(role, ordinal)`. |

All record-contract version fields use `ContractVersion`. Tool, framework, provider, compiler, runner, collector, VCS, component, and derivation versions use `ExternalVersion` unless their exact identified owner supplies a contract-version scheme.

#### C.1.3 Required closed-binding registry

`BindingRef<x>` is a required closed discriminated union. Only the listed branches and members are accepted.

| Binding ID | Exact branches |

Every `contentManifestRef` is a `RawArtifactRef` constrained to the registered repository-content-manifest media type and exact `JAN-CSAA-007-EAT-C-004` decoded shape. Its `/entries` is `SET_CANONICAL` over `JAN-CSAA-007-EAT-C-003` by `RepositoryContentManifestEntryCanonicalKey` (`JAN-CSAA-007-ECK-023`). Each entry contains exactly normalized repository path, source-bearing artifact-class hint, byte availability, and raw-byte `artifactContentDigest`; duplicate paths are invalid. It contains no Repository Snapshot, Artifact Descriptor, Subject Occurrence, or other record reference and finalizes before the snapshot under FDR-006 / `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D009`. |
