#### C.1.4 Non-core `$defs` and enum closure

Every PascalCase type and every `EnumRef` used by §C.4 resolves to a closed `$defs` or closed enum row in the same frozen Contract Package. The direct aliases corrected here are authoritative: `NonEmptyString`, `RepositoryPath`, `Count`, `DurationMs`, `ContractVersion`, `ExternalVersion`, and `ProviderNativeId`. Appendix E is the normative closure registry for the auxiliary logical types, exact enum/property sets, reference targets and predicates, canonical-key projections, and bounded substitutions consumed by Appendix C. A residual unresolved local type, enum, reference target, predicate, or key prevents Appendix C package closure; it is never widened to `JsonValue`.

### C.2 ObjectProfileShapeBinding registry

A profile binding is a schema fragment, not serialized instance data. The top-level `/profile` value remains one scalar. Each profile fragment narrows fields already owned by the assigned common envelope and constrains how §C.4 payload fields participate in identity; it creates no child member beneath `/profile` and does not duplicate an envelope value under `/payload`.

#### C.2.1 Complete source-facet mapping

| JAN-CSAA-002 profile facet | Authoritative JAN-CSAA-007 location |
| --- | --- |
| `identity` | §C.4 `ID` descriptors plus the registered digest projection; derived digest fields remain `NON_ID` |
| `subjectBinding` | `/subject` for `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope`, `/scope` for `ScopedObservationEnvelope`, or `/applicabilityPolicy` for `DefinitionEnvelope`, exactly as assigned in §C.3 |
| `revisionBinding` | repository/static/execution coordinates within the authoritative `/subject`, `/scope`, or `/applicabilityPolicy`; never a parallel payload subject |
| `provenance` | `/provenance`, `/definitionProvenance`, or the envelope-specific source/evidence surface |
| `owner` | top-level `/ownerRef`; a `DefinitionEnvelope` additionally constrains `/semanticOwnerRefs` to include it |
| `lifecycle` | `/lifecycle` |
| `versioningAndInvalidation` | `/invalidationDependencies` plus `/lifecycle/predecessorRelations` |
| `requiredMetadata` | required §C.4 `/payload` descriptors only |
| `optionalMetadata` | optional §C.4 `/payload` descriptors only; all are `NON_ID` |
| `authorityAndEpistemicLimits` | `/epistemic`, `/informationControls`, `/limitations`, and applicable provenance authority references |
| `supportedTreatment` | `/epistemic/capabilityCoverage`, `/epistemic/supportBasis`, and `/epistemic/inference` |
| `inferredTreatment` | `/epistemic/supportBasis`, `/epistemic/inference`, and `/epistemic/rationale` |
| `unknownTreatment` | the applicable explicit unknown values plus `/epistemic/unresolvedRegionRefs` |
| `conflictingTreatment` | `/epistemic/conflict`, `/epistemic/conflictingRecordRefs`, and `/epistemic/rationale` |
| `serializationOwner` | top-level `/serializationOwnerRef` and, for `DefinitionEnvelope`, its same-valued specialization |
| `crossGraphInvariants` | top-level `/invariantIds` fixed by §C.3 |

For `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope`, `/provenance/invocationRefs`, `/provenance/rawArtifactRefs`, `/provenance/validationResultRefs`, `/provenance/transformationRefs`, `/provenance/authorityRefs`, and `/provenance/sourceLocations` use `SET_CANONICAL` with the applicable exact §7.2 key or `SourceLocationCanonicalKey`. `/provenance/inputRefs` remains `ORDERED(key=role,ordinal,ContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey)`. An analysis or execution profile narrows those paths but does not replace them with payload duplicates.

### C.3 Exact envelope, owner, serialization-owner, invariant, and relation-projection assignments

The assignments below are part of Appendix C and do not depend on a future Package Manifest for their meaning. A Package Manifest repeats and verifies them without changing them.

#### C.3.1 Envelope assignment

The following three sets are disjoint and contain exactly `OBJ-001` through `OBJ-127` once:

| Envelope | Exact object rows | Exact subject or scope policy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ScopedObservationEnvelope` | `OBJ-001`–`OBJ-011`, `OBJ-018` | OBJ-001–OBJ-004 use immutable repository/VCS coordinate scope; OBJ-005–OBJ-006, OBJ-009, and OBJ-011 use repository observation scope with cutoff; OBJ-007–OBJ-008 use exact comparison/construction scope; OBJ-010 uses the construction policy in §C.3.2; OBJ-018 uses exact external-advisory scope. No row in this set fabricates a `SubjectBinding`. |
| `DefinitionEnvelope` | `OBJ-033`–`OBJ-036`, `OBJ-038`, `OBJ-084`, `OBJ-086`–`OBJ-089`, `OBJ-097`–`OBJ-098`, `OBJ-101`, `OBJ-103`, `OBJ-110`–`OBJ-111`, `OBJ-121` | `/applicabilityPolicy` binds exact repository/static/execution scope where relevant; `/definitionProvenance` owns producer, method, source, and observation facts. Test and selection rows in this set are definitions, not run evidence. |
| `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` | `OBJ-012`–`OBJ-017`, `OBJ-019`–`OBJ-032`, `OBJ-037`, `OBJ-039`–`OBJ-083`, `OBJ-085`, `OBJ-090`–`OBJ-096`, `OBJ-099`–`OBJ-100`, `OBJ-102`, `OBJ-104`–`OBJ-109`, `OBJ-112`–`OBJ-120`, `OBJ-122`–`OBJ-127` | `/subject/repositorySnapshotRef` is present. Static semantic facts also carry `/subject/staticSemanticSnapshotRef`; dynamic evidence uses the non-self-containing member policy below until the later Execution Evidence Set is finalized. Comparison records name every subject in `/subject/comparisonSubjectRefs`. |
| `ControlEventEnvelope` | none | No Appendix A object row is a governed action or technical effect. |
| `PackageEnvelope` | none | No Appendix A object row is the package/schema descriptor itself; reference objects do not acquire package-envelope authority. |

OBJ-039, OBJ-091–OBJ-096, OBJ-102, OBJ-104–OBJ-107, OBJ-112–OBJ-120, and any other record that can become a member of a later Execution Evidence Set carry the repository and Static Semantic Snapshot portions of `/subject` but omit the self-containing `/subject/executionEvidenceSetRef`. The later OBJ-126 set content-binds each finalized member. Run, attempt, collector observation, trace, span, event, fact, and graph records therefore remain subject occurrences without forming an evidence-set cycle.

OBJ-121 carries its local query-subject perimeter only in its `DefinitionEnvelope.applicabilityPolicy`; OBJ-124 carries the exact referenced finding subject only in its `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope.subject`. Neither variant serializes a parallel `SubjectBinding` in `/payload`.

#### C.3.2 Non-self-referential Repository Snapshot policy

OBJ-010 is finalized under `ScopedObservationEnvelope`. Its `/scope` is a closed `RepositorySnapshotConstructionScope` containing the repository reference, required `RepositorySnapshotConstructionBinding`, included perimeter, context manifest, and observation cutoff. It does not contain a `repositorySnapshotRef` and cannot refer to the record being constructed. The following are non-serialized schema aliases only: `/payload/repositoryRef` → `/scope/parameters/repositoryRef`; `/payload/construction` → `/scope/parameters/construction`; `/payload/includedPerimeterRef` → `/scope/parameters/perimeterRef`; and `/payload/contextManifestRefs` → `/scope/parameters/contextManifestRefs`. No alias is a JSON member, and the four `/scope/parameters/*` paths are the sole authoritative serialized construction inputs. After OBJ-010 is finalized, later `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` records bind it through `/subject/repositorySnapshotRef`. This is the sole bootstrap exception and does not weaken §7.5 for subject occurrences.

### C.5 Closure rules

1. The `ObjectVariantDefinition` registry contains one and only one row for every Appendix A ordinal 1 through 127, and the discriminator and `Definition ID` are immutable package keys.
2. A variant schema is the closed intersection of the common envelope, exactly one `ObjectProfileShapeBinding`, the exact §C.3 assignment, and exactly one row from §C.4. No row authorizes a generic extension point.
3. Every `ObjRef`, `ContentBoundRecordRef`, `ContractRef`, `ExternalRef`, and `RawArtifactRef` dependency participates in the §7.2 acyclic content-bound dependency rule. Where a parent record needs forward navigation to a child that binds back to it, the parent uses `ObjIdentityRef`; the reverse content-bound navigation is derived.
4. Branch-dependent state uses the required closed bindings in §C.1.3. `RepositorySnapshotConstructionBinding`, `augmentation-target`, `runtime-dependency-target`, `test-target-context`, `analysis-subject`, `diagnostic-location`, `query-result-subject`, and `raw-trace-location` reject both an empty branch set and an unauthorized simultaneous branch.
5. Every `EnumRef`, every non-§7 PascalCase type, every collection key tuple, every identity projection, and every Limit invariant appears in the Contract Package Manifest and schema-linkage verification. An unresolved type or registry reference is a package-integrity failure.
6. A derived identity-digest field, including `repositorySnapshotIdentityDigest`, `staticSemanticSnapshotIdentityDigest`, and `executionEvidenceSetIdentityDigest`, is `NON_ID` because its value is the output of its registered identity projection. Implementations recompute and validate the field and do not include that field as an input to its own projection.
7. Finalization follows §7.2 exactly. Build Artifact identity-references its not-yet-finalized Build Execution and the final Build Execution content-binds produced artifacts. Test Attempt identity-references its not-yet-finalized Test Run and the final Test Run content-binds attempts. Provider Invocation identity-references its not-yet-finalized Analysis Run and the final Analysis Run content-binds invocations and produced records. Trace identity-references its not-yet-finalized Runtime Execution; Span and Event identity-reference their not-yet-finalized Trace; the final Trace content-binds spans and events; and the final Runtime Execution content-binds traces.
8. Graph construction mints the OBJ-115 Graph Snapshot identity first. OBJ-116 Graph Layer identity-references that parent and finalizes first. OBJ-117 Graph Node and OBJ-118 Graph Edge identity-reference the Graph Snapshot and content-bind the finalized Graph Layer; every Graph Edge endpoint content-binds a finalized Graph Node. Object and relation population manifests then finalize, and the final Graph Snapshot content-binds its ordered layers and both population manifests. Reverse navigation is derived.
9. OBJ-126 predecessor lineage appears only in `/lifecycle/predecessorRelations` as `LineagePredecessorRelation`. No payload predecessor field is permitted. A successor evidence set content-binds its predecessor through that common lifecycle surface.
10. The exact O-REL equality constraints in §C.3.4 are validated together with the required `semanticRelationRef`; object and relation representations cannot be accepted independently when their kind, endpoints, order, conditions, method, evidence, or subject identity differ.
11. Artifact construction mints the Artifact Descriptor identity first. A material Artifact Origin may identity-reference that live descriptor when output correlation is required, but it never content-binds the descriptor. After the Origin is finalized, the final descriptor content-binds it through the required `/payload/originRef`. No reciprocal origin/output content-bound pair is permitted, and supplementary O-ART producer, input, invocation, or mapping fields must equal the facts in the bound Origin rather than create a second origin authority. OBJ-039 is a Build Execution rather than an Artifact Descriptor and is the sole O-ART row to which this `originRef` requirement does not apply.

## Appendix D — Exact semantic-relation shape-definition registry

### D.1 Common field ownership and relationship-profile registry

This section supplies the closed eight-row relationship-semantic-profile registry required by `JAN-CSAA-002@0.3.0` §4.2 and `JAN-CSAA-007` §§7.2–7.11 and 10.3. It binds, but does not restate as relation-specific payload, every one of the sixteen source-owned facets. The `REL-001` through `REL-137` variant rows contribute only their exact endpoint and per-variant supplements.

The following paths have one authoritative storage location:

- `IdentityEnvelope` owns `/schemaId`, `/contractVersion`, `/kind`, `/recordId`, `/recordDigest`, `/lifecycle`, and `/extensions`.
- `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` owns `/subject`, `/provenance`, `/epistemic`, `/informationControls`, `/invalidationDependencies`, and `/limitations`.
- `SemanticRelationRecord` owns `/relationKind`, `/profile`, `/endpoints`, conditional `/ordinal`, `/conditions`, `/requiredMetadata`, `/optionalMetadata`, `/ownerRef`, `/serializationOwnerRef`, and `/invariantIds`.
- `SubjectBinding` owns `/subject/repositorySnapshotRef`, `/subject/staticSemanticSnapshotRef`, `/subject/executionEvidenceSetRef`, `/subject/projectVariantRefs`, `/subject/comparisonSubjectRefs`, and `/subject/perimeterRef`.
- `Provenance` owns producer, method, run/invocation/input/raw-artifact/source-location/validation/transformation/authority references, `observedAt`, and `recordedAt`.
- `EpistemicState` owns support basis, capability coverage, execution health, freshness, conflict, inference, supporting/conflicting/unresolved-region references, and rationale.

Owner and serialization-owner tokens in the tables are closed registry shorthand, not bare serialized strings. They resolve as follows:

- `JAN-CSAA-002` resolves to the exact content-bound source-owner reference for `JAN-CSAA-002@0.3.0 / Draft`, path `JAN-CSAA-002 - TypeScript Semantic Model and Invariant Catalog.md`, and 162,179 exact stored bytes, as frozen by `JAN-CSAA-007` §4.1. Its digest descriptor is `{ algorithm: sha256, value: 9bcaa9f9a2212d66ae7c417af84c4f0e14672d282c04e73d719f7f9cceda1911, profileId: urn:janumi:csaa:digest-profile:raw-bytes:1.0.0, profileVersion: 1.0.0, representation: raw-bytes }`. Materialization uses the exact typed owner-reference and digest fields registered by §7.2; the shorthand never serializes as a document-ID string.
- `JAN-CSAA-003` resolves analogously to exact bound input `JAN-CSAA-003@0.1.0 / Draft`, path `JAN-CSAA-003 - Analysis Enrichment Query and Change Impact Specification.md`, and 169,676 exact stored bytes. Its digest descriptor uses the same raw-byte profile with value `65b3a9379dd47a25de1693ed709eafd11f7a9063db1cfd80b5da2bba01b46d10`.
- `JAN-CSAA-004` resolves analogously to exact bound input `JAN-CSAA-004@0.1.0 / Draft`, path `JAN-CSAA-004 - Code Analysis Rule Gate and Analyzer Provider Contract.md`, and 176,071 exact stored bytes. Its digest descriptor uses the same raw-byte profile with value `8812dc55c05167223341b08d3d5bc85b8b1e5ad085c9a0e198a13512af69dc89`.
- `JAN-CSAA-007` in a candidate-registry row designates candidate identity `JAN-CSAA-007@1.0.1` and path `JAN-CSAA-007 - Semantic Snapshot Graph Query Analysis Record and Adapter Contract Package.md`. This candidate does not embed its own content digest. Finalized package and integrity evidence bind the final document and schema digest externally; every later material record uses the resulting exact finalized `ContractRef`, including `schemaId` and the complete typed `contractContentDigest`.
- An advisory or other external concern owner resolves to the exact applicable `AuthorityRef`, `ExternalRef`, or `ContractRef` carried or content-bound by the relation endpoint and provenance. An owner without the complete fields of its selected §7.2 reference type is invalid. The owner union is closed; a display label, URI, organization name, or bare document ID is not an owner reference.

All `/ownerRef = …` and `/serializationOwnerRef = …` cells below resolve through these rules. This document therefore neither embeds a self-digest nor permits a future record to omit its finalized contract digest.

Endpoint-type tokens are also closed registry shorthand. A PascalCase endpoint name derived from an Appendix A source-object name resolves one-to-one to that row's Appendix C discriminator and definition. A material non-object endpoint resolves to the exact §7.11 material-definition name. `SemanticRelation.REL-nnn` resolves to that exact Appendix D relation variant. Any other endpoint-type alias is an unresolved schema-definition defect and never widens to a generic reference.

Consequently, `/requiredMetadata` does not repeat any subject or revision binding, provenance, source-location collection, support basis, lifecycle field, invalidation-dependency collection, limitation collection, owner, serialization owner, or invariant set. A schema that accepts both an inherited path and a shadow copy such as `requiredMetadata.subjectRef`, `requiredMetadata.staticSubjectRef`, `requiredMetadata.revisionBindings`, `requiredMetadata.provenance`, `requiredMetadata.provenanceRef`, `requiredMetadata.sourceLocationRefs`, `requiredMetadata.supportBasis`, `requiredMetadata.limits`, or `requiredMetadata.limitations` is ambiguous and invalid.

All 137 material Semantic Relation variants use `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope`. This is one exact assignment rule keyed to the complete relation set in D.1.2, not a deferred manifest choice. The primary `/subject/repositorySnapshotRef` is content-bound. A relation involving static semantics also content-binds `/subject/staticSemanticSnapshotRef`; a relation involving execution evidence also content-binds both the compatible static semantic snapshot and `/subject/executionEvidenceSetRef`. A cross-snapshot or cross-subject relation places every additional exact subject in role-labelled `/subject/comparisonSubjectRefs`; each endpoint role maps to exactly one primary or comparison binding. No relation invents a subject, names itself as its subject, or leaves an endpoint's snapshot association implicit.

`REL-131` remains a subject-bound semantic/history relation. It does not perform or authorize invalidation. An actual invalidation effect is a separately finalized `TechnicalEffectRecord` or `InvalidationRecord` using `ControlEventEnvelope`; when `REL-131` claims that effect as support, its provenance or epistemic supporting-record reference content-binds that effect record and its affected-target identity equals the relation's `affectedRecord` endpoint. The effect remains the only authority for effect kind, scope, actor, authority binding, effective time, and target.

Collection bindings use the exact registered keys:

- every set of `RecordIdentityRef` values uses `RecordIdentityRefCanonicalKey`;
- every set of `ContentBoundRecordRef` values uses `ContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey`;
- every set of `ContractRef`, `ExternalRef`, `RawArtifactRef`, or `AuthorityRef` values uses its corresponding §7.2 named canonical key;
- an ordered reference collection prefixes the applicable named reference key with its explicit semantic role and ordinal;
- every Source Location set uses `SourceLocationCanonicalKey`;
- every common-envelope collection uses the exact §7.10 path rule, with no fallback key.

`SourceLocationSetOrNotApplicable` is a closed discriminated binding. Its `applicable` branch contains a nonempty `locations` set using `SourceLocationCanonicalKey`; its `not-applicable` branch contains only the scalar `NotApplicable` value. The union itself is a required scalar binding. Collection semantics never apply to the `not-applicable` branch.

An optional metadata field is presentation-only. It has identity participation `NO`, invalidation `NONE`, and no power to alter subject, support, authority, lifecycle, or relation meaning.

### D.2 Descriptor grammar and auxiliary bindings

This registry is a normative, closed-field expansion of `JAN-CSAA-002@0.3.0` §4.2 and §15, reconciled to `JAN-CSAA-007` Appendix B and closed transitively by the auxiliary logical-type, exact enum/property, reference-target/predicate, canonical-key, and bounded-substitution registries in Appendix E. It defines `REL-001` through `REL-137`. A generated schema rejects any endpoint or per-variant field not named by the applicable row or its exact Appendix E closure row. Inherited common-envelope and relationship-profile fields are bound once by D.1 and do not reappear in these descriptors.

Descriptor grammar used below:

- `E(role; types; card; order; id; unresolved)` is one endpoint descriptor. `role` is the literal endpoint role; `types` is the closed allowed-type-reference list; `card` is endpoint cardinality; `order` is `ORDERED(slot=n)`, `ORDERED(key=(<named or complete canonical key>))`, `SET_CANONICAL(key=(<named or complete canonical key>))`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE`; `id` states identity participation; and `unresolved` is `FORBIDDEN` or `ALLOWED_AS_DESCRIPTOR`. Every collection-valued endpoint declares its complete deterministic key or cites the exact named key registered by `JAN-CSAA-007` §7.2.
- `F(pointer; type; card; collection; id; invalidation)` is one closed field descriptor outside the inherited common envelope. `pointer` is the exact JSON Pointer; `type` is the exact scalar, closed enum, closed record, or typed reference; `card` is field or collection-item cardinality as applicable; `collection` is `SCALAR`, `ORDERED(key=(<complete tuple>))`, or `SET_CANONICAL(key=(<named or complete canonical key>))`; `id` states identity participation; and `invalidation` states the change that creates a successor or invalidates dependent use. Every collection-valued field names its complete deterministic key and tie-break tuple or cites the exact key registered by `JAN-CSAA-007` §7.2 or §7.3. `NONE` means a presentation-only field never participates in identity or invalidation.
- `NotApplicable` is an explicit singleton, not `null`, absence, or an empty string. `UnresolvedEndpointDescriptor` is the closed descriptor defined by `JAN-CSAA-007` §10.3. `UnsupportedFlowDescriptor` is a closed unsupported-construct descriptor carrying construct kind, reason, attempted methods, and analysis frontier. A type written as `oneOf<A,B>` is a closed union. `RecordIdentityRef<T>` is descriptor shorthand for `#/$defs/RecordIdentityRef` constrained to the exact target kind, closed target-kind union, or named semantic-subtype predicate `T`; it never adds fields to the reference contract. `ExpressionOrConditionRef` is an exact closed `RecordIdentityRef` target-kind union and therefore uses `RecordIdentityRefCanonicalKey`.
- Every nonprimitive type token resolves to one exact local `$defs` target or externally owned contract reference. A PascalCase endpoint target name derived from an Appendix A source-object name resolves one-to-one to that row's Appendix C discriminator and definition. A material non-object endpoint target resolves to the exact §7.11 material-definition name. `SemanticRelation.REL-nnn` resolves to that exact Appendix D variant. Any other alias is an unresolved schema-definition defect and never widens to a generic reference. `ContentBoundRecordRef<T>` is not implied by `RecordIdentityRef<T>` and appears only where the finalization-direction registry permits it.
- Every `requiredMetadata` and `optionalMetadata` object is closed. `ClosedEmptyObject` means the required, closed `requiredMetadata` object has zero per-variant members after inherited envelope/profile facets are applied. Every optional field below has cardinality `0..1`, identity `NO`, and invalidation `NONE`. No row authorizes a generic map, metadata bag, provider-native property bag, or undeclared extension.
- Owner and serialization-owner cells use only the closed shorthand resolved by D.1. Thus `JAN-CSAA-002` means its exact §4.1 content-bound typed owner reference, `JAN-CSAA-007` means the candidate identity/version/path whose self-digest is bound externally by finalized package evidence, and an external concern owner means its exact typed `AuthorityRef`, `ExternalRef`, or `ContractRef`. No cell authorizes a bare serialized owner string.

The discriminator-to-shape projection is owned by `RelationshipSemanticProfileDefinition` and realized by `RelationshipProfileShapeBinding`. The exact bindings are `JAN-CSAA-007-RPSB-R-STR`, `JAN-CSAA-007-RPSB-R-RES`, `JAN-CSAA-007-RPSB-R-SEM`, `JAN-CSAA-007-RPSB-R-INF`, `JAN-CSAA-007-RPSB-R-MAP`, `JAN-CSAA-007-RPSB-R-EXE`, `JAN-CSAA-007-RPSB-R-EXT`, and `JAN-CSAA-007-RPSB-R-LIF`. Each binding carries the profile-owned subject, revision, provenance, lifecycle, source-location applicability, epistemic treatment, authority-and-limit, owner, serialization-owner, and cross-graph facets. Removing those common fields from a row does not remove their semantics; it prevents a divergent second serialization path.

Additional canonical-key and auxiliary bindings are exact:

- `OrderedRecordIdentityRefCanonicalKey` is `(ordinal, reference.RecordIdentityRefCanonicalKey)`. `OrderedContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey` is `(ordinal, reference.ContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey)`.
- `EndpointRevisionBindingCanonicalKey` is `(endpointRole, subjectRef.RecordIdentityRefCanonicalKey, revisionRef.RecordIdentityRefCanonicalKey)`.
- `SourceLocationCanonicalKey` means the complete discriminator, full `artifactRef` canonical key, exact range coordinates, bases/encoding where applicable, and artifact role defined by `JAN-CSAA-007` §7.3. `SourceLocationSetOrNotApplicable` is the required closed discriminated binding `applicable` with a nonempty `locations` set keyed by `SourceLocationCanonicalKey`, or scalar `not-applicable`; collection semantics belong only to the `applicable.locations` branch.
- `OrderedSourceLocationBinding` is the closed record `{ ordinal: Count, role: NonEmptyString, reference: ObjRef<source-location> }`. Its key is `OrderedSourceLocationBindingCanonicalKey = (ordinal, role, reference.ContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey)`. It is used only when relation semantics require ordered, role-labelled references to material Source Location objects rather than actual `SourceLocation` values.
- `LimitScopeBinding` is a closed union discriminated by `scopeKind`: `subject`, `record`, `contract`, `provider-adapter`, `operation-run`, `artifact`, `population-perimeter`, or `not-applicable`. Every applicable variant carries only its exact typed reference or closed population/perimeter binding; `not-applicable` carries an exact reason and rationale. Every variant carries `scopeCanonicalDigest: DigestDescriptor` over the complete binding. `LimitScopeBindingCanonicalKey` is `(scopeKind, scopeCanonicalDigest.algorithm, scopeCanonicalDigest.value, scopeCanonicalDigest.profileId, scopeCanonicalDigest.profileVersion, scopeCanonicalDigest.representation)`.
- `LimitStatement` is the closed record `{ limitCode, scope: LimitScopeBinding, statementDigest: DigestDescriptor }`. `LimitStatementCanonicalKey` is `(limitCode, scope.LimitScopeBindingCanonicalKey, statementDigest.algorithm, statementDigest.value, statementDigest.profileId, statementDigest.profileVersion, statementDigest.representation)`. Every profile-carried limitation collection uses that exact key.

Every `REL-001` through `REL-137` relation uses `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope`; an `R-LIF` graph relation is not thereby a `ControlEventEnvelope` effect or an independent lifecycle authority. `InvalidationEffectBinding` is a closed union: `applied` carries one `effectRef: ContentBoundRecordRef<oneOf<TechnicalEffectRecord,InvalidationRecord>>`, while `not-applied` carries exactly one `relationRole: candidate|observed-dependency` and no effect reference. For `applied`, the relation's affected endpoint set equals the effect record's controlled targets. `FreshnessProjectionBinding` carries one `basisRef: ContentBoundRecordRef<oneOf<FreshnessAssessmentRecord,InvalidationRecord>>` and its exact `basisKind`. `LineagePredecessorRelation<K>` is the exact successor-owned lifecycle entry constrained to relation kind `K`.

`InvalidationCause`, `InvalidatableRecord`, `StaleRecord`, `ConflictParticipant`, `CorroborationParticipant`, `CorrectableRecord`, `SupersedableRecord`, `DerivableSemanticObjectOrRelation`, and `DerivationSource` resolve to exact named, closed `$defs` semantic-subtype predicates. They are not extensible aliases. The reference mode remains the explicit outer `RecordIdentityRef` or `ContentBoundRecordRef` shown in each row; a subtype predicate never changes that mode.

### D.4 R-LIF equality, finalization, and completeness

#### D.4.1 Lifecycle and finalization direction

Lifecycle and finalization direction is exact. REL-131 content-binds a separate finalized effect record only in its `applied` branch and never mutates or authorizes the affected endpoint. REL-132 projects its content-bound freshness or invalidation basis and never mutates freshness. REL-135 and REL-136 content-bind the finalized successor and predecessor and carry the exact matching successor-owned `lifecycle.predecessorRelations` entry; kind, predecessor, effective time, reason, and authority are equal. REL-137 runs from the finalized derived record to finalized source records. Reverse indexes and reverse successor/effect navigation are derived and are never serialized. Optional `native*Id` values are non-authoritative provider/display correlations only; they never supply record identity, endpoint identity, ordering, lineage, or finalization.

- `REL-131` is evidence/history only. If it cites an invalidation effect, the relation content-binds the separately finalized `TechnicalEffectRecord` or `InvalidationRecord` as support; the effect's target equals the relation's `affectedRecord`. The relation does not carry a second authority binding or independently mutate freshness.
- `REL-132` content-binds the exact Freshness Assessment or Invalidation basis that establishes the stated dependency condition. Its stale-record and dependency endpoints, reason, cutoff, and basis agree with that record. It projects freshness; it does not set or mutate it.
- `REL-133` is symmetric. Its two content-bound participant endpoints use `SET_CANONICAL(ContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey)` and no source/target ordering.
- `REL-134` retains directed corroborating-to-corroborated roles and distinct provenance. Corroboration does not merge record identity or evidence lineage.
- `REL-135` and `REL-136` content-bind finalized successor and predecessor records and identify the exact matching successor-owned `/lifecycle/predecessorRelations` entry. Relation kind, predecessor reference, effective time, reason, and authority reference equal that entry. A relation without the matching entry is invalid and has no independent lifecycle authority.
- `REL-137` uses the one-way finalization direction derived-record identity to already-finalized source records. Every `sourceRecord` is a `ContentBoundRecordRef`, its set uses `ContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey`, reverse derivation lookup is derived, and no source record embeds a later derived-record or relation digest.

#### D.4.2 Completeness predicates

An integrated Appendix D passes this registry only when:

1. exactly eight RPSB rows exist and each exposes all sixteen named facets;
2. exactly 137 unique relation assignments exist, with no missing or duplicate `REL` identifier;
3. every relation has exactly one profile, one `SubjectOccurrenceEnvelope` assignment, one subject policy, one owner policy, one serialization owner, and one invariant set;
4. every inherited field is stored only at its authoritative path;
5. every cross-snapshot endpoint maps to a primary or role-labelled comparison subject;
6. every collection cites the applicable named canonical key or spells the complete registered tuple;
7. every content-bound reference targets an already-finalized, digest-valid record without introducing a cycle;
8. every optional metadata field has identity `NO` and invalidation `NONE`; and
9. `REL-131`, `REL-132`, `REL-135`, and `REL-136` satisfy the non-conflation and equality rules in D.4.1.

## Appendix E — Exact auxiliary-type, reference, key, and substitution closure registry

This appendix is a preserved legacy-family serialization decision carried into `JAN-CSAA-007@1.0.1 / Draft`. It closes the object-side auxiliary vocabulary used by Appendix C without transferring semantic ownership from `JAN-CSAA-002@0.3.0 / Draft`. The registry contains exactly 89 PascalCase leaf types, the one `RepositorySnapshotConstructionScope` composition token, and 82 `EnumRef` registry IDs. A conforming schema generator treats every row as closed. An undeclared member, branch, literal, null, extension point, generic property bag, or residual reference is a validation failure.

The source-owned rows below are local wire projections of already named JAN-CSAA-002 meaning. They do not add authority, correctness, completeness, or behavioral claims. A row labelled `CONSERVATIVE_CANDIDATE_REPAIR` closes a former documentation gap only for this candidate Contract Package; it is not attributed to an external source and is displaced by any later, valid concern-owner definition through an explicit successor and compatibility decision.

### E.1 Closed-shape grammar and common rules

#### E.1.1 Grammar

The exact compact grammar used in §§E.2–E.3 is:

```text
closed-object{ member[cardinality]:TypeExpression; ... }
closed-union(discriminator=member){ literal=>closed-object{...}; ... }
one-of(TypeExpression,...)
alias(TypeExpression where predicate)
lit(value-1,value-2,...)
ordered(TypeExpression; members=m..n; key=(complete-key))
set(TypeExpression; members=m..n; key=(complete-key))
```

`closed-object` admits exactly the declared members. `closed-union` admits exactly one listed branch and requires the discriminator literal written in that branch. `one-of` is an untagged union whose alternatives are distinguishable by JSON primitive/object shape or disjoint required-member sets; exactly one alternative validates. `alias` preserves the complete underlying wire representation and adds only the stated predicate. `lit` is an exhaustive set of JSON string, numeric, or Boolean literals; `other-declared` and `unknown` are ordinary literals, never wildcards. `ordered` preserves accepted order. `set` is sorted by the named complete canonical key after duplicate rejection. `m..n` uses `*` for an unbounded maximum. Inline `closed-object`, `closed-union`, and `one-of` expressions are anonymous shapes, not additional named registry tokens.

Field cardinalities are exactly `[1]` or `[0..1]`. Collection membership cardinality appears inside `ordered` or `set`; a collection-valued field itself is `[1]`. An omitted optional field and an empty collection are distinct. Null is never admitted. When a collection key names a component not native to `TypeExpression`, the serialized member is exactly a closed wrapper containing each such component and `value[1]:TypeExpression`; `ordinal` has type `Count`, `role` has type `NonEmptyString`, and another wrapper component has the type fixed by the cited Appendix C key registry or spelled in the consuming row. The complete key applies to that wrapper, and no wrapper field is synthesized after acceptance. For a composite key, an absent optional component contributes the distinguished empty component defined by the enclosing registry; it does not contribute null. Every equality or ordering predicate is evaluated on the normalized, JCS-compatible representation fixed by §7.10.

#### E.1.2 Reused vocabulary and reference discipline

The following names are direct reuse, not new definitions: §7.1 primitives other than forbidden `JsonValue`; §7.2 `RecordIdentityRef`, `ContentBoundRecordRef`, `ContractRef`, `ExternalRef`, `RawArtifactRef`, and `AuthorityRef`; §7.3 `SourceLocation`; §7.4 `ObservationScope`, `ObservationTargetBinding`, and `ObservationPopulationBinding`; Appendix C `ExternalVersion`, `ProviderNativeId`, `PermanentId`, `MediaType`, `JsonPointer`, `Limitation`, the six named canonical reference keys, `SourceLocationCanonicalKey`, and the registered `ObjRef`, `ObjIdentityRef`, `ObjRefChoice`, `ObjIdentityRefChoice`, `ManifestRef`, and `BindingRef` forms. `RepositorySnapshotConstructionBinding` is the exact four-branch binding registered in Appendix C. No row below changes any reused representation.

Every record reference uses the complete applicable §7.2 representation. Every collection of record references uses the complete named canonical key. A field ending in `Ref` carries one typed reference and never an embedded mutable object. A provider-native identifier has meaning only together with the provider/compiler/collector identity and exact `ExternalVersion` that issued it.

#### E.1.3 Basis, ownership, limits, and invalidation

Each row has one basis:

| Basis | Exact effect |
| --- | --- |
| `CORE_REUSE` | The row is an exact alias or enumeration already closed by current JAN-CSAA-007 core text. |
| `SOURCE_PROJECTION` | JAN-CSAA-002 owns the named semantic facet; JAN-CSAA-007 owns only the closed local serialization selected here. |
| `CONSERVATIVE_CANDIDATE_REPAIR` | Current source and core text leave the shape or values underdefined. This appendix selects the smallest operationally useful closed candidate, states the limit, and claims no external authority for the selection. |

The serialization owner of every row is `JAN-CSAA-007@1.0.1 / Draft`; the exact source-projection rows are unchanged from the preserved predecessor. The semantic-owner/source column identifies meaning, not wire ownership. A source projection is invalidated when a source subject, bound record, tool/provider identity or version, governing configuration, source mapping, observation cutoff, or named semantic-owner definition on which its value depends changes. A candidate repair is additionally invalidated by a conflicting concern-owner definition; replacement requires an explicit successor and compatibility treatment. A core alias follows the invalidation and compatibility rules of its aliased core contract. These common rules are supplemented, not weakened, by each row's limit/invalidation cell.

#### E.1.4 Prohibited widenings

No registry row admits `JsonValue`, `object`, `any`, an arbitrary map, a generic `attributes`, `properties`, `metadata`, `data`, or `details` bag, an open enum, an unspecified extension branch, or an implicit placeholder. Raw/provider-native material remains in a typed `RawArtifactRef`, `ExternalRef`, or version-bound native binding. A normalized category never erases the exact native identity required to reproduce the observation.

### E.3 Exact `EnumRef` registries

Each row lists the complete permitted literal set. There is no case folding, aliasing, numeric substitute, implied “other,” or acceptance of a producer-native code. An empty set, written `∅`, is also exhaustive: it makes the legacy `EnumRef` uninhabitable and activates the exact descriptor substitution in §E.4.2. This treatment is used for four version-sensitive TypeScript-native spaces that cannot honestly be frozen as package-wide, version-independent enums.

Validation, partiality, conflicts, withholding authority, or publication policy change invalidates it. |

### E.RL Relation logical-type and bounded-substitution registry

This fragment is a preserved legacy-family serialization decision carried into `JAN-CSAA-007@1.0.1 / Draft`. It closes the relation-side logical types used by Appendix D after the exact core types, Appendix C object aliases, inline-closed tokens, and the separately registered reference, subtype-predicate, and canonical-key rows are excluded. Semantic ownership remains with `JAN-CSAA-002@0.3.0 / Draft`; `JAN-CSAA-007` owns only the closed serialization projection. A schema generator rejects an undeclared member, branch, literal, null, extension member, generic property bag, unbounded integer, or unresolved leaf.

#### E.RL.1 Closed-shape grammar and common rules

The notation is the Appendix E object-registry notation:

- `closed-object{member[cardinality]:Type;...}` is an object with exactly the listed members.
- `closed-union(discriminator=d){v=>closed-object{d[1]:lit(v);...};...}` is a finite tagged union.
- `alias(T where predicate)` is a scalar or structural alias with the complete stated predicate.
- `ordered(T; members=m..n; key=(...))` and `set(T; members=m..n; key=(...))` are the only collection forms.
- `lit(a,b,...)` is a finite literal set. `NotApplicable` is the existing singleton and is never encoded as `null`, an empty string, or absence.

Every row has owner `JAN-CSAA-002@0.3.0`; every serialized projection has serialization owner `JAN-CSAA-007@1.0.1`; its legacy-family representation is unchanged. `SOURCE_PROJECTION` means the source catalog supplies the concern and the row makes its package representation exact. `CONSERVATIVE_CANDIDATE_REPAIR` means the source names the concept but does not close its representation; the row supplies the narrowest representation that preserves the stated distinction and evidence boundary. `CORE_REUSE` and `OBJECT_REGISTRY_REUSE` introduce no new values.

References named in a representation resolve only through the companion `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-*` reference/predicate registry. Canonical keys named in a representation resolve only through the companion `JAN-CSAA-007-ECK-*` registry. This fragment does not define or widen either family. All string comparison uses exact Unicode scalar values after NFC normalization unless a cited core type or key row specifies a stricter representation. Every digest uses the complete `DigestDescriptor`; every reference uses its complete registered canonical key.

#### E.RL.5 Exact bounded-substitution attachment

Each row is a mandatory descriptor-level replacement before Appendix D is treated as closed. A replacement changes only the named token, pointer, endpoint alternative, or helper; all other descriptor cells remain byte-for-byte semantically identical. Cardinality and collection order remain those already declared by the relation row unless this table explicitly replaces them. No row licenses a later-wave implementation or source mutation.

##### E.RL.5.1 Primitive and presentation normalization

The following four rows account for all 400 raw `string` occurrences exactly: 131 provider-native identifiers, four repository display paths, and 265 other nonempty text fields. `131 + 4 + 265 = 400`.

7. every collection has one cardinality declaration, one deterministic complete key, and explicit absence treatment for every optional projected key component;
8. every reference has an exact outer mode, target set or predicate, and finalization direction in the companion registry;
9. the object, relation-profile, relation-variant, reference/key, and this logical-type fragment are validated from one synchronized source snapshot; and
10. the stored form is UTF-8 without BOM, CRLF only, with exactly one terminal CRLF.

Failure of any item is a blocking closure defect. Local success is recorded as `RELATION_LOGICAL_AND_SUBSTITUTION_CLOSED`. ### E.R Exact reference-target, semantic-subtype, and finalization registry

This section is the preserved legacy-family reference closure carried into `JAN-CSAA-007@1.0.1 / Draft`. It closes the reference semantics present in Appendices C and D, the frozen object-auxiliary and relation-auxiliary Appendix E fragments, and the core-side EAT-C rows without changing semantic ownership held by `JAN-CSAA-002`, `JAN-CSAA-003`, or `JAN-CSAA-004`. Its whole-Appendix-E proof state is recorded solely in §E.V.

The pre-substitution C/D baseline consists of exactly 181 bare-reference field consumers: 163 in §C.4, fourteen transitive consumers in §§C.1–C.2, and four in §D.3. EOT-SUB-001 and EOT-SUB-006 retire three direct §C.4 paths without adding a direct bare-reference descriptor, so the integrated direct C/D surface contains exactly 178 consumers: 160 in §C.4, fourteen transitive consumers in §§C.1–C.2, and four in §D.3. The permanent ERT-R-C namespace preserves the three retired source-path IDs as non-consumer tombstones and closes their nested replacement references through V009 and V011. The frozen Appendix E auxiliary representations add exactly 335 standalone lexical reference occurrences, and the seven core EAT-C rows add twenty lexical occurrences on seventeen normalized reference-bearing paths. The registries below close every reference alias, source-owned reference target, semantic-subtype predicate, reuse edge, substitution output, and finalization direction in those surfaces.

No target set in this section is extensible. `A{x}` means exactly the Appendix A semantic-object discriminator or contiguous ordinal range identified by `x`, as shape-bound by Appendix C. `B{x}` means exactly the Appendix B relation identifier or contiguous identifier range identified by `x`, as shape-bound by Appendix D. `M{x}` means exactly the named §7.11 material definition. A slash such as `A{test-target}/M{TestTargetRecord}` identifies one material target through its discriminator and material-definition names; it does not add a second target. A consumer that cites an `ERT-R-T` row admits exactly that row's members.

`IDENTITY_FINAL` is an outer `RecordIdentityRef` whose target identity resolves to an already-finalized immutable record; the reference does not assert target bytes. `IDENTITY_LIVE(FDR-nnn)` is an outer `RecordIdentityRef` whose not-yet-finalized target is allowed only by the cited finalization-direction rule. `CONTENT_FINAL(FDR-nnn)` is an outer `ContentBoundRecordRef` to already-finalized, digest-valid bytes in the direction fixed by the cited rule. `CONTENT_FINAL(D-nnn)` uses the explicit acyclic direction row in §E.R.6. `EMBEDDED` is a closed descriptor and cannot be wrapped in a record reference. `RAW_ARTIFACT` is the exact §7.2 `RawArtifactRef` contract.

Every `ContentBoundRecordRef` target is finalized before its consumer unless an existing FDR explicitly defines a parent-finalization sequence. No target content-binds a later consumer. Reverse navigation is always a derived query or index and is never serialized into an accepted target or consumer.

#### E.R.5 Finalization-direction atoms

| Direction ID | Exact acyclic rule |
| --- | --- |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D001` | The target is finalized and digest-valid before the consumer. The consumer may content-bind it. The target contains no direct or transitive content-bound path to the later consumer. Reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D002` | The target identity resolves to a finalized immutable record before consumer finalization. The consumer keeps identity-only correlation. Neither side obtains a reciprocal content-bound field. Reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D003` | Object/relation projection identities may be minted before either correlated record finalizes. Both records finalize independently without a reciprocal content-bound edge; exact kind/endpoints/subject equality is validated. Reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D004` | Apply FDR-001: Rule Application Result finalizes first; the finding content-binds it; the result never embeds a later finding digest; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D005` | Apply FDR-002: Test Run identity is live while attempts identity-reference it; finalized attempts are content-bound by the final run; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D006` | Apply FDR-003: Build Execution identity is live while artifacts identity-reference it; finalized artifacts are content-bound by the final execution; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D007` | Apply FDR-004: artifact-descriptor identity may precede its origin; origin identity-references the live descriptor and binds finalized inputs; descriptor finalization content-binds the origin; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D008` | Apply FDR-005: source/target artifacts finalize before Source Map or origin mapping; mappings content-bind artifacts/raw map bytes; artifacts carry at most identity-only expected-map references; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D009` | Apply FDR-006: repository/revision/change/perimeter/context inputs and the non-self-referential raw manifest finalize before Repository Snapshot; later subject occurrences bind the snapshot; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D010` | Apply FDR-007: Analysis Run identity, then Provider Invocation identities, then model-exchange children; invocation binds exchanges and run binds invocations/produced records; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D011` | Apply FDR-008: Runtime Execution identity, then Trace identities, then Span/Event children; Trace binds children and Runtime Execution binds traces; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D012` | Apply FDR-009: Graph Snapshot identity, then layers, then nodes/edges/manifests, then finalized Graph Snapshot; only the specified identity-live edges point to the parent; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D013` | Apply FDR-010: Graph Delta identity may precede Graph Delta Entry children; each child identity-references only that live parent under the registered state/revision/token fields; finalized entries are content-bound by the final delta; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D014` | Apply FDR-011: Query Result identity may precede witness/explanation children; final result binds admitted children; no child content-binds the result; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D015` | Apply FDR-012: fixture, scenario, expected-judgment, mutation, and degradation inputs finalize before the Oracle Lifecycle record; later Rule Application Results content-bind the finalized oracle version; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D016` | Apply FDR-013: contract and schema artifacts finalize before the Contract Package Manifest; the finalized manifest is then content-bound by Compatibility Map and Decision records; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D017` | Apply FDR-014: redaction-manifest identity may be live; output finalizes with identity-only manifest reference; manifest then binds output; response then binds both; reverse navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D018` | Apply FDR-015: predecessor finalizes before successor; successor content-binds predecessor; relation matches successor-owned predecessor entry; reverse successor navigation is derived. |
| `JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-D019` | Apply FDR-016: an Analysis Status, Operation Progress, or Cancellation control may identity-reference a live operation, run, or invocation only with expected lifecycle state, monotonic revision, concurrency-token digest, authorization scope, and observation cutoff; the live target never content-binds the observation/control, while a later response or Audit Event content-binds the finalized observation/control in forward time; reverse navigation is derived. |

#### E.R.6 Bare-reference consumer registry

Every `I-FINAL`, `I-LIVE`, or `C-FINAL` row below is one exact active field consumer. `I-FINAL` means `RecordIdentityRef` plus `IDENTITY_FINAL`; `I-LIVE` means `RecordIdentityRef` plus the cited live FDR; `C-FINAL` means `ContentBoundRecordRef` plus finalized digest-valid target. `RETIRED` identifies a permanent non-consumer tombstone for a pre-substitution path eliminated by an enumerated EOT-SUB operation; it admits no target or reference, its ID is not reusable, and its replacement reference closure is carried only by the cited V-row. Collection cardinality and ordering for active rows remain those of Appendix C or D.

### E.K Exact canonical-key projection registry

This section closes the fourteen named key references and all 58 normalized real key expressions audited in the 709,576-byte pre-substitution Appendices C and D baseline, all 68 accepted key occurrences in the frozen Appendix E representation cells, and every transitive, substitution-output, and core-side key consumer. ECK-001 through ECK-027 are the exact named projections, ECK-N001 is their common normalization profile, ECK-X001 through ECK-X058 close the pre-substitution C/D source expressions, ECK-E001 through ECK-E014 close the frozen accepted-cell expressions, and ECK-T001 through ECK-T017 close reuse and substitution outputs. After bounded substitution, the integrated C/D source contains 57 active real key expressions: six historical expressions are removed and five named replacement keys are introduced, with their exact carriage closed by ESUB and ECK-T. The collision-bearing name `OrderedSourceLocationObjectRefCanonicalKey` is replaced by `OrderedSourceLocationBindingCanonicalKey`; no second alias is admitted.

#### E.K.1 Common key normalization profile

`JAN-CSAA-007-ECK-N001` governs every key row below:

1. Each key is a JSON array whose components occur in the exact written order. Nested named keys are spliced as their ordered scalar components unless a row explicitly identifies one nested JCS array component.
2. Every value is first validated and normalized by its closed TypeRef. `NonEmptyString`, `PermanentId`, `ProviderNativeId`, `RepositoryPath`, `JsonPointer`, `UriReference`, and enum literals are NFC strings; `RepositoryPath` additionally uses the §7.1 repository-path normalization. `Count` is a JCS safe integer. `Timestamp` is converted to its RFC 3339 instant with uppercase `Z`, the shortest fractional-second form preserving the instant, and no negative zero offset.
3. `DigestDescriptor` always contributes `(algorithm,value,profileId,profileVersion,representation)`. `RecordIdentityRef`, `ContentBoundRecordRef`, `ContractRef`, `ExternalRef`, `RawArtifactRef`, `AuthorityRef`, and `SourceLocation` always contribute the complete named projection in §E.K.2. A key never substitutes record ID alone, digest value alone, URI alone, presentation path, or a generic start coordinate.
4. JCS serializes the resulting array. Ordering compares unsigned UTF-8 bytes of that JCS serialization lexicographically. Numeric components therefore retain JCS number representation inside the array rather than becoming strings.
5. Null is never a component. A required missing component is invalid. Where a row explicitly says `or-empty`, absence contributes the zero-length string; the component TypeRef excludes the zero-length string when present, so absence cannot collide with a present value. For an optional `DigestDescriptor`, absence contributes five consecutive zero-length strings.
6. Key equality between distinct accepted members is a duplicate-key validation failure. There is no fallback to source order, whole-object bytes, locale collation, provider order, record ID, or an unstated tie-break. An `ORDERED` wrapper that needs repeated semantic values carries an explicit ordinal component.

Used by ECK-003, ECK-004, ECK-005, ECK-006, ECK-013, ECK-014, ECK-016, ECK-017, and every expression row that projects a digest. |

## Appendix F — Exact operational wire-closure registry
### F.1 Authority, closure grammar, and package boundary

This appendix is the exact candidate wire closure required by `JAN-CSAA-009@0.1.0`. `JAN-CSAA-009` retains operational meaning. `JAN-CSAA-007@1.0.1` owns only the serialization decisions below. No row instantiates an operational profile, creates a schema, authorizes persistence or execution, selects a storage or orchestration mechanism, reports a runtime observation, or changes an executable state.

The operational family is deliberately disjoint from the 144-definition legacy material universe closed by Appendix E:

- `JAN-CSAA-007-OEAR-001` through `032` are the 32 operational envelope assignments;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-T001` is the closed 31-record runtime operational target set;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-T002` is the singleton `OperationalProfileDefinitionRecord` target;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-T003` is the union of T001 and T002;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-A001` is `OperationalIdentityRef<T>` and carries `contractRef`, `recordId`, the role-specific stable identity, and role-specific state revision where applicable;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-A002` is `OperationalContentBoundRef<T>` and additionally carries the finalized `recordDigest`;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-A003` is the directional bridge to a finalized legacy `ContentBoundRecordRef<JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-T068>`;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-A004` is the directional bridge to a finalized operational `OperationalContentBoundRef<JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-T001>`;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-A005` is `MigrationEpochRef`, exactly `OperationalContentBoundRef<MigrationExecutionRecord>` at `PROPOSED` or a later registered migration state; its content-bound target carries the exact `migrationExecutionId`, state revision, source physical profile, target physical profile, and migration-scope binding, uses OCK-002, and follows D002;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-D001` is predecessor-before-successor operational finalization;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-D002` is finalized-content-before-operational-consumer;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-D003` is operational-identity correlation to a live machine whose state is not content-bound;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-D004` is sealed-candidate-before-publication-decision;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-D005` is finalized publication decision before the branch-complete legacy Publication Manifest; both finalized records precede the later lifecycle successor that binds them, and a published decision precedes every current-binding or acquired-read observation;
- `JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-D006` is replay-basis-before-candidate and output-complete-replay-after-candidate;

Every operational collection expands to the exact `OperationalCollection<Member, Mode, Key>` wrapper. `Mode` is `ORDERED` only when the field registry expressly supplies an ordinal; otherwise it is `SET_CANONICAL`. Every field token ending in `Refs` is, by grammar, `OperationalCollection<OperationalReference, SET_CANONICAL, OCK-005>` unless F.3.1 expressly overrides that exact token; its selected reference variant remains closed and typed. The remaining collection registry in F.3.1 is exhaustive for F.2 and F.3. Duplicate projected keys are invalid. No operational collection is `UNORDERED`; canonicalization never dereferences a target, invents an order, coerces a missing value, or silently removes a duplicate.

`OperationalReference` is the exact six-branch serialized union below. No generic string, URI, object, map, or unregistered reference branch is admitted:

```text
operational-content { refKind=operational-content, operationalRef:OperationalContentBoundRef<JAN-CSAA-007-ORT-T001> }
legacy-content { refKind=legacy-content, legacyRef:ContentBoundRecordRef<JAN-CSAA-007-ERT-R-T068> }
authority { refKind=authority, authorityRef:AuthorityRef }
artifact { refKind=artifact, artifactRef:RawArtifactRef }
policy { refKind=policy, policyRef:ContractRef }
external { refKind=external, externalRef:ExternalRef }
```

OCK-005 projects exactly the selected branch's full registered canonical key: OCK-002 for `operationalRef`, ECK-003 `ContentBoundRecordRefCanonicalKey` for `legacyRef`, ECK-007 `AuthorityRefCanonicalKey` for `authorityRef`, ECK-006 `RawArtifactRefCanonicalKey` for `artifactRef`, ECK-004 `ContractRefCanonicalKey` for `policyRef`, or ECK-005 `ExternalRefCanonicalKey` for `externalRef`. The projected selected key is not a serialized field. Exactly one branch value is present and fields from unselected branches are prohibited. The `policy` branch identifies an exact policy contract and never stands for a policy decision or policy-controlled material occurrence. Target eligibility, direction, and finalization still follow the reference-direction registry; the discriminator never grants authority or makes an unfinalized target content-bound.

Every operational material record is a closed `OperationalRecordEnvelope<Role, Payload>` with exactly:

```text
schemaId
contractId = JAN-CSAA-007-CF-OPS
contractVersion = 1.0.0
recordRole
recordId
recordDigest
semanticOwnerRef = exact applicable JAN-CSAA-009@0.1.0 content identity
serializationOwnerRef = JAN-CSAA-007-CF-OPS@1.0.0
roleIdentity
predecessorRefOrNotApplicable
operationalProfileInstantiationRefOrNotApplicable
projectionCoordinates = SET_CANONICAL<ProjectionCoordinate, OCK-003>; exactly P01 through P12
securityPartitionRef
authorizationContextRef
accessDecisionRef
informationControlBindingRef
observedAtOrEffectiveAt
provenance
evidenceRefs
limitations
payload
extensions
```

`recordId` is independently minted and is never presumed equal to a lifecycle, content, decision, claim, work, attempt, read, cache, backup, restore, migration, retention, tombstone, or other role identity. `OperationalProfileInstantiationRecord` alone may use reason `self-establishing-profile-instantiation` for its absent instantiation reference; every other not-applicable value requires the exact operation/profile policy reason. A role's exact F.3 payload is the sole serialization site for its machine state and state revision; the common envelope does not duplicate them. A state revision is another immutable occurrence with a new `recordId`, the same applicable stable machine identity, a monotonically increasing machine-specific revision, and an exact predecessor reference. Operational states do not extend the common `LifecycleState` creation-role vocabulary or the closed operation-response state union. `OperationTransitionRecord` exists only when the same event is an actual 007 operation-response transition.

Required fields appear without `?`; optional fields carry `?`; `oneOf(...)` is a closed tagged union; `ordered(...)` and `set(...)` use the registered keys above. Null is never a missing-value representation. A role-specific `notApplicable(reason)` branch exists only where the role table or source-owned applicability matrix expressly permits it.

### F.2 Operational Profile Definition

`OperationalProfileDefinitionRecord` uses `DefinitionEnvelope` and assignment `JAN-CSAA-007-OEAR-001`. Its payload is exactly `operationalProfileId`, `operationalProfileVersion`, and `facets`. Lifecycle, predecessor relations, semantic owner, serialization owner, definition provenance, applicability policy, invalidation dependencies, limitations, `recordId`, and `recordDigest` occur only in the inherited `DefinitionEnvelope`; the payload never duplicates them.

`facets` is an `ORDERED` fixed-length 30-entry tuple keyed by its explicit `facetOrdinal`, with `facetId` exactly O01 through O30 in ascending order. Every entry is the closed `OperationalProfileFacetEntry { facetOrdinal, facetId, applicability, value, basisRefs, limitations }`. `applicability` is exactly:

- `applicable`, requiring `value` and prohibiting not-applicable fields; or
- `not-applicable`, prohibiting `value` and requiring `applicabilityOwnerRef`, `reasonCode`, `explanation`, and nonempty `basisRefs`.

`value` is exactly `envelope-binding` or `governed-record-set`. `envelope-binding` is permitted only for O01 and contains the six fixed JSON pointers `/payload/operationalProfileId`, `/payload/operationalProfileVersion`, `/lifecycle/predecessorRelations`, `/lifecycle`, `/semanticOwnerRefs`, and `/recordDigest`; it serializes no duplicate value. `governed-record-set` contains one or more `RoleLabelledOperationalReference` members in `valueRefs`, keyed by OCK-009, whose selected reference is a finalized content-bound definition or exact policy contract, plus a closed completeness value `complete-for-declared-facet` or `partial-nonpass`. Missing, duplicate, blank, reordered, silently defaulted, merged, ownerless-not-applicable, or unresolved-value entries are invalid.

| Facet | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `O01` | Permanent operational profile identity and version plus the fixed inherited-envelope bindings for predecessor, lifecycle, owner, and exact record digest |
| `O02` | Exact governed document, contract-package, semantic-owner, implementation, and configuration identities |
| `O03` | Supported repository, worktree, branch, snapshot, evidence-set, principal, tenant, and confidentiality perimeters |
| `O04` | Deployment-independent component roles, trust crossings, side effects, and failure containment |
| `O05` | Immutable material classes, authoritative source for each class, identity, digest, and finalization rules |
| `O06` | Physical durability commitment for request, attempt, raw, normalized, candidate, publication, audit, and recovery material |
| `O07` | Security-partition, publication-channel, candidate, operation, cache, read-view, and generation-guard projections with applicability and placement independence |
| `O08` | Current-binding model, publication predecessor, fencing/concurrency token, and linearization proof |

| `O10` | Read-view acquisition, page/stream continuation, comparison, and mixed-revision prevention |
| `O11` | Dependency observation, invalidation event, conservative closure, broadening, and unresolved-dependency treatment |
| `O12` | Incremental plan, reuse provenance, recomputation, clean-full equivalence, and allowed-difference policy |
| `O13` | Cache and derived-index key, admission, validation, isolation, invalidation, eviction, and miss behavior |
| `O14` | Concurrent reader, writer, publisher, invalidator, migrator, retention actor, and recovery interaction |
| `O15` | Work claim, attempt, heartbeat or liveness observation, fencing, duplicate delivery, and stale-worker behavior |
| `O16` | Admission, priority, fairness, backpressure, deadline, timeout, progress, and resource-budget behavior |
| `O17` | Cancellation request, propagation, effective boundary, partial material, cleanup, and late-cancellation behavior |
| `O18` | Retry classification, uncertainty reconciliation, idempotency key, attempt limits, delay policy, and terminal outcome |
| `O19` | Crash and restart boundaries, durable checkpoints, startup reconciliation, abandoned work, and recovery ownership |
| `O20` | Integrity verification, corruption classes, quarantine, blast-radius analysis, repair, rebuild, and residual loss |
| `O21` | Backup set, consistency boundary, encryption, retention, restore isolation, validation, activation, and recovery objectives |
| `O22` | Storage/contract migration inventory, compatibility, shadow/dual modes, reconciliation, cutover, rollback, and decommission |
| `O23` | Retention policy, holds, archival, redaction, deletion, tombstone or unavailability evidence, and derivative inheritance |
| `O24` | Garbage-collection roots, reachability proof, grace boundary, deletion authorization, race prevention, and audit |
| `O25` | Authentication, authorization, least privilege, secret handling, encryption, key rotation, egress, and disclosure control |
| `O26` | Audit event classes, safe payloads, correlation, causation, ordering, integrity, retention, and access |
| `O27` | Health, readiness, liveness, freshness, integrity, backlog, capacity, dependency, and degraded-mode dimensions |
| `O28` | Metrics, traces, logs, service-objective parameters, workload measurements, cardinality, redaction, and evidence retention |
| `O29` | Storage/orchestration alternatives, unresolved decisions, safe defaults, experiment requirements, strongest opposing case, and exit criteria |
| `O30` | Requirement trace, 008 conformance allocation, failure-injection matrix, implementation authority, review, and residual risks |

The profile definition is definition-plane controlled material. `OperationalProfileInstantiationRecord` is runtime configuration truth. `OperationalObservation` is the abstraction realized by the specialized immutable occurrence records below. `OperationalQualificationAssessment` belongs to later qualification and V&V. The four concepts are not interchangeable; this appendix serializes the first two and the specialized observation roles, not a generic qualification result.

---

### F.3 Exact 31-role operational record registry

The rows are in the exact `JAN-CSAA-009` §7.1 order. Each assignment is unique, uses `OperationalRecordEnvelope`, and admits only the listed closed payload fields plus common envelope fields. A required `*Refs` field is always serialized, but its default cardinality is `0..*`; empty is an exact empty population, not omission, unknown, not-applicable, or proof of completeness. A role/state rule or the F.3.1 registry may narrow that cardinality to `1..*`, an exact count, or a phase-specific population. No collection is made nonempty merely because its field name ends in `Refs`.

`OperationalProfileInstantiationRecord` and `OperationalProfileDefinitionRecord` never alias. `RecomputationPlanRecord`, `CacheDecisionRecord`, `MigrationCutoverRecord`, `CapacityAdmissionRecord`, and `ProjectionBuildRecord` use ordinary independent `recordId` plus the exact correlation named in the table; no unregistered semantic identity is invented.

Claims and cache entries use conceptual `ABSENT` prestates. Failed claim acquisition creates no `claimId`, `claimRevision`, or `claimTokenDigest`. A bare exact-key cache miss may carry `cacheKeyDigest` in a `CacheDecisionRecord` but creates no `cacheEntryId`. Read acquisition always has `readViewLifecycleId`; the typed acquired-view identity is absent unless the lifecycle reaches `ACQUIRED`.

Reference-collection cardinality follows record phase rather than a name-based default. A `WorkAttemptRecord` in `CREATED` has exactly empty `rawMaterialRefs` and `outputRefs`; `RUNNING`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, or `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` admits `0..*` finalized members actually observed by that revision; `SUCCEEDED` requires a nonempty `outputRefs` population that satisfies every required `expectedOutputDescriptors` entry of its exact work unit, while `rawMaterialRefs` remains `0..*`. An initial `ExecutionClaimRecord(claimState=ACTIVE)` has exactly empty `renewalEvidenceRefs`; a later `ACTIVE` revision whose `claimRevision` advances carries one or more renewal evidence references, and a terminal `RELEASED`, `EXPIRED`, or `REVOKED` revision preserves the exact cumulative population, which may be empty when no renewal occurred. Every `RepairExecutionRecord` revision requires nonempty `authoritativeBasisRefs`; repair cannot begin, continue, verify, fail, or close without retaining its exact authoritative basis. `ReplayManifestRecord.eligibleAuditObservationRefs` and `eligibleHealthObservationRefs` are independently `0..*`. Its `outputAggregateDigests` is empty exactly when `outputRefs` is empty; otherwise it is nonempty, and its closed entries partition the exact `outputRefs` population with complete coverage and no overlap. `PublicationDecisionRecord.recoveryEvidenceRefs` is `0..*` for a directly proven decision and nonempty exactly when recovery established a decision after prior outcome uncertainty. Every other reference collection uses the source-owned role/state rule where one exists and otherwise admits the exact `0..*` observed population; empty never means complete, successful, authorized, or not-applicable without the separate registered state or completeness carrier.

`InvalidationDecisionRecord.stateBranch` is the sole carrier of state, revision, and phase-dependent binding:

- `observed { invalidationState=OBSERVED, invalidationStateRevision, bindingAttemptRefs:0..* }` prohibits exact dependency, prior result, bound subject, affected closure, unknown frontier, broadening, and failure fields;
- `observation-failed-unbound { invalidationState=OBSERVATION_FAILED_UNBOUND, invalidationStateRevision, bindingAttemptRefs:1..*, bindingFailureRef }` prohibits exact dependency, prior result, bound subject, affected closure, unknown frontier, and broadening fields;
- `bound { invalidationState=BOUND, invalidationStateRevision, changedDependencyRefs:1..*, priorResultRefs:1..*, boundSubjectRef, closureProgress=not-computed }` prohibits affected closure, unknown frontier, broadening, closure-failure, and conservative-noncurrent-scope fields;
- `closure-partial { invalidationState=CLOSURE_PARTIAL, invalidationStateRevision, changedDependencyRefs:1..*, priorResultRefs:1..*, boundSubjectRef, closureProgress=partial { affectedClosure, unknownFrontier, broadeningDecision } }` requires an explicit nonempty unresolved frontier;
- `closure-complete { invalidationState=CLOSURE_COMPLETE, invalidationStateRevision, changedDependencyRefs:1..*, priorResultRefs:1..*, boundSubjectRef, closureProgress=complete { affectedClosure, broadeningDecision } }` prohibits an unresolved frontier;
- `invalidated { invalidationState=INVALIDATED, invalidationStateRevision, changedDependencyRefs:1..*, priorResultRefs:1..*, boundSubjectRef, closureProgress=complete { affectedClosure, broadeningDecision }, stateEvidenceRefs:1..* }`; and
- `post-bound-work-or-terminal { invalidationState=RECOMPUTING \| REVALIDATED \| SUCCEEDED_BY_SUCCESSOR \| RECOMPUTATION_FAILED_NONCURRENT, invalidationStateRevision, changedDependencyRefs:1..*, priorResultRefs:1..*, boundSubjectRef, closureProgress, stateEvidenceRefs:1..* }`, where `closureProgress` is exactly `not-established { originState=BOUND, closureFailureRef, conservativeNoncurrentScopeRef }`, `partial { affectedClosure, unknownFrontier, broadeningDecision }`, or `complete { affectedClosure, broadeningDecision }` and preserves the latest established closure evidence without invention or loss.

The discriminator fixes the allowed fields; no record can pair an unbound branch with BOUND-or-later state or a bound branch with OBSERVED/OBSERVATION_FAILED_UNBOUND. Direct `BOUND -> RECOMPUTATION_FAILED_NONCURRENT` replaces `not-computed` with `not-established`, names the closure failure and complete conservative noncurrent scope, and invents no affected closure; failure from `CLOSURE_PARTIAL` retains the exact `unknownFrontier`; failure from `CLOSURE_COMPLETE` retains the complete closure. `INVALIDATED` is admitted only after complete closure. A later `RECOMPUTING` or `REVALIDATED` transition from a failed noncurrent state preserves whichever exact closure-progress branch that failure carried until newer evidence lawfully advances it. The closure-progress choice must equal the exact predecessor transition's latest established closure basis; it cannot be selected merely to satisfy a later state.
