For every `OperationalNamedEntry`, `entryId` is a nonempty permanent identifier within its containing collection and `valueDigest` is ODP-002 over `(entryKind, entryId, value)` with every exact empty collection preserved and must reproduce. Every `PermanentId`, `MediaType`, `NonEmptyString`, `JsonPointer`, `Timestamp`, `DigestDescriptor`, `ContractRef`, `AuthorityRef`, `RawArtifactRef`, and `OperationalReference` uses its already closed package type. OCK-009 projects the complete role and reference key, so the same target may occupy two distinct declared roles without collision while an exact duplicate role/reference member is invalid. OCK-010 additionally prefixes the contiguous assessment ordinal; repeated ordinals, repeated complete keys, gaps, or target kinds outside finalized operational or legacy content are invalid. `OperationalOutputAggregateDigestEntry.coveredOutputRefs` is nonempty; across the containing replay record those populations are pairwise disjoint and their union equals `outputRefs`, and each `aggregateDigest` applies its declared profile only to its own canonical covered population. In `MaterialLaneBinding`, the selected artifact branch's `RawArtifactRef` is the sole material identity and carries the exact bytes digest and media type; no duplicate scalar identity, digest, or type exists. Its authoritative `basisRefs` and exact `provenanceRefs` are independently nonempty. `integrityObservationRef` and `availabilityObservationRef` are exact finalized operational or legacy content references that own those distinct observations; the containing raw view has no duplicate top-level integrity or availability scalar. OCK-007 orders the nested material entry after `materialOrdinal`. `declaredDifferenceEntryId` must name exactly one `OperationalAllowedDifferenceEntry` in the same replay basis. A predicate's `entryId` fixes its rule; `source-owned-not-applicable` requires its exact owner, reason, explanation, and nonempty basis and is allowed only where that predicate's applicability rule expressly permits it. A safe-retained-field entry carries only a digest and safe reason/authority, never removed sensitive value bytes.

The following table is the exhaustive registry for every remaining collection-valued token in Appendix F; any unlisted non-reference collection field is invalid.

| Field token | Member | Mode | Key and cardinality |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `facets` | `OperationalProfileFacetEntry` | `ORDERED` | explicit `facetOrdinal`; exactly 30, O01–O30 |
| `projectionCoordinates` | `ProjectionCoordinate` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-003; exactly 12, P01–P12 |
| `channelBindings` | `RequestTargetPublicationChannelBinding` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-013; nonempty, with one unique exact `laneLabel` per governed request lane |
| `valueRefs` | `RoleLabelledOperationalReference` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-009; nonempty |
| `assessmentRefs` | `OrderedAssessmentReference` | `ORDERED` | OCK-010; nonempty with contiguous zero-based `assessmentOrdinal` |
| `expectedOutputDescriptors` | `OperationalExpectedOutputDescriptorEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; nonempty |
| `readinessConsequences` | `OperationalReadinessConsequenceEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; nonempty |
| `omissions` | `OperationalOmissionEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; zero or more |
| `allowedDifferences` | `OperationalAllowedDifferenceEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; zero or more |
| `allowedDifferenceResults` | `OperationalAllowedDifferenceResultEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; one per declared allowed difference |
| `predicateResults` | `PublicationPredicateResultEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007 with `entryId` equal predicate ID; selected branch of required `predicateEvaluation`, with exact branch cardinality below |
| `staticValidationResults` | `StaticValidationStageResultEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; exactly V01 through V06 once each, all finalized before seal |
| `canonicalAggregateDigests` | `DigestDescriptor` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-006; nonempty |
| `outputAggregateDigests` | `OperationalOutputAggregateDigestEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; empty iff `outputRefs` is empty, otherwise exact partition coverage |
| `publicationVector` | `PublicationLaneBinding` | `ORDERED` | OCK-008 with explicit `laneOrdinal`; nonempty |
| `observedPublicationVector` | `PublicationLaneBinding` | `ORDERED` | OCK-008 with explicit `laneOrdinal`; zero or more, with phase-correct equality to P07 defined by F.6 |
| `compatibilityPairs` | `CompatibilityPairBinding` | `ORDERED` | OCK-011 with contiguous `pairOrdinal`; exact directed-pair coverage defined by F.6 |
| `observedPhysicalBindings` | `CurrentPhysicalBindingEntry` | `ORDERED` | OCK-012 with explicit `laneOrdinal`; exactly one per corresponding publication-vector lane |
| `materialVector` | `MaterialLaneBinding` | `ORDERED` | explicit `materialOrdinal` followed by OCK-007; nonempty |
| `includedInventory` | `OperationalBackupInventoryEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; nonempty |
| `excludedInventory` | `OperationalBackupExclusionEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; zero or more |
| `restoreReadinessEntries` | `OperationalNamedEntry<restore-readiness-entry,RestoreReadinessEntry>` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; nonempty |
| `validationResults` | `RestoreValidationResultEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; exactly RST-V01 through RST-V12 |
| `laterActionResults` | `RestoreLaterActionResultEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; exactly RST-L01 through RST-L08 |
| `safeRetainedFields` | `OperationalSafeRetainedFieldEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; zero or more safe fields only |
| `currentnessLimitations` | `OperationalCurrentnessLimitationEntry` | `SET_CANONICAL` | OCK-007; zero or more |

`PublicationCandidateLifecycleRecord.predicateEvaluation` is always serialized as exactly one closed branch and never omits its nested `predicateResults`: `not-started { evaluationPhase=not-started, predicateResults=[] }`, `in-progress { evaluationPhase=in-progress, predicateResults=0..15 }`, or `complete { evaluationPhase=complete, predicateResults=exactly 16 }`. `ABSENT` and `ASSEMBLING` require `not-started`. `SEALED` permits any branch and persists each partial evaluation only through the explicit `in-progress` branch. `ELIGIBLE`, `INELIGIBLE`, `COMMITTING`, `COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, `PUBLISHED`, and `SUPERSEDED` require `complete`. `REFUSED`, `ABANDONED`, and `QUARANTINED` preserve the exact predecessor branch and population. Every populated branch contains at most one entry for each `PUB-P01` through `PUB-P16`; `complete` contains all sixteen exactly once. No transition may discard, fill, fabricate, or infer a result.

Every `StaticValidationStageResultEntry` has `entryId=stageId`, targets a finalized `ValidationResultRecord` whose stage equals that same ID, and binds the exact candidate subject and `validationInputBasisRef`. The six-entry set is complete and contains V01 through V06 exactly once. Those results finalize before the candidate and cannot reference its future candidate identity, lifecycle, legacy Manifest, decision, current binding, or postdecision result. V07 is prohibited from the sealed candidate and appears only as `PublicationDecisionRecord.publicationEligibilityValidationRef` after complete predicate evaluation; that V07 record may bind the finalized candidate and predicate basis but cannot reference the future decision, legacy Manifest, pair-binding successor, or current-binding observation.

`BackupSetRecord.consistencyBoundary` is exactly one closed branch. `crash-consistent` and `application-consistent` carry only `boundaryKind`, `boundaryRef`, and nonempty `basisRefs` and prohibit `boundaryDefinitionRef`; `other-declared` additionally requires `boundaryDefinitionRef:ContractRef`. Thus a standard boundary has one serialization rather than an optional redundant definition. `captureBoundary` is exactly `instant { capturedAt }` or `window { startedAt, endedAt, cutoff }`, with nondecreasing times and `cutoff` within the closed window. `inventorySummary` is `{ includedItemCount, excludedItemCount, includedByteCount, includedLogicalCount, aggregateDigest }`. Its counts equal the exact collection cardinalities and safe-integer sums; its `aggregateDigest` reproduces ODP-002 over the canonical OCK-007-ordered `includedInventory`.

Each `OperationalBackupInventoryEntry` binds one included source to one captured `RawArtifactRef`; that artifact's bytes digest is the sole per-item bytes digest. `sourceBindingDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over the discriminator plus the branch's canonical semantic-source projection: the complete partition or channel `DigestDescriptor`; ECK-003 of a Publication Manifest; `(securityPartitionId, publicationChannelId, publicationGeneration, OCK-002(publicationDecisionRef), OCK-002(publicationCandidateRef), completedLegacyManifestProjectionDigest, ECK-003(publicationManifestRef), bindingObservationCutoff)` for current binding; OCK-005 of immutable material; ECK-003 of an `AuditEventRecord`; OCK-005 of a policy; or `(sourceRole, ECK-004(roleDefinitionRef), OCK-005(sourceRef))` for `other-declared`. `bindingObservationBasisRefs` is evidence for the current-binding assertion and is deliberately excluded from semantic-source identity; changing only sufficient evidence cannot create another source digest. OCK-005 covers all six reference branches, including ECK-005 external and ECK-007 authority keys. The same digest field and rule apply to an exclusion's `excludedSource`. The union of included and excluded inventory is keyed for scope-partition purposes by `sourceBindingDigest`, independently of the OCK-007 entry key; duplicate source digests, a digest mismatch, or one digest in both collections is invalid. `itemSizeBytes` and `itemLogicalCount` are exact nonnegative counts. `referenceClosure` is the inline, content-bound backup closure proof and does not depend on an unregistered operational role or repurpose code-call reachability. Its `sourceBindingDigest` equals the containing entry, its `captureCutoff` equals the containing backup cutoff, and `requiredRefs` is the complete canonical transitive population required to reconstruct and validate the captured source. Every required member is finalized by the cutoff and maps to exactly one included inventory source; no required member may be excluded. `closureDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over `(sourceBindingDigest, ECK-006(capturedArtifactRef), captureCutoff, requiredRefs)`, `unresolvedRefs` is exactly empty, and nonempty `evidenceRefs` supports rather than substitutes for the closure. A `ReachabilityAssessmentRecord` may appear only as genuinely applicable evidence; it is never reinterpreted as general persisted-reference closure. An omitted, open, partial, stale, unsupported, failed, differently scoped, differently cut off, non-reproducing, or unresolved closure is invalid. The classification plus nonempty information-control policy set applies to that captured item. Every information-control policy member is either an exact policy contract or a finalized `InformationControlBinding`, never an arbitrary artifact, authority, external, or unrelated content reference. Distinct entries may carry byte-identical artifacts because their source bindings and source-binding digests remain distinct. The declared backup scope partitions every applicable security partition, publication channel, Publication Manifest, current binding, immutable material, audit population, and policy population into exactly one included or excluded entry; no scoped source is omitted or appears in both collections. A repeated source binding, missing included member, second per-item bytes-digest carrier, or item not covered by the aggregate is invalid. `excludedInventory` records every exact exclusion with reason, authority, and nonempty basis; it never counts as captured material.

`OperationalBackupSourceBinding` is a total, mutually exclusive semantic-source union. `security-partition` and `publication-channel` are the only encodings of those logical perimeter values. `publication-manifest` is used only when a finalized legacy Manifest is captured as an independently retained noncurrent/historical material source. `current-binding` is the only branch that conveys currentness. `audit` is the only branch for an audit-population member and targets only a finalized `AuditEventRecord`; `policy` is the only branch for an exact policy contract. `immutable-material` identifies only a finalized record or artifact captured for its immutable bytes and confers no currentness, policy, audit, Manifest, channel, or partition meaning. Capturing an immutable record that also participates in a current binding does not satisfy or replace the separately required `current-binding` scope entry. `other-declared` is permitted only when `roleDefinitionRef` proves that the source role cannot be represented by any named branch; it is prohibited whenever a named branch applies. The same semantic source and role therefore has one branch and one `sourceBindingDigest`; changing only the discriminator, evidence population, or invented source role is invalid.

Define the backup `captureCutoff` as `instant.capturedAt` or `window.cutoff`. An `OperationalBackupSourceBinding.current-binding` is valid only when its `bindingObservationCutoff` equals that `captureCutoff` and its nonempty `bindingObservationBasisRefs` prove the actual authoritative physical binding at that cutoff. Its complete key/value tuple is `(securityPartitionId, publicationChannelId, publicationGeneration, publicationDecisionRef, publicationCandidateRef, completedLegacyManifestProjectionDigest)` and must equal the actual binding defined by F.5. `publicationDecisionRef` targets `decision=published`; its lifecycle and both common-envelope partitions equal `securityPartitionId`; its channel, resulting generation, candidate reference, and completed projection digest equal the serialized values; and the decision/Manifest pair is the exact pair bound by the later lifecycle successor under F.5/F.6. The Manifest must reproduce the candidate static projection and decision complete projection. A publication-manifest source binds a finalized digest-valid noncurrent/historical legacy Manifest; a security-partition or publication-channel source uses the exact P01–P02 or P03–P05 digest. These rules apply at the backup consistency/capture boundary independently of any later read view. A stale, superseded-as-current, mismatched, outcome-unknown, pre-Manifest, unpaired, corrupt, unavailable, or unobserved binding is not captured as a valid current-binding entry and remains an explicit exclusion or backup failure.

`operationalBasis` is the closed object `{ operationalProfileRef, storageFormatRef, contractPackageRefs, migrationEpoch, encryptionBinding }`; `operationalProfileRef` targets one finalized `OperationalProfileInstantiationRecord`, `storageFormatRef` is the exact storage-format contract, `migrationEpoch` is exact `MigrationEpochRef` or owner-backed not-applicable, every contract-package member is a finalized `ContractPackageManifestRecord`, and `encryptionBinding` always carries an exact encryption-property `ContractRef` plus one or more finalized opaque `SecretReferenceRecord` references without key material. `lineageBinding` is `full { lineageRefs=[] }` or `incremental { baseBackupSetRef:OperationalContentBoundRef<BackupSetRecord>, deltaBasisRefs:1..* }`. `protectionBinding` carries nonempty retention, access, and destruction policy references; hold members only as finalized `RetentionReferenceRecord` values; and `copyBinding` as either reasoned `no-additional-copy` or nonempty exact `RawArtifactRef` copies, plus exact location-class `ContractRef`.

`restoreReadiness.restoreReadinessEntries` is nonempty and OCK-007 keyed. In every entry, `sourceSurface` mechanically reproduces the containing backup's operational profile, storage-format contract, complete contract-package population, migration epoch, and encryption-property contract. `surfaceDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over those five preceding fields in declared order. `targetSurface` names one exact prospective restore surface and computes the same projection. `exact-equality` is valid only when source and target surface digests are byte-equal and its nonempty basis proves that equality; a single unlabeled profile reference, partially equal surface, or omitted component is invalid. `assessed` targets only a finalized successful `CompatibilityClaimRecord` and requires its direction, exact source/target profiles and contracts, semantic owners, assumptions, complete differing-surface coverage, evidence, loss treatment, distinct author/review, validity, and invalidations to reproduce the entry. Its `compatibilityUseProjectionDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over `(sourceSurface.surfaceDigest, targetSurface.surfaceDigest, prerequisiteRefs, ECK-003(compatibilityRef), direction, result, semanticLossTreatment, validity)`. Every differing component must be covered; an unrelated, expired, invalidated, unsuccessful, partially scoped, or reverse-only claim is invalid. The `sourceSurface` and `targetSurface` roles never collapse into an unlabeled set.

The selected `RestoreExecutionRecord.restoreReadinessEntryId` names exactly one entry in its content-bound backup. Its target operational profile and storage format equal that entry's `targetSurface`; the complete target surface and every prerequisite are rechecked at `candidateBasisCutoff`. Backup-time compatibility alone is insufficient, and no missing comparison, owner-backed-not-applicable compatibility, or unrelated successful claim can authorize restore or activation.

`recoveryObjectives` is `{ objectiveOwnerRef:AuthorityRef, recoveryPointObjectiveMilliseconds:Count, recoveryTimeObjectiveMilliseconds:Count, basisRefs:1..* }`. These are owner-supplied parameters; this Draft selects no value. `verification` is exactly `not-verified`, `passed`, or `failed`; every branch carries `creationEvidenceRef`, nonempty exact `AuthorityRef` reviewers, nonempty finalized `CoverageMatrixCellRecord` test allocations, and an exact `verificationRefs` collection that is empty only for `not-verified` and nonempty otherwise. The common-envelope `limitations` field is the sole known-limitation carrier. Together these closed carriers bind the §18.1 profile, format, contract, migration, encryption/key, capture, inventory, digest/size/count/reference/classification, lineage, retention/hold/copy/location/access/destruction, restore, RPO/RTO, creation, verification, review, test-allocation, and limitation surfaces without selecting a mechanism, product, topology, or objective value.

Each `RestoreExecutionRecord` is one terminal, immutable observation for one `restoreExecutionId`; retry, restart, repair, disaster-recovery test, or separately initiated prospective activation receives a new identity rather than another attempt member under the old identity. `candidateBasisCutoff` is the common pre-candidate restore, validation, and later-action reconciliation cutoff; `completedAt` is the later terminal restore observation cutoff. Its nonempty `restoreAttemptRefs` are only finalized bounded restore/material-reconstruction `WorkAttemptRecord` substeps whose outputs and terminal evidence exist no later than `candidateBasisCutoff`; publication-intent, comparison, decision, response, or postcandidate work is prohibited from that population. The content-bound `backupSetRef` fixes source bytes and capture cutoff, `restoreReadinessEntryId` fixes one exact target surface, and `restorePurpose` is exactly one of the four declared values. `targetIsolation.targetSecurityPartitionId` is the exact logical security partition of the scoped backup material; `targetIsolationId` is the distinct isolated non-current restore destination and never substitutes for or changes that security identity. `targetIsolation.proven-isolated` proves no later than `candidateBasisCutoff` that this destination is non-current, physically separated from every authoritative current-binding target, and unable to overwrite newer authoritative history; `isolation-not-proven` preserves the exact failed proof and blocks all restore material use and activation. Every activation-capable outcome requires `proven-isolated`, and the target profile/storage-format pair equals the selected readiness target.

`validationResults` contains exactly twelve OCK-007-keyed entries, each with matching `entryId=validationId`, one registered method, nonempty evidence finalized no later than `candidateBasisCutoff`, and explicit `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `UNKNOWN`: `RST-V01` backup identity; `RST-V02` inventory completeness; `RST-V03` per-item and aggregate integrity; `RST-V04` encryption and key access; `RST-V05` contract compatibility; `RST-V06` physical-format and migration compatibility; `RST-V07` destination isolation and no-overwrite; `RST-V08` collection and reference reconstruction; `RST-V09` Publication Manifest and current-binding-candidate reconstruction; `RST-V10` audit and policy reconstruction; `RST-V11` authorization and security; and `RST-V12` recovery validation. Missing, duplicate, renamed, inferred, post-cutoff, or unevidenced results are invalid. Activation requires all twelve to be `PASS`; any `FAIL` or `UNKNOWN` blocks activation.

`laterActionResults` contains exactly eight OCK-007-keyed entries, each with matching `entryId=actionClassId`: `RST-L01` publication; `RST-L02` invalidation; `RST-L03` revocation; `RST-L04` policy; `RST-L05` retention or hold; `RST-L06` deletion or tombstone; `RST-L07` key action; and `RST-L08` security action. For each class, `actionRefs` is the complete exact action population after the backup cutoff through `candidateBasisCutoff`. `no-later-action` requires exactly empty `actionRefs` and nonempty proof of absence; `reapplied` or `reconciled` requires nonempty exact action and result evidence finalized by that cutoff; `blocked` or `unknown` preserves the nonpass. Activation permits only `no-later-action`, `reapplied`, or `reconciled` in all eight entries. A later deleted, revoked, stale, superseded, held, unauthorized, or key-inaccessible state can therefore never be silently revived.

Every `refused`, `committed`, or `outcome-unknown` activation carries one exact `RestoreDerivedCandidateBinding`. Its source backup, readiness entry, `candidateBasisCutoff`, and restore-attempt population are byte-equal to the containing Restore Execution fields. `restoredAndReconciledOutputRefs` is the complete canonical union of every finalized restore-attempt output after applying all eight later-action results through that cutoff, with no omitted, duplicate, pre-reconciliation, unrelated, blocked, or post-cutoff output. `validationResultsDigest` and `laterActionResultsDigest` are exactly ODP-002 over the complete canonical OCK-007-ordered containing collections. The lifecycle reference targets the exact finalized predecision lifecycle revision that binds `publicationCandidateRef`; the candidate seals only after `candidateBasisCutoff`, and its member, dependency, limitation, and validation-input basis manifests collectively content-bind the source backup, selected readiness basis, complete restored-and-reconciled output population, validation evidence, and later-action evidence. `derivationEvidenceRefs` is nonempty and contains only those finalized pre-candidate source, attempt, validation, and reconciliation inputs; it prohibits the candidate/lifecycle pair, publication intent/decision, terminal Restore Execution record, response, or later audit/health observation. `bindingDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over `(OCK-002(sourceBackupSetRef), restoreReadinessEntryId, candidateBasisCutoff, restoreAttemptRefs, restoredAndReconciledOutputRefs, OCK-002(candidateLifecycleRef), OCK-002(publicationCandidateRef), validationResultsDigest, laterActionResultsDigest, derivationEvidenceRefs)`. A candidate not mechanically derived from this exact pre-candidate restore basis is invalid for the activation branch even if it is otherwise eligible.

`activation` is closed. `not-requested` and `blocked` change no binding. `refused` targets a finalized `PublicationDecisionRecord(decision=refused)` whose lifecycle and candidate equal its `derivedCandidate`. `committed` targets a finalized `decision=published`; its security partition, channel, resulting generation, `derivedCandidate.publicationCandidateRef`, and completed legacy-Manifest projection digest reproduce both that decision and the exact newly fenced authoritative physical binding observed at `bindingObservationCutoff`; no other branch changes current binding. `outcome-unknown` binds the exact durable publication intent whose subject names its derived lifecycle/candidate and carries nonempty reconciliation evidence while preserving absence of a decision. The candidate and lifecycle finalize from predecessor inputs after `candidateBasisCutoff` and before intent/decision. Any publication, invalidation, revocation, policy, retention, deletion, key, or security action after that cutoff is handled by the ordinary PUB-P01–P16, authorization/policy validity, current-guard, fencing, and compare-and-publish checks and must refuse or stale the candidate when incompatible; it is never backfilled into the pre-candidate restore basis. The publication decision, when one exists, finalizes before this restore observation and never content-references the later restore record.

The outcome/activation matrix is exact: `completed-isolated` pairs only with `activation=not-requested`; `activated` pairs only with `activation=committed`; `failed` pairs only with `blocked` or `refused`; `outcome-unknown` pairs only with `activation=outcome-unknown`; and `cancelled` pairs only with `not-requested` or `blocked` and never claims activation. `completed-isolated` and `activated` require `rollback=not-required`. `RestoreRollbackBinding` is exactly `not-required`, verified `completed`, evidenced `failed`, or evidenced `unknown`; branch-incompatible or omitted rollback standing is invalid. `RestoreResidualLossBinding` is exactly verified `none`, authority-backed `bounded-disclosed` with exact affected-scope digest and loss-manifest reference, or evidenced `unknown`. Failed, cancelled, incomplete, validation-nonpass, later-action-nonpass, isolation-nonpass, rollback-unknown, activation-unknown, or residual-loss-unknown execution never becomes current. `completedAt` is not earlier than any carried attempt, validation, reconciliation, activation, rollback, or residual-loss evidence cutoff.

### F.4 Closed operational identity and projection registry

The registry has exactly 37 rows naming 40 independently preserved identities. Companion-row presentation never merges the named identities.

| Identity | Required scope |
| --- | --- |

| `attemptId` | Unique for every retry, restart, repair, recovery, or reconciliation attempt |

| `expectedPublicationGeneration` | Mutable compare-and-publish guard |
| `publicationGeneration` | Monotonic committed current-binding generation inside one channel |
| `publicationCommitId` | Identity minted only with one authoritative finalized Publication Decision |
| `readViewLifecycleId` | One requested-through-terminal acquisition attempt |
| `readViewId` | One successfully acquired immutable publication vector |
| `rawMaterialReadViewId` | One successfully acquired immutable raw-material vector |

`RequestIdempotencyBinding` is a closed union. `no-caller-key` is the sole representation of the source-defined no-caller-key case: it carries the exact no-deduplication standing, fixed absence reason, and nonempty basis; it contains no blank, null, synthetic namespace/value, digest, lifetime, response class, or implied key. The mandatory Operation Request carrier therefore never fabricates caller intent. `caller-key` contains one exact `RequestIdempotencyKey`.

`RequestAdmissionStableKey` is the strict closed `IDEM-01` stable scope from `JAN-CSAA-009` §13.2. `keyVersion` names the exact active IDEM-01 key contract. `callerKeyNamespace` and `callerKeyValueDigest` preserve the caller-supplied deduplication scope without exposing the caller's raw key value. `callerKeyIdentityDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over `(keyKind, keyVersion, callerKeyNamespace, callerKeyValueDigest)` and is the retained lookup identity for caller-key reuse; it deliberately excludes every governed request input so an incompatible reuse cannot evade collision detection by changing the full projection digest. `securityPartitionId` is the exact P01–P02 digest.

`targetBinding` is exactly `publication-channels` when only publication-channel targets are governed, `subject` when only the exact serialized `subjectInput` branch is governed, and `publication-channels-and-subject` when both are governed inputs. Each channel-bearing branch serializes the complete nonempty `channelBindings` population; OCK-013 orders it by the exact nonempty `laneLabel`, and a repeated label is invalid even if the channel digests differ. Every non-comparison operation governed by exactly one channel carries exactly one binding with `laneLabel=primary`. `csaa.comparison.compute` instead carries all and only its independently governed request lanes: each binding's `laneLabel` is byte-equal to the corresponding role label in the complete `SemanticComparisonInput` and governed comparison-subject target population, and its `publicationChannelId` is the exact P03–P05 digest for that same labeled lane. No comparison lane may be absent, extra, relabeled, coalesced, or associated with another lane's channel. A channel population with no exact label-to-request-lane correspondence is invalid. Because `targetBinding` itself is in the `keyDigest` preimage, every label and all five `DigestDescriptor` fields of every corresponding channel participate in request identity.

In both subject-bearing branches, `subjectInputProjectionDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over the complete closed sibling `OperationRequestBase.subjectInput`, including its discriminator and every branch field: resolved Subject Binding; unresolved repository/worktree locator, revision/change coordinates, project hints, and resolution policy; authorized scoped target and target populations; exact content-bound target record; live-target identity, expected state/revision/token and authorization scope; or operation-policy not-applicable. It never substitutes a resolved subject for a locator, scoped target, record, or live target. `source-owned-not-applicable` is admitted only when the exact operation policy permits both publication channel and semantic subject to be not applicable; it carries the exact owner, reason, explanation, and nonempty basis. An empty, ownerless, operation-incompatible, fabricated-resolved, or mismatched target is prohibited. `canonicalRequestDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over the request's operation/version, exact `ControlEventEnvelope.controlScope`, actor and authority binding, controlled-target population, information controls, compatibility input, repository/worktree scope or explicit absence, subject input, operation input, freshness requirement, resource budget, deadline or explicit absence, cancellation semantics, partial-result policy, redaction-policy reference, audit context, and rationale. It excludes `requestId`, the idempotency carrier itself, derived `operationKey`, request/record clock observations, transport/delivery/attempt/schedule facts, record identity/digest, evidence, provenance, and extensions. `RequestAdmissionStableKey.keyDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over `(keyKind, keyVersion, callerKeyNamespace, callerKeyValueDigest, callerKeyIdentityDigest, operationId, operationVersion, securityPartitionId, targetBinding, canonicalRequestDigest)`.

`RequestIdempotencyKey` preserves the additional exact §7.3 identity surface without silently widening the §13.2 stable key. `declaredLifetime.lifetimeMilliseconds` is the caller/profile-declared nonnegative retention-and-replay horizon and `lifetimePolicyRef` is its exact contract; neither is derived from receipt time or retry schedule. `retainedResponseClassRef` names the exact operation/version replayable response and retention contract. `requestIdentityDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over `(stableKey.keyDigest, declaredLifetime, ECK-004(retainedResponseClassRef))`. Request admission first looks up `callerKeyIdentityDigest`; retained request replay requires byte-equal `stableKey.keyDigest` and `requestIdentityDigest`. An equal caller-key identity with an unequal governed stable projection, lifetime, or response class is a collision and refusal, not a second key or permission to reinterpret the retained response. This three-digest composition losslessly preserves both closed source passages; it does not choose one as permission to omit the other.

`EffectIdempotencyKey` is a closed union selected by `ExternalEffectIntentRecord.effectKind`. Every nonpublication externally observable effect uses `external-effect`. Its `ExternalEffectStableKey` is the strict closed `IDEM-04` stable scope from `JAN-CSAA-009` §13.2: `keyKind` is exactly `IDEM-04`; `keyVersion` names the active IDEM-04 contract; the four digest projections are exactly ODP-002 over the intent's `targetSystemRef`, `subjectBinding`, `securityScopeRef`, and `expectedPriorState`; and effect kind/version and intended-payload digest are byte-equal to the intent fields. `ExternalEffectStableKey.keyDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over all preceding stable-key fields in declared order and deliberately excludes operation execution and work unit.

`ExternalEffectIdentityBinding` separately preserves the additional exact §7.3 identity surface. Its `operationExecutionId` and `workUnitRef` are byte-equal to the intent fields, and `effectIdentityDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over `(stableKey.keyDigest, operationExecutionId, OCK-002(workUnitRef))`. Retry/duplicate-effect suppression and uncertainty grouping use the stable-key digest; separately addressable intent correlation uses the extended identity digest. An equal stable key with an unequal operation/work-unit extension is a collision requiring authoritative reconciliation, never permission to repeat or reinterpret the effect. Attempt, claim, worker, clock, schedule, queue, and physical-location facts remain provenance and occur in neither digest. This two-digest composition losslessly preserves both closed source passages without silently widening the IDEM-04 retry-stable key.

Every publication commit instead uses the `publication-commit` branch and carries the exact `PublicationIdempotencyKey`, whose durable intent projection binds operation and work unit under the distinct IDEM-07 scope; a publication commit cannot invent or substitute an IDEM-04 key. `ExternalEffectReconciliationRecord.effectIdempotencyKey` is byte-equal to its finalized `intentRef` target's complete key/binding. An unequal key kind/version, branch, registered projection, identity extension, or digest is a collision and never authorizes replay.

`PublicationIdempotencyKey` is a closed object rather than an untyped digest. `keyKind` is exactly `IDEM-07`; `keyVersion` is the exact active version of the IDEM-07 key contract named by the operational profile; and `commitIntentVersion` is the distinct publication-commit intent version. `keyDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over `(keyKind, keyVersion, publicationChannelId, candidateLifecycleId, publicationCandidateId, expectedPredecessor, expectedPublicationGeneration, authorizationRef, publicationIntentDigest, commitIntentVersion)`.

`publicationIntentDigest` is exactly ODP-002 over the finalized durable intent target's `(effectKind=publication-commit, effectVersion, operationExecutionId, workUnitRef, subjectBinding, securityScopeRef, targetSystemRef, expectedPriorState, authorizationRef)`. The lifecycle `intentRef` targets only a finalized `ExternalEffectIntentRecord` with that effect kind; its `effectVersion` equals `commitIntentVersion`; its subject binding names the exact security partition, channel, lifecycle, and sealed candidate; its target-system binding names the authoritative `(securityPartitionId, publicationChannelId)` binding key; its expected prior state equals `expectedPredecessor` and `expectedPublicationGeneration`; its authorization equals the key projection; its `intendedPayloadDigest` equals `publicationIntentDigest`; and its `effectIdempotencyKey` is the `publication-commit` branch containing a byte-equal copy of the lifecycle's `PublicationIdempotencyKey`. `ABSENT`, `ASSEMBLING`, `SEALED`, `ELIGIBLE`, `INELIGIBLE`, and every precommit terminal revision prohibit `intentRef` and `publicationIdempotencyKey`. `COMMITTING`, `COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, and every later decision-bearing lifecycle revision require both, byte-equal across successor revisions. A `PublicationDecisionRecord` repeats the exact key object from its `candidateLifecycleRef`, and its candidate, guard, and authorization fields reproduce the same key preimage.

The publication key excludes `fencingIdentity`, `fencingStateRevision`, and `guardAcquisitionCutoff`; those mutable comparison/right observations remain independently mandatory in the five-part P12 guard and cannot be inferred from or substituted by the key. Reuse is permitted only for the byte-equal governed projection and its retained authoritative decision. An unequal key kind/version, commit-intent version, durable intent projection, predecessor/generation, authorization, lifecycle, candidate, or channel is a collision and refusal; rebasing never rewrites the key.

`ProjectionCoordinate` is the concrete lossless carrier used by the common operational envelope. It is exactly:

```text
coordinateId
applicabilityKind = exact-value | not-applicable
ownerRef
basisRefs
canonicalValueDigest
canonicalValue?             # required only for exact-value
notApplicableReason?        # required only for not-applicable
```

For `exact-value`, `canonicalValue` is the coordinate-discriminated closed object below and `notApplicableReason` is prohibited. For `not-applicable`, `canonicalValue` is prohibited and the source owner, reason, and nonempty basis are mandatory. `canonicalValueDigest` is ODP-002 over `(coordinateId, applicabilityKind, canonicalValue-or-notApplicableReason, ownerRef, basisRefs)` and must reproduce exactly. The twelve-entry envelope set contains each P01–P12 exactly once. Omission, duplicate coordinate, generic map, untyped JSON value, digest-only value, or placeholder identity is invalid.

`OwnerBackedValue<T>` is the closed union `exact { value:T } | not-applicable { ownerRef, reasonCode, explanation, basisRefs }`; it is used only for a named subcoordinate whose applicability legitimately differs inside an otherwise applicable coordinate.

| `P10` | `operationId`, `operationVersion`, `query:OwnerBackedValue<QueryRef>`, `capability:OwnerBackedValue<CapabilityRef>`, `population:OwnerBackedValue<PopulationRef>`, `budgetRef`, `partialResultPolicy`, `orderingPolicy`, `approximationPolicy`, `inferencePolicy`, `continuation:OwnerBackedValue<ContinuationRef>` |
| `P11` | `dependencyManifestRef`, `transformRefs`, `compatibilityPairs`, `observedPublicationVector`, `authorizationDecisionRef`, `protectionPolicyRefs` |
| `P12` | `expectedPredecessor: existing { predecessorRef:OperationalContentBoundRef<PublicationDecisionRecord> } \| explicit-none { noneReason } \| owner-backed-not-applicable { ownerRef, reasonCode, explanation, basisRefs }`, `expectedPublicationGeneration:OwnerBackedValue<Generation>`, `fencingIdentity:OwnerBackedValue<DigestDescriptor>`, `stateRevision:OwnerBackedValue<Revision>`, `acquisitionCutoff:OwnerBackedValue<Timestamp>` |

For `PublicationDecisionRecord`, the payload's `expectedPredecessor`, `expectedPublicationGeneration`, `fencingIdentity`, `fencingStateRevision`, and `guardAcquisitionCutoff` are the authoritative comparison guard. P12 is mandatory `exact-value` and is their mechanical projection: payload `existing.expectedPredecessorRef` equals P12 `existing.predecessorRef`, payload `explicit-none.noneReason` equals P12 `explicit-none.noneReason`, and the generation, fencing-identity, state-revision, and acquisition-cutoff values are byte-equal. `owner-backed-not-applicable` is prohibited for all five projected guard components.

The payload's `observedCurrentBinding` is the exact observation compared by that guard. An `existing` observation targets the exact prior finalized `PublicationDecisionRecord(decision=published)` for the same channel; `explicit-none` is valid only when the guard basis proves no selected predecessor. A published decision requires its observed branch and predecessor-or-none value to equal `expectedPredecessor` and its observed `publicationGeneration` to equal `expectedPublicationGeneration`. A refused decision instead preserves the actual unequal or otherwise nonpass observation and its exact refusal evidence; it never coerces observed state to the expected guard. `fencingRightRef` targets the exact finalized `ExecutionClaimRecord` revision used by compare-and-publish; its `claimTokenDigest` equals `fencingIdentity`, its `claimRevision` equals `fencingStateRevision`, and it is `ACTIVE` at `guardAcquisitionCutoff`. The claim holder, work subject, authorization, and live lease-or-liveness boundary cover the exact channel, lifecycle, sealed candidate, and comparison cutoff. The outer `ProjectionCoordinate.basisRefs` is the sole guard-basis collection and includes the exact current-binding observation and fencing-right evidence; neither predecessor branch duplicates it. A published decision additionally requires that same right to remain current through the D5 linearization evidence. Every refused decision performs no binding mutation.

Payload-to-P12 guard equality and fencing-right validity are checked before `canonicalValueDigest`, `recordDigest`, comparison, or decision finalization. Expected-to-observed equality is established by comparison and is required only for `decision=published`; an observed predecessor-or-generation mismatch is a valid refused result when the exact nonpass observation and refusal evidence are preserved. A payload-to-P12 mismatch, missing outer basis, untyped predecessor, stale or unequal fencing right, second comparison input, comparison against a non-P12-projected value, or published expected-to-observed mismatch is invalid.

Every field below is therefore either an exact carried value or an expressly permitted owner-backed `notApplicable(reason)` value. Omission or a placeholder identity is invalid.

| Coordinate | Projection | Required meaning | Protected rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `P01` | Security partition | Administrative namespace, repository trust domain, principal, delegation, tenant or owner-backed not-applicable, and purpose | Stable isolation boundary; prevents cross-domain authorization aliasing |
| `P02` | Security partition | Information-control, confidentiality, access, retention, redaction, disclosure, and egress policy identities | Stable protection boundary; prevents reuse under weaker treatment |
| `P03` | Publication channel | Repository plus worktree or synthetic-subject lineage, project/variant, and logical publication class | Stable across successor snapshots; moving refs are observations, not channel identity |
| `P04` | Publication channel | Declared currentness scope, capability/population purpose, and static-versus-execution publication lane | Separates intentionally independent current bindings without using candidate state |
| `P05` | Publication channel | Topology-neutral channel namespace and stable channel-profile identity | Excludes exact contract/provider versions, physical placement, migration epoch, and generation |
| `P06` | Candidate subject | Exact static snapshot, working change set, merge basis, acquisition boundary, and immutable subject digest | Pins every static fact without fragmenting the stable channel |
| `P07` | Candidate/read vector | Candidate projection binds exact new evidence-set identity/revision, source-owned static snapshot, cutoff, and committed upstream lanes; read projection binds each committed lane decision, Manifest, channel, generation, evidence revision, static snapshot, and cutoff | Excludes the candidate lane's own future decision/generation and pins reads only through committed publications |
| `P08` | Candidate subject | Project/configuration closure plus exact `operationalProfileInstantiationId`, contract, semantic-owner, rule/profile, adapter, provider/method, toolchain, and generated-context versions | Prevents incompatible semantic or operational reuse |
| `P09` | Material basis | Migration epoch, physical-format compatibility, integrity state, exact `integrityIncidentId`, `repairExecutionId`, and prepublication `replayBasisManifestId` when applicable, transform, and storage-profile identity | Excludes the same candidate's future output-complete `replayManifestId` |
| `P10` | Operation key | Operation/version, query, capability, population, budget, partial-result, ordering, approximation, inference, and continuation projection | Prevents request/result-shape aliasing |
| `P11` | Cache key | Complete dependency manifest, transform, compatibility decision, observed publication vector, authorization decision, and protection policy | Prevents reuse that weakens subject, compatibility, currentness, or access |
| `P12` | Concurrency observation | Expected predecessor, expected publication generation, fencing identity, state revision, and acquisition cutoff | Mutable guard/read state only; excluded from every stable channel and candidate-subject key |

#### F.4.1 Seventeen-operation coordinate-applicability matrix

The existing §16.1 operation/input policy controls whether a subject is required, optional, or owner-backed not-applicable. This closed matrix controls P01–P12 operational projection. Every `OperationRequestBase` carries both `requestIdempotencyKey` and `operationKey`; the latter is the digest of exact P10. Each operation accepts only its own request-input variant, so the 17 × 16 = 272 cross-pairings are invalid independently of coordinate validity.

| Operation | Security/channel applicability | P07 publication-vector applicability | P10 operation projection | Required boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `csaa.contract.negotiate` | Security/authorization projection required; subject channel owner-backed not-applicable | owner-backed not-applicable | compatibility-request | Preserve authorization context; invent no subject, channel, snapshot, or evidence identity |
| `csaa.subject.describe` | Locator/acquisition scope; channel only after exact resolution | owner-backed not-applicable | subject-description | Unresolved or denied locator remains explicit |
| `csaa.snapshot.get` | Exact stable static channel | One committed static publication | snapshot-read | Content read cannot use a no-current health view |
| `csaa.analysis.plan` | Exact subject lineage and prospective channel | Optional exact base publication vector through `OwnerBackedValue` | plan | No publication is implied |
| `csaa.analysis.start` | Exact subject lineage and target channel | Optional exact base vector; candidate basis required | analysis-start plus required request-idempotency projection | Separate execution authority required |
| `csaa.analysis.status` | Inherited from exact live/final target | Target-observed vector or owner-backed not-applicable | live-target | State revision and public concurrency token required |
| `csaa.analysis.cancel` | Inherited from exact live target | Target-observed vector or owner-backed not-applicable | cancellation | No new subject or currentness invented |
| `csaa.query.execute` | Exact channel | Committed static plus every execution lane used | query/continuation | Implicit analysis prohibited |
| `csaa.slice.compute` | Exact channel | Committed static plus every execution lane used | slice/continuation | Implicit analysis prohibited |
| `csaa.comparison.compute` | One exact channel per labeled lane | One committed publication vector per lane | comparison | No lane is silently coalesced |
| `csaa.impact.compute` | Exact channel | Committed static plus every execution lane used | impact | Unresolved frontier remains explicit |
| `csaa.finding.get` | Exact channel | Committed publication vector owning the finding | finding | No treatment or disposition mutation |
| `csaa.finding.list` | Exact channel | Committed publication vector owning the population | page/continuation | No generation mixing |
| `csaa.raw.get` | Exact security partition; channel only when publication-bound | Exact owning publication or owner-backed not-applicable | raw-retrieval | Authorization precedes existence disclosure |
| `csaa.fixture.describe` | Exact fixture subject; channel owner-backed not-applicable | Owner-backed not-applicable unless the fixture references a committed publication | fixture | No fixture execution or oracle conferral |
| `csaa.gate.evaluate` | Exact gate/profile scope | Exact input vector only if a future effective RGP exists | gate | Current baseline refuses; no profile is invented |
| `csaa.health.get` | Exact observation scope; subject/channel may be owner-backed not-applicable | `committed-publication-vector`, `no-current-binding`, `binding-unavailable`, or `binding-corrupt` | health-observation | Non-content health view cannot expose semantic content |

The five derived identities are closed:

```text
securityPartitionId = digest(ODP-002, P01, P02)
publicationChannelId = digest(ODP-002, P03, P04, P05)
candidateSubjectKey = digest(ODP-002, P06, candidate-form(P07), P08, P09)
operationKey = digest(ODP-002, P10)
cacheKeyDigest = digest(ODP-002, P06, phase-correct(P07), P08, P09, P10, P11)
```

P12 participates in compare/fence observations but in none of these five stable or immutable projection identities. Content equality permits physical deduplication only after digest profile, purpose, policy, security partition, and identity-bearing metadata compatibility is established; logical record multiplicity and provenance remain distinct.
